title: Adjuvant human papillomavirus vaccination after excisional treatment for cervical precancer.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adjuvant 9-valent human papillomavirus vaccination improves viral clearance and reduces recurrence after excisional treatment for high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN2+). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included women aged 18 years and older who underwent loop electrosurgical excision procedure for histologically confirmed CIN2+ between December 2023 and January 2026. Women with pre-treatment human papillomavirus positivity, negative surgical margins, and available post-treatment follow-up data were included. Patients were stratified according to post-treatment vaccination status. The primary outcome was human papillomavirus clearance at 24 months. Secondary outcomes included clearance at 6 and 12 months, persistent infection, time to viral clearance, and CIN2+ recurrence. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression analyses were performed. RESULTS: A total of 666 women were included, of whom 212 (31.8%) received adjuvant vaccination and 454 (68.2%) did not. Clearance of human papillomavirus was higher in vaccinated than in unvaccinated women at 6 months (60.8% vs. 46.3%), 12 months (78.3% vs. 58.8%), and 24 months (87.7% vs. Persistent infection at 24 months was lower in the vaccinated group (12.3% vs. CIN2+ recurrence occurred in 3.8% of vaccinated women and 11.9% of unvaccinated women. Adjuvant vaccination was independently associated with faster viral clearance (adjusted hazard ratio: 2.0, 95% confidence interval: 1.5-2.7, p<0.001). CONCLUSION: Adjuvant 9-valent human papillomavirus vaccination after excisional treatment was associated with higher viral clearance and lower CIN2+ recurrence.

title: Perceptions and practices among students, parents, and teachers of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination: A pilot feasibility study from Rural Kerala.
abstract: BACKGROUND: India bears the world's highest cervical cancer burden, yet awareness and uptake of the effective HPV vaccine remain low. Although Kerala has initiated pilot HPV vaccination programmes, stakeholder knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) are not well documented. This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility of a KAP study and to identify gaps in the questionnaire, and refine study procedures (tool and process refinement) for a future large-scale analytical study. METHODS: A cross-sectional pilot study was conducted in a school in Pulinkunnu, Kerala, among students aged 11-15 years, their parents, and teachers. A structured, validated questionnaire, developed in English, translated into Malayalam, was administered during school hours. Responses were entered into secure electronic spreadsheets. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise questionnaire responses and assess the feasibility, clarity, and performance of study items. As this pilot study was designed primarily to refine study procedures and measurement tools rather than test hypotheses, no inferential or multivariable analyses were performed. RESULTS: The pilot included 75 students and 20 teachers; no parents participated despite planned recruitment, highlighting an important feasibility challenge for the proposed full-scale study. Among participants, females constituted the majority. HPV-related knowledge was low across groups, with widespread misconceptions and limited awareness of vaccine availability and cervical cancer screening. Attitudes toward vaccination were mixed, marked by safety concerns and modest willingness to receive or recommend the vaccine. Practices reflected low prior awareness and uptake, with few respondents having heard of or received the HPV vaccine. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot revealed major gaps in HPV-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among participating students and teachers, while also identifying important methodological challenges, particularly parental recruitment and questionnaire refinement. The findings support modifications to recruitment strategies, study procedures, and measurement tools before implementation of a larger analytical study.

title_zh: 学生、家长和教师对 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 的看法和实践:来自喀拉拉邦农村地区的试点可行性研究。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: India bears the world's highest cervical cancer burden, yet awareness and uptake of the effective HPV vaccine remain low. Although Kerala has initiated pilot HPV vaccination programmes, stakeholder knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) are not well documented. This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility of a KAP study and to identify gaps in the questionnaire, and refine study procedures (tool and process refinement) for a future large-scale analytical study. METHODS: A cross-sectional pilot study was conducted in a school in Pulinkunnu, Kerala, among students aged 11-15 years, their parents, and teachers. A structured, validated questionnaire, developed in English, translated into Malayalam, was administered during school hours. Responses were entered into secure electronic spreadsheets. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise questionnaire responses and assess the feasibility, clarity, and performance of study items. As this pilot study was designed primarily to refine study procedures and measurement tools rather than test hypotheses, no inferential or multivariable analyses were performed. RESULTS: The pilot included 75 students and 20 teachers; no parents participated despite planned recruitment, highlighting an important feasibility challenge for the proposed full-scale study. Among participants, females constituted the majority. HPV-related knowledge was low across groups, with widespread misconceptions and limited awareness of vaccine availability and cervical cancer screening. Attitudes toward vaccination were mixed, marked by safety concerns and modest willingness to receive or recommend the vaccine. Practices reflected low prior awareness and uptake, with few respondents having heard of or received the HPV vaccine. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot revealed major gaps in HPV-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among participating students and teachers, while also identifying important methodological challenges, particularly parental recruitment and questionnaire refinement. The findings support modifications to recruitment strategies, study procedures, and measurement tools before implementation of a larger analytical study.

title: Clinical application of modified Yihuang Decoction for the treatment of cervical high-risk HPV persistent infection
abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) infection is a major cause of cervical cancer. While vaccines exist, treatment options for those already infected are limited. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and immune response of combining human interferon α2b (hIFN) with modified Yihuang Decoction (YHD) for HR-HPV infection. METHODS: This trial was conducted with 108 patients diagnosed with persistent HR-HPV infection. Participants received either hIFN monotherapy or a combination of hIFN and YHD (hIFN-YHD) for 3 months, followed by a 6-month follow-up. The primary outcomes included clinical efficacy, HR-HPV clearance rates, and changes in immune markers, such as IFN-γ, IL-4, and FPR3, in cervical biopsy tissues and vaginal lavage fluid. RESULTS: Treatment with hIFN-YHD resulted in significantly higher recovery (46.8%) and overall response rates (85.1%) compared with hIFN monotherapy (28.9% and 60.0%, respectively; p < 0.05). The negative conversion rate for HR-HPV was also significantly higher in the hIFN-YHD group, especially in patients with single and multiple infections (p < 0.001). Immunological analysis revealed increased FPR3 and IFN-γ expression and reduced IL-4 levels in the hIFN-YHD group. Additionally, hIFN-YHD treatment significantly increased IFN-γ levels and decreased IL-4 levels in vaginal lavage fluid (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The combination of hIFN and YHD significantly improves clinical outcomes and enhances immune responses in patients with persistent HR-HPV infection.

title: From human papillomavirus (HPV) infection to HPV-associated cancers in systemic lupus erythematosus: A systematic review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The current cervix-focused screening paradigm in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) may underestimate extra-cervical anogenital cancer risk. This meta-analysis aimed to quantify the risk of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and HPV-associated cancers in SLE patients. METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed (2010), Embase (2010), and Cochrane Library (2010) to August 8, 2025. Odds Ratios (ORs) and Standardized Incidence Ratios (SIRs) with 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) were calculated. The study protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251122192). RESULTS: SLE was associated with significantly increased odds of HPV infection (OR = 4.12, 95% CI 2.03, 8.32). We further assessed the risk of HPV-associated malignancies in SLE patients. SLE patients exhibited substantially elevated risks across multiple HPV-associated cancers (SIR = 1.90, 95% CI 1.51, 2.38). The risk of cervical cancer was more than doubled (SIR = 2.25, 95% CI 1.75, 2.89). Notably, even higher risks were observed for extra-cervical anogenital cancers, namely vulvar/vaginal cancers (SIR = 5.60, 95% CI 3.71, 8.43). CONCLUSIONS: SLE is associated with elevated risks of HPV infection and a broad spectrum of HPV-associated cancers. Subgroup analyses suggested that cyclophosphamide use, multiple sexual partners, and Asian populations may constitute higher-risk subgroups. These findings highlight the need for additional prospective evidence to better characterize HPV-associated cancer risks in SLE patients.

title: Health Economic Evaluation of Human Papillomavirus Vaccination for Age- Eligible Females in Guangxi: An Analysis Based on the PRIME Model
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer ranks among the most common malignancies affecting women in China, and the disease burden in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region is especially pronounced. Although human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination offers the most effective form of prevention, coverage among age-eligible girls in Guangxi has remained extremely low. In 2025, domestic HPV vaccine prices dropped substantially and Guangxi launched a free vaccination program, necessitating an updated health economic evaluation under current pricing and policy parameters. Methods Using the WHO-recommended PRIME (Papillomavirus Rapid Interface for Modelling and Economics) v2.3 model, we evaluated the cost-effectiveness of HPV vaccination for 13-year-old girls in Guangxi from both healthcare system and societal perspectives. Epidemiological parameters were anchored to 2021, sourced from Guangxi death registration and cancer registry systems, while vaccine prices reflected the latest 2025 government procurement rates. The primary outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) per disability-adjusted life year (DALY) averted, with per capita GDP as the willingness-to-pay threshold. Eight vaccine types, 16 age×coverage combinations, and one-way sensitivity analyses were conducted. Results Under the base-case scenario (domestic bivalent HPV vaccine at 27.5 RMB/dose, age 13, 70% coverage), the discounted ICER was − 15,033 RMB/DALY (-0.30× per capita GDP) from the healthcare system perspective, indicating a cost-saving strategy. The benefit-cost ratio was 4.99, meaning each RMB spent on vaccination averts nearly 5 RMB in cervical cancer treatment costs. The domestic 9-valent vaccine (531 RMB/dose) was highly cost-effective (ICER = 25,316 RMB/DALY, 0.50× per capita GDP), and the imported 9-valent vaccine under the 2-dose promotional program (equivalent to 675 RMB/dose) was also well below the cost-effectiveness threshold (ICER = 35,050 RMB/DALY, 0.70× per capita GDP). The societal perspective ICER for the domestic bivalent vaccine was − 14,014 RMB/DALY (-0.28× per capita GDP), remaining economically dominant. One-way sensitivity analyses confirmed that the domestic bivalent vaccination remained cost-saving across all parameter variations. Conclusions Under the 2025 procurement pricing, vaccinating age-eligible girls in Guangxi with the domestic bivalent HPV vaccine is a cost-saving strategy, with every 1 RMB invested averting approximately 5 RMB in direct cervical cancer medical costs. The domestic 9-valent HPV vaccine is also highly cost-effective. Results support accelerating the free HPV vaccination program for age-eligible girls in Guangxi, prioritizing the domestic bivalent vaccine for broad coverage; regions with sufficient fiscal capacity and a pursuit of broader HPV type protection may consider the domestic 9-valent vaccine.

abstract_original: Abstract Background Cervical cancer ranks among the most common malignancies affecting women in China, and the disease burden in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region is especially pronounced. Although human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination offers the most effective form of prevention, coverage among age-eligible girls in Guangxi has remained extremely low. In 2025, domestic HPV vaccine prices dropped substantially and Guangxi launched a free vaccination program, necessitating an updated health economic evaluation under current pricing and policy parameters. Methods Using the WHO-recommended PRIME (Papillomavirus Rapid Interface for Modelling and Economics) v2.3 model, we evaluated the cost-effectiveness of HPV vaccination for 13-year-old girls in Guangxi from both healthcare system and societal perspectives. The primary outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) per disability-adjusted life year (DALY) averted, with per capita GDP as the willingness-to-pay threshold. Eight vaccine types, 16 age×coverage combinations, and one-way sensitivity analyses were conducted. title: Live-Attenuated HSV-1 VC2 Vectoring Capsid-Displayed HPV-16 E7m Elicits Th1-Polarized CD8+ T Cell Responses and Protection Against Cervical Cancer Challenge
abstract: Cervical cancer is a major cause of mortality worldwide and has been attributed to long-lasting (persistent) infections with the human papillomavirus (HPV). Although more than 50 types of HPVs are known the infect the genital tract, fewer than a dozen of them are regularly linked to cervical cancers leading to these types being designated as “high risk” HPVs. Worldwide, over 90% of cervical cancers arise from persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and the infectious nature of the virus procures the need for preventative vaccines against cervical cancer. To address this, we have developed a live-attenuated herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) VC2-vectored vaccine expressing a catalytically inactive mutant of HPV-16 E7 (E7m) fused to the viral capsid protein VP26. Incorporation of E7m into the VC2 backbone resulted in stable incorporation of VP26-E7m fusion protein in cell free viral particles and detectable intracellular expression within infected cells. The recombinant virus (E7m VC-2) maintained growth kinetics comparable to parental VC2 in vitro, though plaque size was modestly reduced, suggesting a minimal fitness cost associated with transgene insertion. To evaluate prophylactic efficacy, mice received a one-dose vaccine schedule of E7m VC-2 prior to challenge with syngeneic HPV-16 E6/E7-expressing tumor cells. In mice that did develop tumors, growth kinetics were attenuated relative to unvaccinated animals. Importantly, neither E7m VC-2 nor adjuvanted E7m protein alone achieved statistically significant protection versus untreated controls. Immunohistochemical analysis of tumor tissue revealed markedly increased CD8+ T cell infiltration in E7m VC-2 vaccinated mice, demonstrating that vaccination promotes a cytotoxic immune microenvironment capable of restricting tumor progression. Three-dose vaccination of mice with E7m VC-2 induced a robust Th1-polarized immune response characterized by strong interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) secretion in response to HPV16 E7 expressing syngeneic cell lines, consistent with the induction of cell-mediated antitumor immunity and superior to responses elicited by adjuvanted E7m protein alone. With an extended three-dose vaccination schedule E7m VC-2 conferred significantly greater protection against tumor establishment relative to untreated controls (80% vs. Collectively, these findings establish proof-of-concept for the HSV-1 VC2 platform as an effective vector for HPV-targeted cancer immunotherapy, delivering statistically significant prophylactic protection alongside potent induction of tumor-reactive CD8+ T cells. Future studies will incorporate both E6 and E7 antigens to broaden antigenic coverage, evaluate therapeutic efficacy in established tumor models, and optimize dosing regimens with the long-term goal of advancing this Louisiana-developed platform toward IND-enabling studies and clinical translation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, primarily driven by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPVs), necessitating the development of effective preventative and therapeutic interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated a live-attenuated herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) VC2 vector expressing a mutant HPV-16 E7 antigen in mice, using a one-dose or three-dose prophylactic vaccination schedule prior to challenge with HPV-16 E6/E7-expressing tumor cells.
analysis.methods: The recombinant virus (E7m VC-2) was engineered to incorporate a VP26-E7m fusion protein, with stable expression confirmed in viral particles and infected cells, and its growth kinetics were compared to the parental VC2 strain in vitro.
analysis.main_results: A three-dose E7m VC-2 vaccination regimen induced a Th1-polarized immune response with strong IFN-γ secretion and significantly reduced tumor establishment (80% protection) compared to untreated controls, while neither E7m VC-2 nor adjuvanted E7m protein alone achieved statistically significant protection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish proof-of-concept for the HSV-1 VC2 platform as an effective vector for HPV-targeted cancer immunotherapy, demonstrating potent induction of tumor-reactive CD8+ T cells and prophylactic protection against HPV-16-associated tumor challenge.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study supports the potential of the HSV-1 VC2 vector platform for advancing HPV-targeted immunotherapies, particularly for cervical cancer prevention, and lays groundwork for further development toward clinical translation.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a live-attenuated HSV-1 VC2 vector expressing a mutant HPV-16 E7 antigen (E7m VC-2) to evaluate prophylactic efficacy against HPV-16-associated tumor challenge in mice. The recombinant virus maintained stable transgene expression and comparable growth kinetics to the parental strain, with minimal fitness cost. title_zh: 减毒活 HSV-1 VC2 载体衣壳展示的 HPV-16 E7m 引发 Th1 极化 CD8+ T 细胞反应并针对 宫颈癌 挑战提供保护
source_body_en: Cervical cancer is a major cause of mortality worldwide and has been attributed to long-lasting (persistent) infections with the human papillomavirus (HPV). Although more than 50 types of HPVs are known the infect the genital tract, fewer than a dozen of them are regularly linked to cervical cancers leading to these types being designated as “high risk” HPVs. Worldwide, over 90% of cervical cancers arise from persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and the infectious nature of the virus procures the need for preventative vaccines against cervical cancer. To address this, we have developed a live-attenuated herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) VC2-vectored vaccine expressing a catalytically inactive mutant of HPV-16 E7 (E7m) fused to the viral capsid protein VP26. Incorporation of E7m into the VC2 backbone resulted in stable incorporation of VP26-E7m fusion protein in cell free viral particles and detectable intracellular expression within infected cells. The recombinant virus (E7m VC-2) maintained growth kinetics comparable to parental VC2 in vitro, though plaque size was modestly reduced, suggesting a minimal fitness cost associated with transgene insertion. To evaluate prophylactic efficacy, mice received a one-dose vaccine schedule of E7m VC-2 prior to challenge with syngeneic HPV-16 E6/E7-expressing tumor cells. In mice that did develop tumors, growth kinetics were attenuated relative to unvaccinated animals. Importantly, neither E7m VC-2 nor adjuvanted E7m protein alone achieved statistically significant protection versus untreated controls. Immunohistochemical analysis of tumor tissue revealed markedly increased CD8+ T cell infiltration in E7m VC-2 vaccinated mice, demonstrating that vaccination promotes a cytotoxic immune microenvironment capable of restricting tumor progression. Three-dose vaccination of mice with E7m VC-2 induced a robust Th1-polarized immune response characterized by strong interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) secretion in response to HPV16 E7 expressing syngeneic cell lines, consistent with the induction of cell-mediated antitumor immunity and superior to responses elicited by adjuvanted E7m protein alone. With an extended three-dose vaccination schedule E7m VC-2 conferred significantly greater protection against tumor establishment relative to untreated controls (80% vs. Collectively, these findings establish proof-of-concept for the HSV-1 VC2 platform as an effective vector for HPV-targeted cancer immunotherapy, delivering statistically significant prophylactic protection alongside potent induction of tumor-reactive CD8+ T cells. Future studies will incorporate both E6 and E7 antigens to broaden antigenic coverage, evaluate therapeutic efficacy in established tumor models, and optimize dosing regimens with the long-term goal of advancing this Louisiana-developed platform toward IND-enabling studies and clinical translation.
abstract_zh: 宫颈癌 是全球 死亡率 的主要原因,归因于 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 的长期(持续)感染。尽管已知有超过 50 种 HPV 会感染生殖道,但其中只有不到十几种经常与 宫颈癌 相关,导致这些类型被指定为“高风险”HPV。在世界范围内,超过 90% 的 宫颈癌 是由持续的高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染引起的,该病毒的传染性导致需要针对 宫颈癌 进行预防性 疫苗。为了解决这个问题,我们开发了一种减毒活的单纯疱疹病毒 1 型 (HSV-1) VC2 载体 疫苗,表达与病毒衣壳蛋白 VP26 融合的 HPV-16 E7 (E7m) 催化失活突变体。将 E7m 掺入 VC2 主链中,导致 VP26-E7m 融合蛋白稳定掺入无细胞病毒颗粒中,并在感染细胞内检测到细胞内表达。重组病毒 (E7m VC-2) 在体外保持了与亲本 VC2 相当的生长动力学,尽管噬斑大小略有减小,这表明与转基因插入相关的适应性成本最小。为了评估预防效果,小鼠在用表达同基因 HPV-16 E6/E7 的肿瘤细胞攻击之前接受一剂 疫苗 方案的 E7m VC-2。在确实产生肿瘤的小鼠中,相对于未接种疫苗的动物,生长动力学减弱。重要的是,与未治疗的对照组相比,单独使用 E7m VC-2 或佐剂 E7m 蛋白均未达到统计学上显着的保护作用。肿瘤组织的免疫组织化学分析显示,E7m VC-2 疫苗接种小鼠中 CD8+ T 细胞浸润显着增加,表明 疫苗接种 促进能够限制肿瘤进展的细胞毒性免疫微环境。具有 E7m VC-2 的小鼠的三剂量 疫苗接种 诱导了强大的 Th1 极化 免疫应答,其特征是响应表达 HPV16 E7 的同系细胞系而强烈分泌干扰素-γ (IFN-γ),这与细胞介导的抗肿瘤免疫的诱导一致,并且优于单独使用佐剂 E7m 蛋白引起的反应。与未经治疗的对照组相比,延长三剂量的 疫苗接种 方案 E7m VC-2 显着增强了对肿瘤形成的保护(80% vs. 总体而言),这些发现为 HSV-1 VC2 平台作为 HPV 靶向癌症免疫治疗的有效 媒介 提供了概念验证,在有效诱导肿瘤反应性 CD8+ T 细胞的同时,提供了统计学上显着的预防性保护。未来的研究将结合 E6 和 E7 抗原,以扩大抗原覆盖范围,评估已建立肿瘤模型的治疗效果,并优化给药方案,长期目标是将路易斯安那州开发的平台推向 IND 研究和临床转化。

title: Incidence and Prevalence of Human Papillomavirus Infection to Predict Outcomes from HPV-Based Cervical Cancer Screening in Women and People with a Cervix Living with HIV.
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) testing has been implemented in many organized cervix screening programs; however, understanding how this screening methodology affects rates of colposcopy and further follow-up procedures remains underexplored, especially among women with HIV. In the absence of HPV screening program data in British Columbia (BC), Canada, we sought to determine HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopies among a cohort of women with HIV using the BC Cervix Screening algorithm. Setting: HPV data were collected and analyzed from a prospective HPV vaccine immunogenicity cohort study of women with HIV from 14 sites of HIV care across Canada from 2008 to 2015. Methods: HPV data were obtained during the screening (month −3), baseline (month 0), month 12, and month 24 time points (Linear Array assay). Participant demographic and clinical characteristics (CD4 + count, HIV viral load, etc.) were assessed to determine associations between HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopy using rate ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Results: Overall, 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening which would result in a colposcopy referral. In total, 15.9% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, month 12, and month 24 time points, which would result in 3 consecutive referrals to colposcopy. Participants with repeat oncogenic HPV detected were less likely to have a suppressed HIV viral load compared with participants without oncogenic HPV detected. Conclusions: Results of this study suggest that HPV testing will result in a high proportion of referrals to colposcopy and follow-up procedures among women with HIV, which will require preparation and planning. Further work is needed to provide the appropriate support and education for women with HIV when incorporating HPV testing into cervix screening programs.
journal: JAIDS Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer screening programs increasingly use HPV testing, but its downstream impact on colposcopy referrals in women with HIV remains poorly understood. The study aimed to address this gap by estimating HPV prevalence and colposcopy referral rates in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective cohort study analyzed HPV data from a Canadian HPV vaccine immunogenicity cohort of women with HIV recruited from 14 HIV care sites between 2008 and 2015.
analysis.methods: HPV status was assessed at screening (month −3), baseline (month 0), month 12, and month 24 using the Linear Array assay. Participant characteristics, including CD4+ count and HIV viral load, were collected to evaluate associations with HPV prevalence and colposcopy referral.
analysis.main_results: Overall, 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, which would result in a colposcopy referral. Among these, 15.9% had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, month 12, and month 24, indicating three consecutive referrals. Participants with repeat oncogenic HPV detection were less likely to have a suppressed HIV viral load than those without.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as indicating that HPV testing in women with HIV will lead to a high burden of colposcopy referrals, necessitating system-level preparation. They highlight the need for targeted support and education for this population when integrating HPV testing into screening programs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that HPV-based screening in women with HIV may substantially increase colposcopy demand, requiring resource allocation and programmatic adjustments. They also underscore the importance of addressing virologic control in this population to mitigate referral risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and lack of a comparator group, which constrains causal inference. The evidence strength is moderate due to potential unmeasured confounding and generalizability restricted to women with HIV in Canada.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated HPV prevalence and colposcopy referral rates among women with HIV in Canada using a prospective cohort design. It found that nearly half of participants had oncogenic HPV at baseline, with nearly 16% showing persistent detection across three time points, leading to repeated colposcopy referrals. Repeat oncogenic HPV detection was associated with unsuppressed HIV viral load. The authors conclude that HPV-based screening will significantly increase colposcopy demand in this population, necessitating system preparation and targeted support. The evidence is moderate in strength due to observational design limitations and potential confounding.

title: Family Physicians’ Knowledge Levels and Awareness Regarding HPV Infection and HPV Vaccines
abstract: Background: In primary care settings, cervical cancer screening and prevention are highly dependent on healthcare provider initiatives, particularly in countries like Türkiye where the HPV vaccine is not yet integrated into the national routine immunization schedule. Since HPV vaccines provide over 90% protection against cervical cancer, the proactive guidance of primary care providers is critical. This study evaluated family physicians’ knowledge levels and awareness of HPV infection and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines in primary care settings in Türkiye. Methods: A total of 238 family physicians working in Türkiye participated in this descriptive cross-sectional study using a convenience sampling method. Data were collected through an online questionnaire administered via Google Forms. The survey included a sociodemographic information form and a 33-item HPV knowledge scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, normality assessment, chi-square test, Mann–Whitney U test, Kruskal–Wallis test, and hierarchical logistic regression analysis. Results: Overall, 81.1% of participants recommended the HPV vaccine, and 83.6% believed it should be included in the national schedule. Notably, only 15.1% of the participating physicians had received the HPV vaccine themselves, whereas 40.6% of the unvaccinated subgroup (82/202) stated they were considering personal vaccination. HPV knowledge levels were generally high, but lower when regarding the current national program. Vaccine recommenders and female participants had significantly higher knowledge scores, while out-of-pocket vaccine cost emerged as a major barrier to clinical recommendation. abstract_zh: 背景:在初级保健机构中,宫颈癌 筛查和预防高度依赖于医疗保健提供者的举措,特别是在土耳其等国家,HPV 疫苗 尚未纳入国家常规免疫计划。由于 HPV 疫苗 对 宫颈癌 提供超过 90% 的保护,因此初级保健提供者的主动指导至关重要。本研究评估了土耳其初级保健机构中家庭医生对 HPV 感染和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 的知识水平和认识。方法:共有 238 名在土耳其工作的家庭医生使用便利抽样方法参与了这项描述性横断面研究。数据是通过 Google Forms 管理的在线调查问卷收集的。该调查包括社会人口统计信息表和 33 项 HPV 知识量表。使用描述性统计、正态性评估、卡方检验、Mann-Whitney U 检验、Kruskal-Wallis 检验和层次逻辑回归分析对数据进行分析。结果:总体而言,81.1% 的参与者推荐 HPV 疫苗,83.6% 的参与者认为应将其纳入国家计划。值得注意的是,只有 15.1% 的参与医生自己接种了 HPV 疫苗,而 40.6% 的未接种疫苗亚组 (82/202) 表示他们正在考虑个人 疫苗接种。HPV 知识水平普遍较高,但当前国家计划的知识水平较低。疫苗 推荐者和女性参与者的知识得分显着较高,而自付费用 疫苗 成为临床推荐的主要障碍。在多变量层次逻辑回归中,控制人口统计数据后,单个知识领域并没有作为独立的预测因子出现,只有当前国家计划的知识显示出边缘趋势(p = 0.066),尽管将知识变量作为一个集体块包含在内显着提高了整体模型的解释力(p = 0.003)。结论:土耳其的家庭医生普遍表现出较高的 HPV 相关知识和较高的 HPV 疫苗 推荐率。这项研究阐明,初级保健倡导是由专业知识和压倒性结构因素的综合影响形成的,而不是作为独立预测因素的单个知识领域。虽然未来的战略必须侧重于发展有针对性的继续医学教育,以弥合特定的知识差距并优化机会咨询,但实现最佳免疫覆盖率最终取决于将 疫苗 纳入国家计划,以减轻自付费用障碍。

title: [Prevalence of cervical human papillomavirus infection among women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China].
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and epidemiological characteristics of cervical human papilloma virus (HPV) infection among ethnic minority and Han Chinese women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture of Yunnan Province to provide a theoretical basis for the strategy of cervical cancer prevention and treatment in this region. Methods: A consecutive cohort of 12,605 female residents who underwent cervical HPV genotyping across four medical centers in the Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture between January 2018 and June 2024 was enrolled. The overall HPV prevalence and genotype distribution was analyzed and the disparities in infection patterns among different ethnic groups were compared. Results: The overall HPV prevalence among women in this region was 17.88% (2,254/12,605). Infections solely with high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) predominated, with a prevalence of 14.75%, accounting for 82.48% (1,859/2,254) of all HPV-positive cases. The three most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV-52 (4.53%), HPV-16 (2.41%), and HPV-58 (2.01%). HPV infections exhibited a striking age-specific clustering among younger demographics; the prevalence in both the <20 and 20-29 years age groups reached 100%. The prevalence declined significantly with advancing age, dropping to 5.20% in the ≥60 years age group. Single-genotype infections constituted the primary pattern (74.00%, 1,668/2,254). However, multiple infections-particularly mixed infections of HR-HPV and low-risk HPV (LR-HPV)-were exceptionally prominent in the <20 years age group, peaking at 24.14%. Demographically, the overall HPV prevalence among ethnic minority women was significantly higher than that of Han women (23.14% vs. 15.62%, P<0.001), with the highest rates observed in the Dai (27.10%), Hani (26.30%), and Miao (25.17%) ethnicities. Although the general infection patterns (single vs. multiple) were similar between ethnicminority and Han women, ethnicminority women bore a significantly higher burden of specific HR-HPV types compared with Han women, including HPV-16 (3.56% vs. 1.92%), HPV-58 (3.03% vs. 1.58%), HPV-51 (2.45% vs. 1.24%), and HPV-59 (0.92% vs. 0.30%) (all P<0.05). Furthermore, inter-ethnic variations in genotype distribution were observed among the minority groups; notably, the distribution of HR-HPV-56 showed the most significant difference (P=0.018), with the highest prevalence found in women from the Dai ethnicity (3.74%). Conclusions: Cervical HPV infections among women in this region are predominantly driven by HR-HPV types 52, 16, and 58, exhibiting significant age and ethnic heterogeneity. Young women aged <30 years are highly susceptible not only to overall HPV infection, but also to mixed exposure involving multiple genotypes. Compared to Han women, ethnic minority women face a substantially more severe burden of HR-HPV infections. These findings suggest that future cervical cancer prevention and control strategies in this region should shift interventions to earlier stages, prioritizing early screening and health education for young women. Simultaneously, it is imperative to account for ethnic disparities, promote multivalent HPV vaccines that cover the predominant endemic strains, and develop targeted, precision-based prevention strategies tailored to specific ethnic regions.

This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and epidemiological characteristics of cervical HPV infection among ethnic minority and Han Chinese women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture to inform local cervical cancer prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A consecutive cohort of 12,605 female residents who underwent cervical HPV genotyping across four medical centers in the Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture between January 2018 and June 2024 was enrolled. The study compared infection patterns among different ethnic groups and analyzed genotype distribution.
analysis.methods: The overall HPV prevalence and genotype distribution were analyzed using cervical HPV genotyping data. The study compared disparities in infection patterns among ethnic minority and Han Chinese women, focusing on high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) and low-risk HPV (LR-HPV) genotypes.
analysis.main_results: The overall HPV prevalence was 17.88% (2,254/12,605), with HR-HPV infections predominating at 14.75% (1,859/2,254), accounting for 82.48% of all HPV-positive cases. The three most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV-52 (4.53%), HPV-16 (2.41%), and HPV-58 (2.01%). HPV infections showed strong age clustering, with prevalence reaching 100% in women aged <20 and 20–29 years, declining to 5.20% in those ≥60 years.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that cervical HPV infections in this region are predominantly driven by HR-HPV types 52, 16, and 58, with significant age and ethnic heterogeneity. Novelty lies in the identification of ethnic disparities and the high burden of mixed infections in younger women, highlighting the need for targeted prevention strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support prioritizing early screening and health education for young women, particularly in ethnic minority populations who face a substantially higher burden of HR-HPV infections. The data also underscore the importance of multivalent HPV vaccines covering prevalent endemic strains and precision-based prevention strategies tailored to specific ethnic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and reliance on genotyping data from clinical centers may limit generalizability and introduce selection bias. While the large sample size (n=12,605) strengthens precision, the absence of longitudinal follow-up and standardized sampling across centers reduces causal inference and may underestimate regional heterogeneity. The evidence is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and epidemiological characteristics of cervical HPV infection among ethnic minority and Han Chinese women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture to inform local cervical cancer prevention strategies.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A consecutive cohort of 12,605 female residents who underwent cervical HPV genotyping across four medical centers in the Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture between January 2018 and June 2024 was enrolled. The study compared infection patterns among different ethnic groups and analyzed genotype distribution.
analysis_en.methods: The overall HPV prevalence and genotype distribution were analyzed using cervical HPV genotyping data. The study compared disparities in infection patterns among ethnic minority and Han Chinese women, focusing on high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) and low-risk HPV (LR-HPV) genotypes.
analysis_en.main_results: The overall HPV prevalence was 17.88% (2,254/12,605), with HR-HPV infections predominating at 14.75% (1,859/2,254), accounting for 82.48% of all HPV-positive cases. The three most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV-52 (4.53%), HPV-16 (2.41%), and HPV-58 (2.01%). HPV infections showed strong age clustering, with prevalence reaching 100% in women aged <20 and 20–29 years, declining to 5.20% in those ≥60 years.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that cervical HPV infections in this region are predominantly driven by HR-HPV types 52, 16, and 58, with significant age and ethnic heterogeneity. Novelty lies in the identification of ethnic disparities and the high burden of mixed infections in younger women, highlighting the need for targeted prevention strategies.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support prioritizing early screening and health education for young women, particularly in ethnic minority populations who face a substantially higher burden of HR-HPV infections. The data also underscore the importance of multivalent HPV vaccines covering prevalent endemic strains and precision-based prevention strategies tailored to specific ethnic regions.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and reliance on genotyping data from clinical centers may limit generalizability and introduce selection bias. The evidence is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

title_zh: 云南省红河哈尼族彝族自治州妇女宫颈患病率感染情况分析
source_body_en: Objective: This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and epidemiological characteristics of cervical human papilloma virus (HPV) infection among ethnic minority and Han Chinese women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture of Yunnan Province to provide a theoretical basis for the strategy of cervical cancer prevention and treatment in this region. Methods: A consecutive cohort of 12,605 female residents who underwent cervical HPV genotyping across four medical centers in the Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture between January 2018 and June 2024 was enrolled. The overall HPV prevalence and genotype distribution was analyzed and the disparities in infection patterns among different ethnic groups were compared. Results: The overall HPV prevalence among women in this region was 17.88% (2,254/12,605). Infections solely with high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) predominated, with a prevalence of 14.75%, accounting for 82.48% (1,859/2,254) of all HPV-positive cases. The three most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV-52 (4.53%), HPV-16 (2.41%), and HPV-58 (2.01%). HPV infections exhibited a striking age-specific clustering among younger demographics; the prevalence in both the <20 and 20-29 years age groups reached 100%. The prevalence declined significantly with advancing age, dropping to 5.20% in the ≥60 years age group. Single-genotype infections constituted the primary pattern (74.00%, 1,668/2,254). However, multiple infections-particularly mixed infections of HR-HPV and low-risk HPV (LR-HPV)-were exceptionally prominent in the <20 years age group, peaking at 24.14%. Demographically, the overall HPV prevalence among ethnic minority women was significantly higher than that of Han women (23.14% vs. 15.62%, P<0.001), with the highest rates observed in the Dai (27.10%), Hani (26.30%), and Miao (25.17%) ethnicities. Although the general infection patterns (single vs. multiple) were similar between ethnicminority and Han women, ethnicminority women bore a significantly higher burden of specific HR-HPV types compared with Han women, including HPV-16 (3.56% vs. 1.92%), HPV-58 (3.03% vs. 1.58%), HPV-51 (2.45% vs. 1.24%), and HPV-59 (0.92% vs. 0.30%) (all P<0.05). Furthermore, inter-ethnic variations in genotype distribution were observed among the minority groups; notably, the distribution of HR-HPV-56 showed the most significant difference (P=0.018), with the highest prevalence found in women from the Dai ethnicity (3.74%). Conclusions: Cervical HPV infections among women in this region are predominantly driven by HR-HPV types 52, 16, and 58, exhibiting significant age and ethnic heterogeneity. Young women aged <30 years are highly susceptible not only to overall HPV infection, but also to mixed exposure involving multiple genotypes. Compared to Han women, ethnic minority women face a substantially more severe burden of HR-HPV infections. These findings suggest that future cervical cancer prevention and control strategies in this region should shift interventions to earlier stages, prioritizing early screening and health education for young women. Simultaneously, it is imperative to account for ethnic disparities, promote multivalent HPV vaccines that cover the predominant endemic strains, and develop targeted, precision-based prevention strategies tailored to specific ethnic regions.
abstract_zh: 【摘要】:目的:调查云南省红河哈尼族彝族自治州少数民族和汉族妇女宫颈人乳头状瘤病毒(HPV)感染情况及流行病学特征,为该地区制定宫颈癌预防策略和治疗提供理论依据。方法:连续纳入 2018 年 1 月至 2024 年 6 月期间在红河哈尼族彝族自治州四个医疗​​中心接受宫颈 HPV 基因分型的 12,605 名女性居民。分析HPV 患病率总体和基因型分布,并比较不同种族之间感染模式的差异。结果:该地区女性HPV 患病率总体感染率为17.88%(2,254/12,605)。仅感染 高危型HPV (HR-HPV) 为主,患病率 为 14.75%,占所有 HPV 阳性病例的 82.48% (1,859/2,254)。三种最常见的 HR-HPV 基因型是 HPV-52 (4.53%)、HPV-16 (2.41%) 和 HPV-58 (2.01%)。HPV 感染在年轻人群中表现出显着的年龄特异性聚集;<20岁和20-29岁年龄组的患病率均达到100%。患病率随着年龄的增长而显着下降,在≥60岁组中降至5.20%。单基因型感染构成主要模式(74.00%,1,668/2,254)。然而,多重感染,特别是HR-HPV和低危型HPV(LR-HPV)的混合感染,在<20岁年龄组中尤为突出,最高达到24.14%。从人口特征来看,少数民族女性HPV 患病率总体显着高于汉族女性(23.14% vs. 15.62%,P<0.001),其中傣族(27.10%)、哈尼族(26.30%)和苗族(25.17%)感染率最高。尽管少数民族和汉族女性的一般感染模式(单发与多发)相似,但与汉族女性相比,少数民族女性特定HR-HPV类型的负担明显更高,包括HPV-16(3.56% vs. 1.92%)、HPV-58(3.03% vs. 1.58%)、HPV-51(2.45% vs. 1.24%)和HPV-59 (0.92% vs. 0.30%)(均 P<0.05)。此外,在少数群体中观察到基因型分布的种族间差异;值得注意的是,HR-HPV-56的分布差异最为显着(P=0.018),其中患病率在傣族女性中最高(3.74%)。结论:该地区女性宫颈 HPV 感染主要由 HR-HPV 52、16 和 58 型驱动,表现出显着的年龄和种族异质性。年龄<30岁的年轻女性不仅对整体HPV感染高度敏感,而且对涉及多种基因型的混合暴露也高度敏感。与汉族女性相比,少数民族女性面临着更严重的HR-HPV感染负担。这些结果表明,该地区未来的宫颈癌防控策略应将干预措施转向早期阶段,优先考虑对年轻女性的早期筛查和健康教育。同时,要考虑民族差异,推广涵盖优势流行毒株的多价HPV 疫苗,并针对特定民族地区制定有针对性、精准化的预防策略。

title: High diagnostic concordance between vulvar and cervical samples for human papillomavirus detection: a cross-sectional study
abstract: ABSTRACT Low compliance with clinician-collected cervical sampling and implementation barriers in resource-limited settings limit human papillomavirus (HPV)-based cervical cancer prevention. Vulvar sampling is non-invasive and easier to perform, but its agreement with cervical HPV testing remains insufficiently defined. We retrospectively analyzed 719 paired vulvar and cervical specimens tested by clinically validated fluorescence PCR to evaluate concordance between sampling sites and the potential utility of vulvar HPV testing. High-risk HPV (hrHPV) positivity was 47.98% (345/719) in vulvar samples and 43.53% (313/719) in cervical samples, with strong site-to-site concordance (κ = 0.821). The negative predictive value of vulvar hrHPV testing for concurrent cervical hrHPV positivity was 95.72%. Concordance was highest for HPV18 (κ = 0.892; negative predictive value [NPV] = 99.41%), followed by HPV16 (κ = 0.839), and low-risk HPV6/11 (κ = 0.746). Among five biopsy-confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia cases, vulvar and cervical HPV results were fully concordant. Age-stratified analysis showed peak hrHPV infection in women younger than 30 years. In women aged 40–49 years, vulvar hrHPV positivity exceeded cervical positivity (56.52% vs 45.65%). Agreement was lower among women aged ≥40 years for hrHPV and lrHPV testing. Among discordant cases, 93.75% (15/16) of vulvar-negative/cervical-positive cases had prior HPV-related treatment, whereas non-HPV16/18 types predominated in vulvar-positive/cervical-negative cases (91.67%, 44/48). Vulvar HPV testing showed high concordance with paired cervical testing and may help identify women at low likelihood of concurrent cervical hrHPV positivity. These findings support prospective evaluation of vulvar sampling as a non-invasive adjunct for HPV testing, particularly for women with low acceptance of cervical sampling or limited access to conventional screening. IMPORTANCE Conventional cervical human papillomavirus (HPV) screening remains inaccessible to some women because of discomfort, perceived invasiveness, privacy concerns, and implementation barriers. This study shows that HPV testing with vulvar swabs, a truly non-invasive sampling site, has high concordance with paired cervical testing (κ = 0.821). The high negative predictive value of vulvar high-risk HPV (hrHPV) testing for concurrent cervical hrHPV negativity (95.72%) suggests that a negative vulvar result may identify women at low likelihood of cervical hrHPV positivity, potentially reducing unnecessary referrals. These findings are relevant for older and postmenopausal women, in whom cervical atrophy may decrease the sensitivity of HPV detection. Overall, our results provide preliminary support for prospective evaluation of vulvar sampling as a patient-friendly adjunct to HPV testing, particularly for women with low acceptance of cervical sampling or limited access to conventional screening. Population-based validation with cytological and histological endpoints is required before broader implementation.

abstract_zh: 摘要 对临床医生采集的宫颈取样的依从性低,并且在资源有限的环境中实施障碍限制了基于 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 的 宫颈癌 预防。外阴取样是非侵入性的,更容易进行,但其与宫颈 HPV 检测的一致性仍不明确。我们回顾性分析了 719 份配对的外阴和宫颈标本,这些标本通过经过临床验证的荧光 PCR 检测,以评估采样点之间的一致性以及外阴 HPV 检测的潜在效用。外阴样本中 高危型HPV (hrHPV) 阳性率为 47.98% (345/719),宫颈样本中 高危型HPV (hrHPV) 阳性率为 43.53% (313/719),具有很强的位点一致性 (κ = 0.821)。外阴 hrHPV 检测对并发宫颈 hrHPV 阳性的阴性预测值为 95.72%。HPV18 的一致性最高(κ = 0.892;阴性预测值 [NPV] = 99.41%),其次是 HPV16(κ = 0.839)和低危 HPV6/11(κ = 0.746)。在 5 例活检确诊的宫颈上皮内瘤变病例中,外阴和宫颈 HPV 结果完全一致。年龄分层分析显示 30 岁以下女性的 hrHPV 感染高峰。在40-49岁的女性中,外阴hrHPV阳性率超过宫颈阳性率(56.52% vs 45.65%)。年龄≥40 岁的女性对 hrHPV 和 lrHPV 检测的一致性较低。在不一致的病例中,93.75%(15/16)的外阴阴性/宫颈阳性病例既往有HPV相关治疗,而非HPV16/18类型在外阴阳性/宫颈阴性病例中占主导地位(91.67%,44/48)。外阴 HPV 检测与配对宫颈检测高度一致,可能有助于识别同时宫颈 hrHPV 阳性可能性较低的女性。这些发现支持对外阴取样作为 HPV 检测的非侵入性辅助手段进行前瞻性评估,特别是对于宫颈取样接受度较低或传统筛查机会有限的女性。重要性 由于不适、感知到的侵入性、隐私问题和实施障碍,一些女性仍然无法进行传统的宫颈 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 筛查。这项研究表明,使用外阴拭子进行 HPV 检测(真正的非侵入性采样点)与配对宫颈检测具有很高的一致性(κ = 0.821)。外阴 高危型HPV (hrHPV) 检测对并发宫颈 hrHPV 阴性的高阴性预测值 (95.72%) 表明,阴性外阴结果可能会识别出宫颈 hrHPV 阳性可能性较低的女性,从而可能减少不必要的转诊。这些发现与老年和绝经后女性相关,宫颈萎缩可能会降低 HPV 检测的敏感性。总体而言,我们的结果为外阴取样作为 HPV 检测的患者友好型辅助手段的前瞻性评估提供了初步支持,特别是对于宫颈取样接受度较低或常规筛查机会有限的女性。在更广泛的实施之前,需要使用细胞学和组织学终点进行基于人群的验证。

title: Post-Marketing Safety Surveillance of Autoimmune Diseases Following Bivalent Human Papillomavirus Vaccination in China
abstract: Background/Objectives: The potential of vaccines to trigger autoimmune diseases (ADs) has been extensively investigated and remains a routine focus of vaccine-safety research. This post-marketing, real-world study compared the risk of ADs between females who received bivalent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine (Cecolin) and unvaccinated females. Methods: Eligible females aged 9–45 years registered in the Xiamen Health and Medical Big Data Center from September 2020 to December 2023 (post-Cecolin period) were enrolled. Cecolin recipients constituted the exposed cohort, and a matched unexposed cohort was generated in a 1:4 ratio based on age and calendar year. Case validation was conducted to determine optimal identification algorithms. Incidence rates (IRs) were calculated and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were derived from zero-inflated Poisson regression. Results: Overall incidence of ADs was 70.63 per 100,000 person-years (95% CI: 67.59–73.77) in the post-Cecolin period. Compared with matched unexposed cohorts, vaccinated females showed a significantly lower AD risk in both contemporaneously matched (IRR = 0.23, 95% CI: 0.08–0.65; p = 0.006) and historically matched (IRR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.07–0.66; p = 0.008) analyses. Conclusions: Consistent with prior evidence, this study provides real-world evidence further confirming that Cecolin vaccination does not increase the risk of ADs. It adds the first large-scale post-marketing safety evidence for this Chinese domestic bivalent HPV vaccine, filling a critical evidence gap. These results may inform vaccination policy and guide post-licensure safety monitoring in China and other countries that have introduced this vaccine.

title: '...but look how many lives would have been saved if this was available then' Exploring the acceptability of future Human Papillomavirus self-sampling, and the barriers and facilitators of cervical cancer screening for those with intellectual disabilities in Scotland.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening attendance among women with intellectual disabilities (ID) in Scotland is approximately 30%, significantly below the general population rate of 69% and the WHO's recommended 70% target. HPV self-sampling could provide a more accessible screening option for this underserved population. This study aimed to understand the views and experiences of women with ID regarding cervical cancer screening and the acceptability of HPV self-sampling. METHODS: A qualitative study using focus groups was conducted with women with ID who attended third-sector community groups across Scotland, along with their carers. Four focus groups were held between September and October 2024, with a total of 13 participants (11 women with ID, 2 carers). Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Five main themes emerged: (1) National Health Service (NHS) communication as a source of distress; (2) power imbalances between health care providers and women with ID: feeling unheard, dismissed and out of control; (3) enduring consequences of inadequate care; (4) past trauma shapes future avoidance; and (5) self-sampling as a pathway to empowerment. Participants demonstrated high acceptability of self-sampling, viewing it as a potential solution to overcome barriers to traditional screening. CONCLUSION: This research reveals significant systemic inadequacies in current cervical cancer screening services for women with ID, whilst highlighting self-sampling's transformative potential. Successful implementation requires comprehensive accessible information, enhanced health care professional training and trauma-informed care approaches. Self-sampling could significantly advance health equity goals whilst improving health care outcomes for this underserved population.

title_zh: '...but look how many lives would have been saved if this was available then' 探讨未来人乳头瘤病毒自我采样的可接受性,以及苏格兰智力障碍人群进行宫颈癌筛查的障碍与促进因素
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening attendance among women with intellectual disabilities (ID) in Scotland is approximately 30%, significantly below the general population rate of 69% and the WHO's recommended 70% target. HPV self-sampling could provide a more accessible screening option for this underserved population. This study aimed to understand the views and experiences of women with ID regarding cervical cancer screening and the acceptability of HPV self-sampling. METHODS: A qualitative study using focus groups was conducted with women with ID who attended third-sector community groups across Scotland, along with their carers. Four focus groups were held between September and October 2024, with a total of 13 participants (11 women with ID, 2 carers). Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Five main themes emerged: (1) National Health Service (NHS) communication as a source of distress; (2) power imbalances between health care providers and women with ID: feeling unheard, dismissed and out of control; (3) enduring consequences of inadequate care; (4) past trauma shapes future avoidance; and (5) self-sampling as a pathway to empowerment. Participants demonstrated high acceptability of self-sampling, viewing it as a potential solution to overcome barriers to traditional screening. CONCLUSION: This research reveals significant systemic inadequacies in current cervical cancer screening services for women with ID, whilst highlighting self-sampling's transformative potential. Successful implementation requires comprehensive accessible information, enhanced health care professional training and trauma-informed care approaches. Self-sampling could significantly advance health equity goals whilst improving health care outcomes for this underserved population.
abstract_zh: 背景:苏格兰智障女性 (ID) 的 宫颈癌 筛查出勤率约为 30%,远低于总人口 69% 的比率和世界卫生组织建议的 70% 目标。HPV 自我采样可以为这一服务不足的人群提供更方便的筛查选择。本研究旨在了解患有 ID 的女性对 宫颈癌 筛查以及 HPV 自我采样的可接受性的看法和经验。方法:利用焦点小组对参与苏格兰第三部门社区团体的智障女性及其护理人员进行了一项定性研究。2024 年 9 月至 10 月期间举办了四次焦点小组,共有 13 名参与者(11 名患有智力障碍的女性,2 名护理人员)。使用反思性主题分析对数据进行分析。结果:出现了五个主题:(1) 国家卫生服务 (NHS) 沟通是痛苦的根源;(2) 医疗保健提供者和智障妇女之间的权力失衡:感觉被忽视、被忽视和失控;(3) 护理不足造成的持久后果;(4)过去的创伤塑造了未来的回避;(5) 自我抽样作为赋权的途径。参与者表现出对自我采样的高度接受度,将其视为克服传统筛查障碍的潜在解决方案。结论:这项研究揭示了当前 宫颈癌 针对 ID 女性的筛查服务存在显着的系统性缺陷,同时强调了自我采样的变革潜力。成功的实施需要全面的可获取信息、加强的医疗保健专业培训和创伤知情护理方法。自我采样可以显着推进健康公平目标,同时改善这一服务不足人群的医疗保健结果。

title: Homeopathic resolution of HPV-related perianal warts with high-risk HPV-strains: A case report
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a major etiological factor in cervical dysplasia and related gynecological disorders. Even after surgical management of HPV related cervical disease such as high grade precancerous lesions, cancers and , such as total hysterectomy (TH) with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO), HPV persistence remains a clinical concern, as a residual or recurrent VaIN/vaginal dysplasia may occur. We reported the case of a patient with high-risk HPV infection who initially presented with abnormal uterine bleeding and was diagnosed with cervical dysplasia. She underwent a robotic hysterectomy with BSO, the patient experienced persistent HPV positivity and reappearance of Perianal warts (condyloma acuminata), underscoring the importance of continued surveillance in HPV-positive individuals. The patient had significant psychological distress, including anxiety and fear of incurability. The patient was subsequently treated with homeopathic medicine, which resulted in the successful resolution of perianal warts and improvement in mental well-being too. This highlighted the potential role of complementary approaches in managing HPV-related disease and associated psychological burden. This case emphasizes role of continued surveillance in HPV HR positive patient’s and also this necessitating ongoing monitoring for recurrence. It also illustrates the integration of homeopathy as a supportive therapeutic modality in addressing both physical and psychological aspects of HPV-related disease.

title: Cobertura de vacunación contra el virus del papiloma humano en niñas de 15 años en México: análisis comparativo con la Región de las Américas basado en indicadores de la Organización Mundial de la Salud Human papillomavirus vaccination coverage among 15-year-old girls in Mexico: a comparative analysis with the Region of the Americas based on World Health Organization indicators
abstract: Introduction: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is the most effective strategy for preventing cervical cancer, a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women worldwide. The World Health Organization (WHO) established a target of achieving 90% vaccination coverage among girls before 15 years of age. Objective: To compare HPV vaccination coverage among 15-year-old girls in Mexico and the Region of the Americas between 2010 and 2024. Methods: Descriptive and comparative ecological study based on secondary data obtained from the official WHO indicators platform. Results: Differences in vaccination coverage and proximity to the international target are expected to be identified. Conclusion: Continuous monitoring of vaccination coverage is essential to guide public health policies, strengthen national immunization programs, and accelerate the elimination of cervical cancer as a public health problem.
journal: Revista Multidisciplinar Epistemología de las Ciencias

The World Health Organization (WHO) established a target of achieving 90% vaccination coverage among girls before 15 years of age. Objective: To compare HPV vaccination coverage among 15-year-old girls in Mexico and the Region of the Americas between 2010 and 2024. Methods: Descriptive and comparative ecological study based on secondary data obtained from the official WHO indicators platform. Results: Differences in vaccination coverage and proximity to the international target are expected to be identified. Conclusion: Continuous monitoring of vaccination coverage is essential to guide public health policies, strengthen national immunization programs, and accelerate the elimination of cervical cancer as a public health problem.

title: Coexistence of high-risk HPV infection and FANCC heterozygous variation in early young esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background Esophageal cancer poses a major health challenge in China, with current screening targeting individuals over 40. However, rising incidence in younger populations, often with atypical symptoms, leads to delayed diagnosis. Investigating the underlying causes in this group is urgently needed. Case introduction We report a case of a 28-year-old male with early esophageal squamous cell carcinoma presenting with nonspecific abdominal distension and diarrhea. Lesions were identified using magnifying endoscopy with narrowband imaging and treated via endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). Postoperative pathology confirmed carcinoma in situ. Molecular analysis revealed high-risk HPV 16/18 infection and whole exome sequencing showed DNA repair gene alterations, including heterozygous FANCC variants. A review of 12 PubMed cases of patients under 30 highlighted varied and atypical presentations, often diagnosed at advanced stages with poor prognosis. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of clinical vigilance for young individuals with persistent symptoms and risk factors, serving as a potential complement to current age-based screening guidelines. The RNAscope finding (score 3) highly suggests HPV-driven oncogenesis based on established criteria in HPV-associated cancers. A germline heterozygous FANCC VUS was also identified, but no mechanistic conclusion can be drawn from this finding without functional validation. The coexistence of these two findings provides a hypothesis-generating clue for future research.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomavirus (HPV), specifically high-risk types HPV16/18, in the context of early esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) among young individuals, focusing on the central question of whether HPV co-infection with genetic predispositions (e.g., FANCC variants) contributes to oncogenesis in this understudied population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base consists of a single case report and a literature review of 12 PubMed cases of ESCC in patients under 30, identified through unspecified search methods. The review synthesizes clinical, endoscopic, pathological, and molecular findings (e.g., HPV detection via RNAscope, whole exome sequencing for FANCC variants) without reporting formal eligibility criteria, databases, or meta-analytic processes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that high-risk HPV16/18 infection and heterozygous FANCC variants may coexist in early ESCC among young patients, with RNAscope evidence (score 3) suggesting HPV-driven oncogenesis. However, the clinical significance of the FANCC variant remains uncertain due to lack of functional validation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights unresolved questions regarding the mechanistic role of FANCC variants in HPV-associated ESCC, as no functional studies were conducted to confirm causality. Additionally, the literature review of 12 cases under 30 showed varied and atypical presentations, often leading to delayed diagnosis at advanced stages, underscoring diagnostic challenges in this population.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for increased clinical vigilance for young individuals with persistent gastrointestinal symptoms and risk factors, suggesting that current age-based screening guidelines may be insufficient. It also calls for functional validation of FANCC variants and further investigation into HPV-driven oncogenesis in esophageal tissues.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the coexistence of high-risk HPV16/18 infection and heterozygous FANCC variants in a 28-year-old male with early esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), identified via magnifying endoscopy and treated with endoscopic submucosal dissection. Molecular analysis confirmed HPV-driven oncogenesis (RNAscope score 3), while whole exome sequencing revealed a germline FANCC variant of uncertain significance. A literature review of 12 PubMed cases under 30 highlighted atypical presentations and delayed diagnoses, often at advanced stages. The review concludes that HPV may contribute to ESCC in young patients but stresses the need for functional validation of genetic findings and improved diagnostic strategies to address gaps in early detection.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomavirus (HPV), specifically high-risk types HPV16/18, in the context of early esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) among young individuals, focusing on the central question of whether HPV co-infection with genetic predispositions (e.g., FANCC variants) contributes to oncogenesis in this understudied population.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base consists of a single case report and a literature review of 12 PubMed cases of ESCC in patients under 30, identified through unspecified search methods. The review synthesizes clinical, endoscopic, pathological, and molecular findings (e.g., HPV detection via RNAscope, whole exome sequencing for FANCC variants) without reporting formal eligibility criteria, databases, or meta-analytic processes.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that high-risk HPV16/18 infection and heterozygous FANCC variants may coexist in early ESCC among young patients, with RNAscope evidence (score 3) suggesting HPV-driven oncogenesis. However, the clinical significance of the FANCC variant remains uncertain due to lack of functional validation.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights unresolved questions regarding the mechanistic role of FANCC variants in HPV-associated ESCC, as no functional studies were conducted to confirm causality. Additionally, the literature review of 12 cases under 30 showed varied and atypical presentations, often leading to delayed diagnosis at advanced stages, underscoring diagnostic challenges in this population.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for increased clinical vigilance for young individuals with persistent gastrointestinal symptoms and risk factors, suggesting that current age-based screening guidelines may be insufficient. It also calls for functional validation of FANCC variants and further investigation into HPV-driven oncogenesis in esophageal tissues.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述在年轻个体中早期食管鳞状细胞癌 (ESCC) 的背景下检查了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV),特别是高危型 HPV16/18,重点关注 HPV 与遗传易感性(例如 FANCC 变体)的共同感染是否会导致这一被研究人群的肿瘤发生。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 证据基础包括单个 病例报告 和通过未指定的搜索方法确定的 12 例 PubMed 30 岁以下 ESCC 病例的文献综述。该综述综合了临床、内窥镜、病理和分子发现(例如,通过 RNAscope 检测 HPV、FANCC 变异的全外显子测序),但没有报告正式的资格标准、数据库或荟萃分析过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,高危 HPV16/18 感染和杂合 FANCC 变异可能在年轻患者的早期 ESCC 中共存,RNAscope 证据(评分 3)表明 HPV 驱动的肿瘤发生。然而,由于缺乏功能验证,FANCC 变异的临床意义仍不确定。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了有关 FANCC 变异在 HPV 相关 ESCC 中的机制作用的尚未解决的问题,因为没有进行功能性研究来确认因果关系。此外,对 12 例 30 岁以下病例的文献综述显示出不同的非典型表现,常常导致晚期 诊断 延迟,强调了该人群的诊断挑战。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调需要提高对具有持续胃肠道症状和危险因素的年轻人的临床警惕性,这表明当前基于年龄的筛查指南可能还不够。它还呼吁对 FANCC 变体进行功能验证,并进一步研究食管组织中 HPV 驱动的肿瘤发生。

title_zh: 早期年轻食管鳞癌中高危型HPV感染与FANCC杂合变异的共存:病例报告和文献综述
source_body_en: Abstract Background Esophageal cancer poses a major health challenge in China, with current screening targeting individuals over 40. However, rising incidence in younger populations, often with atypical symptoms, leads to delayed diagnosis. Investigating the underlying causes in this group is urgently needed. Case introduction We report a case of a 28-year-old male with early esophageal squamous cell carcinoma presenting with nonspecific abdominal distension and diarrhea. Lesions were identified using magnifying endoscopy with narrowband imaging and treated via endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). Postoperative pathology confirmed carcinoma in situ. Molecular analysis revealed high-risk HPV 16/18 infection and whole exome sequencing showed DNA repair gene alterations, including heterozygous FANCC variants. A review of 12 PubMed cases of patients under 30 highlighted varied and atypical presentations, often diagnosed at advanced stages with poor prognosis. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of clinical vigilance for young individuals with persistent symptoms and risk factors, serving as a potential complement to current age-based screening guidelines. The RNAscope finding (score 3) highly suggests HPV-driven oncogenesis based on established criteria in HPV-associated cancers. A germline heterozygous FANCC VUS was also identified, but no mechanistic conclusion can be drawn from this finding without functional validation. The coexistence of these two findings provides a hypothesis-generating clue for future research.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 食管癌在中国构成了重大健康挑战,目前筛查针对的是 40 岁以上的人群。然而,年轻人群中 发病率 的上升(通常症状不典型)导致 发病率 延迟。迫切需要调查该群体的根本原因。病例介绍 我们报告一例28岁男性,患有早期食管鳞癌,表现为非特异性腹胀和腹泻。使用放大内窥镜和窄带成像来识别病变,并通过内镜粘膜下剥离术(ESD)进行治疗。术后病理证实原位癌。分子分析显示 高危型HPV 16/18 感染,全外显子组测序显示 DNA 修复基因改变,包括杂合 FANCC 变异。对 12 个 30 岁以下患者的 PubMed 病例的回顾强调了不同的和非典型的表现,通常在晚期诊断,预后不良。结论 该病例强调了对具有持续症状和危险因素的年轻人保持临床警惕的重要性,可作为当前基于年龄的筛查指南的潜在补充。根据 HPV 相关癌症的既定标准,RNAscope 的发现(评分 3)高度表明 HPV 驱动的肿瘤发生。还鉴定出种系杂合 FANCC VUS,但未经功能验证,无法从这一发现得出机制结论。这两项发现的共存为未来的研究提供了假设生成线索。

title: Developing an Interactive Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Education Program for Oropharyngeal Cancer Patients and Healthcare Providers: Lessons Learned from the Target Users’ Feedback
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is associated with multiple head and neck cancers, many of which are preventable with the 9-valent HPV vaccine. We developed an interactive HPV vaccination education program (IHVEP) to equip patients with HPV-associated cancers to serve as health educators. Objective: To pilot test the adapted IHVEP, evaluate its content using the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills (IMB) model and the Suitability Assessment of Materials (SAM) instrument, and identify factors relevant to optimizing digital health interventions. Methods: A previously developed cervical cancer–focused IHVEP was adapted for patients with oropharyngeal cancer. Participants completed the program and participated in semi-structured interviews. Feedback was analyzed and organized into themes aligned with the IMB and SAM frameworks. Results: Participants generally perceived the adapted IHVEP as informative, motivating, and empowering. Key motivators included physician recommendation and a desire to protect others. The program appeared to enhance participants’ perceived ability and self-efficacy to promote HPV vaccination. Modules were described as clear, well-organized, linguistically accessible, and culturally appropriate. Feedback identified areas for improvement related to technology, content, and functionality. Conclusions: Findings suggest that effective digital health interventions may benefit from incorporating training in evaluating health information, ensuring intuitive design and navigation, and including content featuring real individuals. These results will inform further refinement of IHVEP and the development of future digital health interventions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: HPV is etiologically linked to preventable head and neck cancers, yet vaccination uptake remains suboptimal among at-risk groups. The study sought to address knowledge gaps in patient-facing HPV education by developing and piloting an interactive HPV vaccination education program tailored to HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A previously developed cervical cancer–focused interactive HPV vaccination education program was adapted for patients with HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer. Participants completed the adapted program and provided feedback through semi-structured interviews.
analysis.methods: The adapted program was evaluated using the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills model and the Suitability Assessment of Materials instrument. Feedback was analyzed and organized into themes aligned with these frameworks.
analysis.main_results: Participants generally perceived the adapted program as informative, motivating, and empowering, with modules described as clear, well-organized, linguistically accessible, and culturally appropriate.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that the program enhanced participants’ perceived ability and self-efficacy to promote HPV vaccination, highlighting the importance of intuitive design, real-person content, and training in evaluating health information.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that digital health interventions for HPV vaccination education can be optimized by incorporating user-centered design elements and content featuring real individuals to improve engagement and effectiveness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a small pilot study with qualitative feedback, which constrains generalizability and precludes causal inference; the strength of evidence is therefore low.

analysis.summary_en: This pilot study adapted an interactive HPV vaccination education program originally designed for cervical cancer patients to serve HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer patients as health educators. Using the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills model and Suitability Assessment of Materials instrument, the authors evaluated participant feedback collected via semi-structured interviews. Participants reported that the adapted program was informative, motivating, and empowering, with modules praised for clarity, organization, accessibility, and cultural appropriateness. Key motivators included physician recommendations and a desire to protect others, while feedback identified areas for improvement in technology, content, and functionality. The authors conclude that effective digital interventions should incorporate training in evaluating health information, intuitive design, and real-person content. However, the study’s small sample and qualitative design limit generalizability and causal inference, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: HPV 在病因学上与可预防的头颈癌有关,但 疫苗接种 在高危人群中的吸收率仍然不理想。该研究旨在通过开发和试点针对 HPV 相关口咽癌患者的交互式 HPV 疫苗接种 教育计划来解决面向患者的 HPV 教育的知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 先前开发的以 宫颈癌 为重点的交互式 HPV 疫苗接种 教育计划适用于 HPV 相关口咽癌患者。参与者完成了改编后的计划,并通过半结构化访谈提供了反馈。
elements_zh.methods: 使用信息-动机-行为技能模型和材料适用性评估工具对改编后的程序进行了评估。反馈被分析并组织成与这些框架一致的主题。
elements_zh.main_results: 参与者普遍认为改编后的课程内容丰富、具有激励性和赋权性,其模块被描述为清晰、组织良好、语言易于理解且文化适宜。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为表明该计划增强了参与者宣传 HPV 疫苗接种 的感知能力和自我效能,强调了直观设计、真人内容和评估健康信息培训的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,可以通过纳入以用户为中心的设计元素和以真实个人为特色的内容来优化 HPV 疫苗接种 教育的数字健康干预措施,以提高参与度和有效性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: HPV is etiologically linked to preventable head and neck cancers, yet vaccination uptake remains suboptimal among at-risk groups. The study sought to address knowledge gaps in patient-facing HPV education by developing and piloting an interactive HPV vaccination education program tailored to HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer patients.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A previously developed cervical cancer–focused interactive HPV vaccination education program was adapted for patients with HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer. Participants completed the adapted program and provided feedback through semi-structured interviews.
analysis_en.methods: The adapted program was evaluated using the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills model and the Suitability Assessment of Materials instrument. Feedback was analyzed and organized into themes aligned with these frameworks.
analysis_en.main_results: Participants generally perceived the adapted program as informative, motivating, and empowering, with modules described as clear, well-organized, linguistically accessible, and culturally appropriate.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that the program enhanced participants’ perceived ability and self-efficacy to promote HPV vaccination, highlighting the importance of intuitive design, real-person content, and training in evaluating health information.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that digital health interventions for HPV vaccination education can be optimized by incorporating user-centered design elements and content featuring real individuals to improve engagement and effectiveness.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a small pilot study with qualitative feedback, which constrains generalizability and precludes causal inference; the strength of evidence is therefore low.

title_zh: 为口咽癌患者和医疗保健提供者开发交互式 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 教育计划:从目标用户反馈中吸取的教训
source_body_en: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is associated with multiple head and neck cancers, many of which are preventable with the 9-valent HPV vaccine. We developed an interactive HPV vaccination education program (IHVEP) to equip patients with HPV-associated cancers to serve as health educators. Objective: To pilot test the adapted IHVEP, evaluate its content using the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills (IMB) model and the Suitability Assessment of Materials (SAM) instrument, and identify factors relevant to optimizing digital health interventions. Methods: A previously developed cervical cancer–focused IHVEP was adapted for patients with oropharyngeal cancer. Participants completed the program and participated in semi-structured interviews. Feedback was analyzed and organized into themes aligned with the IMB and SAM frameworks. Results: Participants generally perceived the adapted IHVEP as informative, motivating, and empowering. Key motivators included physician recommendation and a desire to protect others. The program appeared to enhance participants’ perceived ability and self-efficacy to promote HPV vaccination. Modules were described as clear, well-organized, linguistically accessible, and culturally appropriate. Feedback identified areas for improvement related to technology, content, and functionality. Conclusions: Findings suggest that effective digital health interventions may benefit from incorporating training in evaluating health information, ensuring intuitive design and navigation, and including content featuring real individuals. These results will inform further refinement of IHVEP and the development of future digital health interventions.

title: Epidemiology and genotype distribution of cervical high-risk human papillomavirus infection among women in Punjab, India: A large-scale retrospective analysis
abstract: Abstract Background: The study aimed to determine the prevalence and genotype of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) among women in Punjab region and to assess the association between single/multiple HPV infections and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). Materials and Methods: The study involved retrospective analysis of electronic health records for individuals, for which cervical samples were tested for HPV DNA using a real-time polymerase chain reaction assay (Seegene assay) between January 2023 and July 2025. The study included females participating in out-campus screening camps and those attending the department of preventive oncology for routine screening and consenting to undergo HPV testing. Results: Overall HPV prevalence in the study population was 13.8% (544/3919). The most common genotypes were HPV-16 (35.7%), HPV-18 (14%), and HPV-66 (11%). Single genotype infections were most frequent (66.5%). The peak prevalence occurred in women of age group 36–40 years. Multiple HPV infections were significantly associated with higher CIN 2/3 lesions (χ 2 = 4.6; P = 0.032; odds ratio [OR] = 2.8). HPV-16 women had higher, though nonsignificant odds of developing high-grade CIN (OR = 1.96; P = 0.09). HPV-66-positive women had lower odds of developing high-grade CIN, though statistically nonsignificant (OR = 0.47; P = 0.33). Conclusions: There is substantial HPV burden in local population with HPV-16 and HPV-18 as the dominant genotypes. The unexpected high frequency of HPV-66 genotype warrants further molecular and epidemiological investigations. The study findings reinforce the need for implementing systematic large-scale HPV vaccination and HPV screening and molecular testing programs in India to achieve the World Health Organization’s cervical cancer elimination goals.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:本研究旨在确定旁遮普地区女性高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的感染率与基因型,并评估单一/多重HPV感染与宫颈上皮内瘤变(CIN)的关联。材料与方法:本研究回顾性分析了2023年1月至2025年7月期间通过实时聚合酶链反应(Seegene试剂盒)检测HPV DNA的宫颈样本的电子健康记录。研究对象包括参与院外筛查营的女性及前往预防肿瘤学科室进行常规筛查并同意接受HPV检测的女性。结果:研究人群中HPV总体患病率为13.8%(544/3919)。最常见基因型为HPV-16(35.7%)、HPV-18(14%)和HPV-66(11%)。单一基因型感染最为常见(66.5%)。HPV感染率在36–40岁年龄组女性中达到峰值。多重HPV感染与更高等级CIN 2/3病变显著相关(χ2=4.6;P=0.032;优势比[OR]=2.8)。HPV-16阳性女性发生高级别CIN的优势比虽较高但未达统计学显著(OR=1.96;P=0.09)。HPV-66阳性女性发生高级别CIN的优势比虽较低但未达统计学显著(OR=0.47;P=0.33)。结论:当地人群HPV负担较重,HPV-16与HPV-18为主要基因型。HPV-66基因型的意外高频率需进一步开展分子与流行病学调查。研究结果强化了在印度实施系统性大规模HPV疫苗接种与HPV筛查及分子检测项目的必要性,以实现世界卫生组织消除HPV的目标。
