title: Epigallocatechin gallate, folic acid, vitamin B12 and hyaluronic acid in the management of male Human Papilloma Virus Infection: A case series.
abstract: Human Papilloma Virus infection represents one of the most common sexually transmitted infections worldwide. While research on Human Papilloma Virus has traditionally focused on its role in cervical cancer pathogenesis, such infection is also highly prevalent in the male population. Despite this, the clinical management of Human Papilloma Virus in men still remains limited, with no universally accepted screening protocols or therapeutic guidelines. This clinical case series describes six male patients (aged 26-66 years) with Human Papilloma Virus infection detected in samples of urethral mucosa, anal mucosa, or seminal fluid. Each patient took the dietary supplement containing epigallocatechin gallate (200 mg), folic acid (400 μg), vitamin B12 (1 mg), and hyaluronic acid (50 mg) daily for up to 6 months. After the oral supplementation, each patient reported complete Human Papilloma Virus clearance. These findings provide, for the first time, preliminary evidence on the positive effect of such molecules in promoting Human Papilloma Virus clearance across different male anatomical sites, including anal and urethral mucosa and seminal fluid. Although preliminary, this report highlights the often-overlooked issue of Human Papilloma Virus management in men, thus paving the way for additional clinical studies with the aim of defining the role of such dietary supplements in counteracting Human Papilloma Virus infection in men.

title_zh: 表没食子儿茶素没食子酸酯、叶酸、维生素 B12 和透明质酸治疗男性人乳头瘤病毒感染:病例系列。
source_body_en: Human Papilloma Virus infection represents one of the most common sexually transmitted infections worldwide. While research on Human Papilloma Virus has traditionally focused on its role in cervical cancer pathogenesis, such infection is also highly prevalent in the male population. Despite this, the clinical management of Human Papilloma Virus in men still remains limited, with no universally accepted screening protocols or therapeutic guidelines. This clinical case series describes six male patients (aged 26-66 years) with Human Papilloma Virus infection detected in samples of urethral mucosa, anal mucosa, or seminal fluid. Each patient took the dietary supplement containing epigallocatechin gallate (200 mg), folic acid (400 μg), vitamin B12 (1 mg), and hyaluronic acid (50 mg) daily for up to 6 months. After the oral supplementation, each patient reported complete Human Papilloma Virus clearance. These findings provide, for the first time, preliminary evidence on the positive effect of such molecules in promoting Human Papilloma Virus clearance across different male anatomical sites, including anal and urethral mucosa and seminal fluid. Although preliminary, this report highlights the often-overlooked issue of Human Papilloma Virus management in men, thus paving the way for additional clinical studies with the aim of defining the role of such dietary supplements in counteracting Human Papilloma Virus infection in men.

title: The mediating role of human papillomavirus concern in the relationship between human papillomavirus knowledge and preventive behaviors against sexually transmitted diseases among Turkish women with higher education.
abstract: SUMMARY OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to examine the mediating role of health-related concern in the relationship between human papillomavirus knowledge and behaviors for protection from sexually transmitted diseases among women of higher education. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 623 women. Data were collected online using the Personal Information Form, Human Papillomavirus Knowledge Scale, Behaviors for Protection from Sexually Transmitted Diseases Scale, and human papillomavirus Awareness and Concern Level Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, multiple linear regression analysis, and Structural Equation Modeling with Bootstrap analysis. RESULTS: The mean scores of the participants were 17.06±6.66 for Human Papillomavirus Knowledge Scale and 79.41±9.38 for Behaviors for Protection from Sexually Transmitted Diseases Scale. Correlation analyses showed that human papillomavirus knowledge was positively associated with awareness (r=0.239; p<0.001), health-related concern (r=0.121; p=0.002), and sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors (r=0.423; p<0.001). Stigma-related concern was negatively associated with sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors (r=-0.193; p<0.001). Structural Equation Modeling analyses demonstrated that human papillomavirus knowledge significantly predicted health-related concern (β=0.121; p=0.002), and health-related concern was significantly associated with sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors (β=0.089; p=0.015). The indirect effect was statistically significant but limited (standardized indirect effect=0.011; p<0.05). The mediation model explained 1.5% of the variance in health-related concern and 18.6% of the variance in sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors. CONCLUSION: Health-related concern demonstrated a statistically significant but limited partial mediating role in the relationship between human papillomavirus knowledge and sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors. The findings suggest that cognitive and affective dimensions should be evaluated separately when examining human papillomavirus-related perceptions and preventive sexual health behaviors

analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 623 women with higher education in Turkey.
analysis.methods: Participants completed validated scales measuring HPV knowledge, behaviors for protection from sexually transmitted diseases, and HPV awareness and concern, with data analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, multiple linear regression, and Structural Equation Modeling with Bootstrap.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study of 623 higher-educated Turkish women examined whether HPV knowledge influences sexually transmitted disease prevention behaviors and whether health-related concern mediates this relationship. Using validated scales and Structural Equation Modeling, the authors found that HPV knowledge was positively associated with awareness, concern, and prevention behaviors, while stigma-related concern was negatively associated with behaviors. Mediation analysis revealed a statistically significant but limited indirect effect of HPV knowledge on prevention behaviors through health-related concern (standardized indirect effect=0.011; p<0.05). The mediation model explained 1.5% of the variance in concern and 18.6% in behaviors. The study suggests that cognitive and affective dimensions should be evaluated separately in HPV-related sexual health behavior research, but the cross-sectional design and modest explanatory power limit causal inference and generalizability.

abstract_zh: 摘要目的:本研究的目的是探讨健康相关关注在高等教育女性预防性传播疾病的 人乳头瘤病毒 知识和行为之间的中介作用。方法:这项横断面研究包括 623 名女性。使用个人信息表、人乳头瘤病毒 知识量表、性传播疾病防护行为量表以及 人乳头瘤病毒 意识和关注水平量表在线收集数据。使用描述性统计、Pearson 相关分析、多元线性回归分析和结构方程模型与 Bootstrap 分析对数据进行分析。结果:参与者的人乳头瘤病毒知识量表平均得分为17.06±6.66,性传播疾病防护行为量表平均得分为79.41±9.38。相关分析显示,人乳头瘤病毒 知识与认知度(r=0.239;p<0.001)、健康相关关注(r=0.121;p=0.002)和性传播疾病预防行为(r=0.423;p<0.001)呈正相关。与耻辱相关的担忧与性传播疾病预防行为呈负相关(r=-0.193;p<0.001)。结构方程模型分析表明,人乳头瘤病毒 知识显着预测健康相关担忧(β=0.121;p=0.002),健康相关担忧与性传播疾病预防行为显着相关(β=0.089;p=0.015)。间接效应具有统计学显着性但有限(标准化间接效应=0.011;p<0.05)。中介模型解释了 1.5% 的健康相关关注差异和 18.6% 的性传播疾病预防行为差异。结论:健康相关的关注在 人乳头瘤病毒 知识与性传播疾病预防行为之间的关系中显示出统计显着但有限的部分中介作用。研究结果表明,在检查 人乳头瘤病毒 相关认知和预防性性健康行为时,应分别评估认知和情感维度

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了尽管受过高等教育的女性对性传播疾病预防行为的接受度较低的公共卫生问题,并询问 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 知识是否会影响这些行为,以及健康相关的担忧是否会调节这种关系。

analysis_zh.methods: 参与者完成了经过验证的量表,测量 HPV 知识、预防性传播疾病的行为以及 HPV 认知和关注,并使用描述性统计、皮尔逊相关性、多元线性回归和 Bootstrap 结构方程模型对数据进行分析。

title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus infections among women undergoing HPV testing during 2019–2024 in Xi’an, China
abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) persistent infection is the primary cause of cervical cancer, with significant regional variations in infection prevalence and genotype distribution. This study aimed to clarify the epidemiological characteristics of HPV infection among women in Xi’an from April 2019 to December 2024, and to provide targeted evidence for local cervical cancer screening and prevention strategies. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 33,316 women (aged ≥ 20 years) who underwent HPV testing at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi’an Jiaotong University during the study period, with repeated tests from the same individual excluded. PCR-reverse dot blot hybridization was used to detect 28 HPV genotypes. The chi-square test was applied for intergroup comparison of infection rates, with P Results The overall HPV positivity rate was 13.96% (4,650/33,316), with single-type infections accounting for 74.67% (3,472/4,650) and multiple-type infections for 25.33% (1,178/4,650). The top three prevalent genotypes were HPV52 (18.00%), HPV53 (12.19%), and HPV16 (9.23%). Significant differences in HPV infection rates were observed among health examination population (12.67%), inpatients (20.85%) and outpatients (37.68%) ( P P Conclusions Single-type HPV infection is the main type of infection among women in Xi’an, with HPV52, HPV53 and HPV16 being the dominant genotypes. Infection rates vary significantly by patient source and age, with older women aged 61–70 years at the highest risk of infection. These findings highlight the need to optimize local cervical cancer screening strategies, strengthen HPV vaccination for young women, and conduct regular regional HPV epidemiological surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) infections among women in Xi’an, China, from 2019 to 2024. The research aimed to provide insights for local cervical cancer screening and prevention strategies. A retrospective analysis of 33,316 women who underwent HPV testing at a specific hospital was conducted, excluding repeated tests from the same individual. The PCR-reverse dot blot hybridization method was used to detect 28 HPV genotypes. The overall HPV positivity rate was 13.96%, with most infections being single-type. title: Epidemiological Profile of High-Risk HPV in Cervical Samples for Liquid-Based Cytology: Insights from Screening and Symptomatic Cohorts
abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is the principal etiological factor in cervical cancer, with genotype distribution and cytological associations varying across populations. This retrospective study aimed to characterize the prevalence and genotype distribution of HR-HPV among 1747 Bulgarian women, including a subgroup of 1134 women with paired HPV polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and liquid-based cytology (LBC) results. The study population comprised women undergoing routine cervical screening (76.0%, n = 1328) and women tested because of clinical indications, including gynecological symptoms (24.0%, n = 419). The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 31.4% (549/1747) and was significantly higher among women tested for clinical indications than among those undergoing routine screening. HPV16 was the most frequently detected genotype, followed by multiple HR-HPV infections and other genotypes, including HPV31, HPV51, HPV66, HPV18, HPV45, HPV56, HPV68, and HPV33. Cytological abnormalities were identified in 24.7% (280/1134) of women with paired HPV and cytology results. HR-HPV positivity was strongly associated with abnormal cytology; however, 27.3% (233/854) of women with negative cytology were also HR-HPV positive. Integrating HPV genotyping with cytology may improve risk stratification and support more targeted clinical management. Despite the increasing use of LBC and HPV co-testing, comparative data describing HR-HPV genotype distribution and its relationship with cytological findings in screening and symptomatic populations remain limited. These findings provide epidemiological evidence on HR-HPV infection patterns in Bulgarian women and establish a foundation for future studies evaluating genotype-specific risks, disease progression, and population-based surveillance strategies.

This retrospective study aimed to characterize the prevalence and genotype distribution of HR-HPV among 1747 Bulgarian women, including a subgroup of 1134 women with paired HPV polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and liquid-based cytology (LBC) results. The study population comprised women undergoing routine cervical screening (76.0%, n = 1328) and women tested because of clinical indications, including gynecological symptoms (24.0%, n = 419). The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 31.4% (549/1747) and was significantly higher among women tested for clinical indications than among those undergoing routine screening. HPV16 was the most frequently detected genotype, followed by multiple HR-HPV infections and other genotypes, including HPV31, HPV51, HPV66, HPV18, HPV45, HPV56, HPV68, and HPV33. Cytological abnormalities were identified in 24.7% (280/1134) of women with paired HPV and cytology results. HR-HPV positivity was strongly associated with abnormal cytology; however, 27.3% (233/854) of women with negative cytology were also HR-HPV positive. Integrating HPV genotyping with cytology may improve risk stratification and support more targeted clinical management. Despite the increasing use of LBC and HPV co-testing, comparative data describing HR-HPV genotype distribution and its relationship with cytological findings in screening and symptomatic populations remain limited. These findings provide epidemiological evidence on HR-HPV infection patterns in Bulgarian women and establish a foundation for future studies evaluating genotype-specific risks, disease progression, and population-based surveillance strategies.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 HR-HPV 阳性与异常细胞学之间的密切相关性解释为支持将 HPV 基因分型与细胞学相结合以改善风险分层的证据,并指出 27.3% (233/854) 细胞学阴性的女性为 HR-HPV 阳性。

abstract_zh: 高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV) 感染是 宫颈癌 的主要病因,不同人群的基因型分布和细胞学关联各不相同。这项回顾性研究旨在描述 1747 名保加利亚女性中 HR-HPV 的 患病率 和基因型分布特征,其中包括 1134 名女性亚组,并具有配对 HPV 聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 和液基细胞学 (LBC) 结果。研究人群包括接受常规宫颈筛查的女性(76.0%,n = 1328)和因临床指征(包括妇科症状)而接受测试的女性(24.0%,n = 419)。总体 HR-HPV 患病率 为 31.4% (549/1747),在接受临床指征测试的女性中显着高于接受常规筛查的女性。HPV16 是最常检测到的基因型,其次是多重 HR-HPV 感染和其他基因型,包括 HPV31、HPV51、HPV66、HPV18、HPV45、HPV56、HPV68 和 HPV33。24.7% (280/1134) 的 HPV 和细胞学结果配对的女性中发现细胞学异常。HR-HPV 阳性与细胞学异常密切相关;然而,27.3% (233/854) 细胞学阴性的女性 HR-HPV 也呈阳性。将 HPV 基因分型与细胞学相结合可以改善风险分层并支持更有针对性的临床管理。尽管越来越多地使用 LBC 和 HPV 联合检测,但描述 HR-HPV 基因型分布及其与筛查和有症状人群中细胞学结果的关系的比较数据仍然有限。这些发现提供了保加利亚女性 HR-HPV 感染模式的流行病学证据,并为未来评估基因型特异性风险、疾病进展和基于人群的 监测 策略的研究奠定了基础。

title: Assessment of Human Papilloma Virus Infection and Vaccine Awareness among Female Secondary School Students in Enugu Metropolis, Nigeria: A Pre-Vaccination Rollout Survey
abstract: Background: The prevalence of human papilloma virus(HPV) infection is high in the general population and HPV is considered an important cause of cervical cancer which is a preventable disease. However, previous studies done in other settings in Nigeria and other African countries suggested that there was low level of awareness of HPV infection and its vaccine. Objectives: This study assessed the knowledge and awareness of HPV infection and its vaccine among female secondary school students in Enugu metropolis, Nigeria, prior to the National HPV vaccination rollout in October 2023. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 647 female students aged 10–19 years in Enugu metropolis in October 2023. Data was collected using structured, self-administered questionnaires. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to explore associations between knowledge and demographic variables. Results: The mean age of participants was 13.45 ± 1.81 years. Overall, 78% had never heard of HPV, and 79.8% demonstrated poor knowledge of the HPV vaccine. Students older than 13 years and those with more educated parents showed significantly higher awareness. Schools were the most cited source of information (53%). Misconceptions about HPV symptoms and prevention were common. Conclusion: Awareness of HPV and its vaccine was poor among the target demographic, underscoring the need for early school-based education and multi-sect oral stakeholder engagement to improve awareness of HPV infection and its vaccination uptake.
journal: American journal of public health research

This study aimed to assess knowledge and awareness of HPV infection and its vaccine among female secondary school students in Enugu metropolis before the national HPV vaccination rollout.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted in October 2023 among 647 female secondary school students aged 10–19 years in Enugu metropolis, Nigeria.
analysis.methods: Data were collected using structured, self-administered questionnaires, and associations between knowledge and demographic variables were explored using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests.
analysis.main_results: The mean age of participants was 13.45 ± 1.81 years, 78% had never heard of HPV, and 79.8% demonstrated poor knowledge of the HPV vaccine. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating poor awareness of HPV and its vaccine among the target demographic, highlighting the need for early school-based education and multi-sectoral stakeholder engagement to improve awareness and vaccination uptake.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted educational interventions in schools and community engagement are necessary to address misconceptions about HPV symptoms and prevention, thereby improving vaccine uptake and reducing HPV-associated disease burden.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解读为,目标人群对 HPV 及其 疫苗 的认识较差,强调需要进行早期学校教育和多部门利益相关者参与,以提高认识和 疫苗接种 的采用率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,有必要在学校和社区参与中有针对性的教育干预措施,以消除对 HPV 症状和预防的误解,从而提高 疫苗 的吸收率并减少 HPV 相关疾病负担。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的横断面设计和对自我报告数据的依赖限制了因果推断,并可能引入反应偏差,导致证据强度中等。

title: Human papillomavirus genotypes in cervicitis and atypical squamous cell of undetermined significance lesions among women in Erbil, Iraq: Human Papillomavirus Genotypes in Cervicitis and ASCUS Lesions Among Women in Erbil, Iraq
abstract: Background and objective: Human papillomavirus infection is known to be the primary reason for cervical carcinoma. Steady infection with high risk (HR)-HPV strains is behind most abnormal cervical lesions, this studyaims to investigate the prevalence and genotype distribution of HPV in cervical samples from women between 20 to 50 years old with different cervical lesions, including cervicitis and atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US) cases. Methods: Cervical smears of 113 patients diagnosed with atypical squamous cell of undetermined significance and cervicitis were included in the study and examined for HPV detection used reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and hybridization method, followed by HPV genotyping assay specimens Results: Out of the total 113 cases, 24.74% were positive for HPV infection, and 75.22% were negative for HPV infection. Most of the patients diagnosed with cervicitis were within 35-39 age group, accounting for 26.3% of the total cases. In contrast, most patients with ASCUS were in the 30-34 age group, representing 29.7%. The majority of patients exhibit a single serotype (60.7%), while multiple serotypes were found in 39.3%. HR-HPV16 and multiple genotype HPV (31,35,39,51,52,56,58,59,66, and 68) were the most frequently identified genotypes. Conclusion: The detection of both low- and HR- HPV genotypes were reported and not uncommon among patients with cervicitis and a typical squamous cell of undetermined significance. High risk (HR)-HPV16 and multiple genotypes were the most frequently diagnosed by PCR test. Consequently, it is highly advisable to create a program for cervical cancer screening and prophylactic HPV vaccination for early diagnosis and prevention of cervical abnormalities and neoplasia in Iraq.

title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus in the public health system of the central-northern region of Chile
abstract: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to determine the frequency of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the public health system, as previous research had found a high prevalence in the private health system.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study analyzed 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 in the central-northern region of Chile.
analysis.methods: Samples were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique to detect HR-HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis.main_results: The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had significantly higher rates of LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) than HPV-negative women.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HR-HPV prevalence in the public health system was similar to previously reported national rates but lower than in the private health system in the same region, highlighting potential disparities in HPV infection rates between healthcare systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform public health surveillance and resource allocation by providing age-stratified prevalence data, which can guide targeted screening and prevention strategies for HPV-related diseases in the public health system.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's strength lies in its large sample size and longitudinal design, but limitations include potential selection bias as only women attending gynecological check-ups were included, and the evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the report.

These findings provide valuable data for public health planning and targeted screening programs.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to determine the frequency of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the public health system, as previous research had found a high prevalence in the private health system.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study analyzed 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 in the central-northern region of Chile.
analysis_en.methods: Samples were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique to detect HR-HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis_en.main_results: The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had significantly higher rates of LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) than HPV-negative women.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HR-HPV prevalence in the public health system was similar to previously reported national rates but lower than in the private health system in the same region, highlighting potential disparities in HPV infection rates between healthcare systems.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform public health surveillance and resource allocation by providing age-stratified prevalence data, which can guide targeted screening and prevention strategies for HPV-related diseases in the public health system.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's strength lies in its large sample size and longitudinal design, but limitations include potential selection bias as only women attending gynecological check-ups were included, and the evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the report.

title_zh: 智利中北部地区公共卫生系统中的患病率 人乳头瘤病毒
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

title: The influence of human papillomaviruses on the cytokine profile of blood serum and cervical mucus in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia
abstract: To investigate the influence of different types of human papillomavirus (HPV) and the level of viral load on the profiles of cytokine factors in cervical mucus and blood serum in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Material and methods. The study included 30 healthy women (control group) and 60 patients infected with HPV and diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia of mild (LSIL, n=30) and severe (HSIL, n=30) grade. The levels of immunoregulatory factors were determined in cervical mucus and blood serum using the Pro Human Cytokine 27-plex Assay (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc., USA) on a Luminex 200 analyzer (USA). To assess differences between groups categorized by the presence of the virus, HPV type, and viral load level, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and a two-sample t-test with unequal variances were used. In LSIL, compared to the control group, opposite and significant differences were found in the levels of IL-4, IL-8, FGF, IL-1b, IL1-ra, IL-2, IL-5, IP-10, MCP-1, and PDGF-BB in both blood and cervical mucus. In HSIL, changes were observed in the levels of FGF, IL-10, IL-8, IL-17A, TNF-a, and VEGF. In the blood serum of all HPV-positive patients, regardless of the virus strain, a decrease in the levels of IL-17A, IL-2, IL-5, IL-9, and PDGF-BB, and an increase in the levels of IL-4, IL-7, IL-10, and the IL-10/IL-17A ratio were found compared to healthy women. In the cervical mucus of all virus-positive patients, compared to the HPV-negative group, elevated levels of IL-1b, VEGF, FGF, and a significant decrease in the levels of IL-8 and IP-10 were observed. The main influence on the local and systemic cytokine profile in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia is exerted by the presence of HPV infection in the body, regardless of the virus type and the level of viral load.

title_original: The influence of human papillomaviruses on the cytokine profile of blood serum and cervical mucus in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with oncogenic human papillomaviruses (HPVs) is a necessary cause of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), yet how HPV type and viral load shape local and systemic cytokine profiles in CIN remains incompletely understood. The study aimed to determine whether HPV presence, type, or viral load differentially alters cytokine factor profiles in cervical mucus and blood serum among women with CIN.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study enrolled 30 healthy women as controls and 60 HPV-infected patients with CIN, stratified into 30 with low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) and 30 with high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL).
analysis.methods: Cytokine levels in cervical mucus and blood serum were quantified using the Pro Human Cytokine 27-plex Assay on a Luminex 200 analyzer. Differences between groups were assessed with one-way ANOVA and a two-sample t-test with unequal variances to compare cytokine profiles by HPV presence, type, and viral load.
analysis.main_results: In LSIL, significant differences versus controls were observed for IL-4, IL-8, FGF, IL-1β, IL-1ra, IL-2, IL-5, IP-10, MCP-1, and PDGF-BB in both blood and cervical mucus. In HSIL, changes were noted for FGF, IL-10, IL-8, IL-17A, TNF-α, and VEGF. Across all HPV-positive patients, blood showed decreased IL-17A, IL-2, IL-5, IL-9, and PDGF-BB and increased IL-4, IL-7, IL-10, and the IL-10/IL-17A ratio; cervical mucus showed elevated IL-1β, VEGF, FGF and reduced IL-8 and IP-10.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that HPV infection itself, rather than viral type or load, is the principal driver of altered local and systemic cytokine profiles in CIN. This is the first study to directly compare paired cervical mucus and blood serum cytokine signatures across CIN grades while explicitly testing the influence of HPV presence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that cytokine profiling of blood and cervical secretions could serve as adjunct biomarkers for CIN severity and HPV-associated immune modulation, potentially informing risk stratification and monitoring strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the sample size limits subgroup analyses by HPV type or viral load. The evidence is moderate due to reliance on a single assay platform and lack of longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated whether human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, type, or viral load differentially alters cytokine profiles in cervical mucus and blood serum among women with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). It enrolled 30 healthy controls and 60 HPV-infected patients with CIN (30 LSIL, 30 HSIL), quantifying 27 cytokines using a multiplex immunoassay. Significant cytokine perturbations were observed in both compartments, with LSIL showing differences in IL-4, IL-8, FGF, IL-1β, IL-1ra, IL-2, IL-5, IP-10, MCP-1, and PDGF-BB, and HSIL showing changes in FGF, IL-10, IL-8, IL-17A, TNF-α, and VEGF. Across all HPV-positive patients, blood exhibited decreased IL-17A, IL-2, IL-5, IL-9, and PDGF-BB and increased IL-4, IL-7, IL-10, and the IL-10/IL-17A ratio, while cervical mucus showed elevated IL-1β, VEGF, FGF and reduced IL-8 and IP-10. The authors interpret HPV infection itself as the main driver of these cytokine shifts, independent of viral type or load. These findings may support cytokine profiling as adjunct biomarkers for CIN severity and HPV-associated immune modulation, though the cross-sectional design and single-assay platform limit causal inference and generalizability.

analysis_en.methods: Cytokine levels in cervical mucus and blood serum were quantified using the Pro Human Cytokine 27-plex Assay on a Luminex 200 analyzer. analysis_en.main_results: In LSIL, significant differences versus controls were observed for IL-4, IL-8, FGF, IL-1β, IL-1ra, IL-2, IL-5, IP-10, MCP-1, and PDGF-BB in both blood and cervical mucus. analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that HPV infection itself, rather than viral type or load, is the principal driver of altered local and systemic cytokine profiles in CIN. title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒对宫颈上皮内瘤变血清和宫颈粘液细胞因子谱的影响
source_body_en: To investigate the influence of different types of human papillomavirus (HPV) and the level of viral load on the profiles of cytokine factors in cervical mucus and blood serum in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Material and methods. The study included 30 healthy women (control group) and 60 patients infected with HPV and diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia of mild (LSIL, n=30) and severe (HSIL, n=30) grade. The levels of immunoregulatory factors were determined in cervical mucus and blood serum using the Pro Human Cytokine 27-plex Assay (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc., USA) on a Luminex 200 analyzer (USA). To assess differences between groups categorized by the presence of the virus, HPV type, and viral load level, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and a two-sample t-test with unequal variances were used. In LSIL, compared to the control group, opposite and significant differences were found in the levels of IL-4, IL-8, FGF, IL-1b, IL1-ra, IL-2, IL-5, IP-10, MCP-1, and PDGF-BB in both blood and cervical mucus. In HSIL, changes were observed in the levels of FGF, IL-10, IL-8, IL-17A, TNF-a, and VEGF. In the blood serum of all HPV-positive patients, regardless of the virus strain, a decrease in the levels of IL-17A, IL-2, IL-5, IL-9, and PDGF-BB, and an increase in the levels of IL-4, IL-7, IL-10, and the IL-10/IL-17A ratio were found compared to healthy women. In the cervical mucus of all virus-positive patients, compared to the HPV-negative group, elevated levels of IL-1b, VEGF, FGF, and a significant decrease in the levels of IL-8 and IP-10 were observed. The main influence on the local and systemic cytokine profile in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia is exerted by the presence of HPV infection in the body, regardless of the virus type and the level of viral load.

title: HPV Vaccination as Treatment for Cutaneous Diseases: Beyond Prevention.
abstract: Abstract Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes cutaneous diseases ranging from common warts to cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). Although HPV vaccines were licensed to prevent anogenital infections, they are increasingly used off-label to treat established HPV-associated cutaneous lesions. This narrative review evaluates therapeutic HPV vaccination for recalcitrant warts, non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC), and immunocompromised populations. The only large randomized controlled trial showed no benefit for anogenital warts, and all positive evidence derives from low-quality studies with small sample sizes and heterogeneous designs. Publication bias is likely. Key challenges include lack of coverage for oncogenic β-HPV subtypes and the off-label nature of therapy. Future directions require next-generation vaccines targeting cutaneous HPV types and well-designed trials. Pending robust data, therapeutic HPV vaccination should remain strictly investigational and should be offered only within the context of clinical research or after explicit shared decision-making, rather than as a routine clinical option.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review that synthesizes published evidence on therapeutic HPV vaccination for cutaneous diseases. The review does not report systematic search dates, eligibility criteria, or included-study counts, and it does not perform meta-analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that there is no benefit of HPV vaccination for anogenital warts based on the only large randomized controlled trial, and all positive evidence for therapeutic use derives from low-quality studies with small sample sizes and heterogeneous designs. Publication bias is likely.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Key gaps include the lack of coverage of oncogenic β-HPV subtypes in current vaccines and the absence of high-quality evidence supporting therapeutic efficacy for cutaneous HPV-associated diseases. Heterogeneity in study designs and small sample sizes limit firm conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends that therapeutic HPV vaccination should remain investigational and offered only within clinical research or after shared decision-making, rather than as routine practice, pending robust data from well-designed trials targeting cutaneous HPV types.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review evaluates the therapeutic use of HPV vaccines for established cutaneous diseases, including recalcitrant warts and non-melanoma skin cancer. It finds no benefit for anogenital warts from the only large randomized controlled trial and identifies all positive evidence as deriving from low-quality, heterogeneous studies with likely publication bias. The review highlights gaps in coverage for oncogenic β-HPV subtypes and emphasizes the need for next-generation vaccines and well-designed trials. Pending robust evidence, therapeutic HPV vaccination should remain investigational and restricted to clinical research or shared decision-making contexts.

title_zh: HPV 疫苗接种 和 治疗 用于皮肤疾病:无法预防。
source_body_en: Abstract Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes cutaneous diseases ranging from common warts to cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). Although HPV vaccines were licensed to prevent anogenital infections, they are increasingly used off-label to treat established HPV-associated cutaneous lesions. This narrative review evaluates therapeutic HPV vaccination for recalcitrant warts, non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC), and immunocompromised populations. The only large randomized controlled trial showed no benefit for anogenital warts, and all positive evidence derives from low-quality studies with small sample sizes and heterogeneous designs. Publication bias is likely. Key challenges include lack of coverage for oncogenic β-HPV subtypes and the off-label nature of therapy. Future directions require next-generation vaccines targeting cutaneous HPV types and well-designed trials. Pending robust data, therapeutic HPV vaccination should remain strictly investigational and should be offered only within the context of clinical research or after explicit shared decision-making, rather than as a routine clinical option.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 可引起从寻常疣到皮肤鳞状细胞癌 (cSCC) 等各种皮肤疾病。尽管 HPV 疫苗 被许可用于预防肛门生殖器感染,但它们越来越多地用于治疗已确定的 HPV 相关皮肤病变。这篇叙述性综述评估了 HPV 疫苗接种 对顽固性疣、非黑色素瘤皮肤癌 (NMSC) 和免疫功能低下人群的治疗作用。唯一的大型随机对照试验显示对肛门生殖器疣没有任何益处,所有积极证据都来自小样本和异质设计的低质量研究。发表偏见是可能的。主要挑战包括缺乏对致癌 β-HPV 亚型的覆盖以及治疗的标签外性质。未来的方向需要针对皮肤 HPV 类型的下一代 疫苗 和精心设计的试验。在等待可靠的数据之前,治疗性 HPV 疫苗接种 应保持严格的研究状态,并且仅应在临床研究背景下或在明确的共同决策后提供,而不是作为常规临床选择。

title: Oncoviruses at the Crossroads of Ageing and Cancer: Molecular Mechanisms and Key Signalling Pathways.
abstract: Oncoviruses are responsible for a substantial fraction of human cancers and have emerged as critical modulators of host cellular pathways that also govern ageing. The convergence of viral oncogenesis, ageing, and cancer reflects shared molecular mechanisms, including genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence indicates that oncoviruses such as human papillomavirus, Epstein-Barr virus, hepatitis B and C viruses, and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus actively reprogramme host signalling networks to promote persistent infection, immune evasion, and malignant transformation. This review synthesises current knowledge on how oncoviruses intersect with key hallmarks of ageing and cancer, with particular emphasis on the signalling pathways that bridge these processes. Central pathways, including p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, are frequently targeted by viral proteins, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions not only facilitate tumourigenesis but also accelerate ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, such as immunosenescence and inflammaging. Furthermore, we discuss how virus-induced modulation of the tumour microenvironment and host immune responses contributes to the dynamic interplay between ageing and cancer. Understanding these interconnected pathways provides valuable insights into the dual role of oncoviruses as drivers of both age-related decline and cancer development. Elucidating these mechanisms may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations.

title_zh: 处于衰老和癌症十字路口的肿瘤病毒:分子机制和关键信号通路。
source_body_en: Oncoviruses are responsible for a substantial fraction of human cancers and have emerged as critical modulators of host cellular pathways that also govern ageing. The convergence of viral oncogenesis, ageing, and cancer reflects shared molecular mechanisms, including genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence indicates that oncoviruses such as human papillomavirus, Epstein-Barr virus, hepatitis B and C viruses, and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus actively reprogramme host signalling networks to promote persistent infection, immune evasion, and malignant transformation. This review synthesises current knowledge on how oncoviruses intersect with key hallmarks of ageing and cancer, with particular emphasis on the signalling pathways that bridge these processes. Central pathways, including p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, are frequently targeted by viral proteins, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions not only facilitate tumourigenesis but also accelerate ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, such as immunosenescence and inflammaging. Furthermore, we discuss how virus-induced modulation of the tumour microenvironment and host immune responses contributes to the dynamic interplay between ageing and cancer. Understanding these interconnected pathways provides valuable insights into the dual role of oncoviruses as drivers of both age-related decline and cancer development. Elucidating these mechanisms may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤病毒是导致大部分人类癌症的原因,并且已成为 宿主 细胞途径的关键调节剂,该途径也控制着衰老。病毒肿瘤发生、衰老和癌症的融合反映了共同的分子机制,包括基因组不稳定性、表观遗传改变、端粒磨损和慢性炎症。越来越多的证据表明,人乳头瘤病毒、Epstein-Barr病毒、乙型和丙型肝炎病毒以及卡波西肉瘤相关疱疹病毒等肿瘤病毒会主动重编程宿主信号网络,以促进持续感染、免疫逃避和恶性转化。这篇综述综合了目前关于肿瘤病毒如何与衰老和癌症的关键特征相交叉的知识,特别强调了桥接这些过程的信号通路。包括 p53、mTOR、NF-κB、PI3K/AKT 和 Wnt/β-catenin 在内的中央通路经常成为病毒蛋白的目标,导致细胞存活、增殖和衰老失调。这些相互作用不仅促进肿瘤发生,而且加速与衰老相关的细胞功能障碍,例如免疫衰老和炎症。此外,我们讨论了病毒诱导的肿瘤微环境调节和 宿主 免疫应答 如何促进衰老与癌症之间的动态相互作用。了解这些相互关联的途径可以为了解肿瘤病毒作为与年龄相关的衰退和癌症发展的驱动因素的双重作用提供有价值的见解。阐明这些机制可能会揭示预防和治疗老龄化人群中与病毒相关的恶性肿瘤的新治疗靶点和策略。

title: HPV Self-Collection Experience in US Hispanic/Latinx Women Using a Device Designed for at-Home Collection.
abstract: Background Cervical cancer is a preventable disease, and reaching populations who are under-screened and/or at highest risk is essential to the goal of disease elimination. Hispanic women in the US have a disproportionately higher incidence rate than non-Hispanic women. Objective Post hoc analysis of the SELF-CERV study of the unique experience and preferences among Hispanic compared to non-Hispanic participants with the goal of facilitating and improving screening and follow-up in more vulnerable populations. Methods Women 25 to 65 years who were enrolled performed self-collection (SC) of vaginal samples for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing using a unique device in a simulated at-home environment. For method comparison, a clinician-collected (CC) sample was obtained. Participants also completed usability and screening preference surveys. Results A total of 609 participants were consented and 603 used the SC device. Of the 603 SC users, 115 (19.1%) identified themselves as Hispanic/Latinx. Compared to non-Hispanic women, Hispanic women, had significantly lower annual income (p < .001), a lower percentage of private insurance with more uninsured (p < .001) and lower levels of education (p < .001). There was no significant difference between Hispanic and non-Hispanic women in understanding the purpose of cervical cancer screening. No difference was noted in delaying screening, although English Not Primary speaking Hispanic women were somewhat more likely to delay (p = 0.22). Financial barriers were observed to be more of an impediment to Hispanic women compared to non-Hispanic women (p = 0.016). Negative experiences with in-clinic speculum exams were similar; however, Hispanic women (78%) expressed a significantly higher endorsement of SC than non-Hispanic women (62%), (p = 0.001). Both populations reported that they would be more likely to stay up to date with cervical cancer screening with the at-home SC device, but non-Hispanic women to a significantly lesser degree (p = 0.002). In terms of assessing utility of telemedicine in screening, both populations reported similar engagement in healthcare activities, willingness to try new technology and current use of smartphones. Hispanic and non-Hispanic women were both nearly equally divided as to their preference for in-clinic visits vs telehealth. Conclusions Facilitating screening uptake is especially critical for Hispanic women, who bear a disproportionate burden of cervical cancer diagnoses and mortality while facing more obstacles to screening than non-Hispanic women. A clinically validated and accessible at-home SC alternative holds potential for meaningful impact and improved health outcomes within this community.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically high-risk HPV types, in the context of cervical cancer prevention among US Hispanic/Latinx women. The central question focuses on the acceptability, usability, and barriers to at-home self-collection (SC) of vaginal samples for hrHPV testing compared to clinician-collected (CC) samples, and how these factors differ between Hispanic and non-Hispanic women.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review reports a post hoc analysis of the SELF-CERV study, which enrolled women aged 25 to 65 years to perform self-collection of vaginal samples for hrHPV testing using a unique device in a simulated at-home environment. A clinician-collected sample was obtained for method comparison. Participants completed usability and screening preference surveys. The study included 609 consented participants, with 603 using the SC device.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Hispanic women reported significantly lower annual income, lower private insurance coverage, higher uninsured rates, and lower education levels compared to non-Hispanic women. Financial barriers were more pronounced for Hispanic women. Hispanic women expressed a significantly higher endorsement of SC (78%) than non-Hispanic women (62%), and both groups reported a higher likelihood of staying up to date with screening using the at-home SC device, though non-Hispanic women to a lesser degree.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report significant differences in understanding the purpose of cervical cancer screening or delaying screening between Hispanic and non-Hispanic women, though English-not-primary-speaking Hispanic women were somewhat more likely to delay screening (p = 0.22). The evidence does not report long-term clinical outcomes or diagnostic accuracy of the SC device compared to CC sampling.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need to address financial barriers and improve access to at-home SC devices to facilitate screening uptake among Hispanic women, who face disproportionate cervical cancer burden. Further research is needed to validate the clinical utility and diagnostic performance of the SC device in real-world settings and to evaluate its impact on reducing disparities in cervical cancer screening and outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzes the acceptability and usability of at-home self-collection (SC) for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing among US Hispanic/Latinx women compared to clinician-collected (CC) samples. Hispanic women, who bear a disproportionate burden of cervical cancer, reported greater financial barriers and higher endorsement of SC (78%) than non-Hispanic women (62%). Both groups favored at-home SC for maintaining screening adherence, though non-Hispanic women were less enthusiastic. The study underscores the potential of SC to improve screening uptake in underserved populations but lacks evidence on long-term clinical outcomes or diagnostic accuracy.

title_zh: 美国西班牙裔/拉丁裔女性使用专为家庭收集而设计的设备进行 HPV 自我收集的经验。
source_body_en: Background Cervical cancer is a preventable disease, and reaching populations who are under-screened and/or at highest risk is essential to the goal of disease elimination. Hispanic women in the US have a disproportionately higher incidence rate than non-Hispanic women. Objective Post hoc analysis of the SELF-CERV study of the unique experience and preferences among Hispanic compared to non-Hispanic participants with the goal of facilitating and improving screening and follow-up in more vulnerable populations. Methods Women 25 to 65 years who were enrolled performed self-collection (SC) of vaginal samples for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing using a unique device in a simulated at-home environment. For method comparison, a clinician-collected (CC) sample was obtained. Participants also completed usability and screening preference surveys. Results A total of 609 participants were consented and 603 used the SC device. Of the 603 SC users, 115 (19.1%) identified themselves as Hispanic/Latinx. Compared to non-Hispanic women, Hispanic women, had significantly lower annual income (p < .001), a lower percentage of private insurance with more uninsured (p < .001) and lower levels of education (p < .001). There was no significant difference between Hispanic and non-Hispanic women in understanding the purpose of cervical cancer screening. No difference was noted in delaying screening, although English Not Primary speaking Hispanic women were somewhat more likely to delay (p = 0.22). Financial barriers were observed to be more of an impediment to Hispanic women compared to non-Hispanic women (p = 0.016). Negative experiences with in-clinic speculum exams were similar; however, Hispanic women (78%) expressed a significantly higher endorsement of SC than non-Hispanic women (62%), (p = 0.001). Both populations reported that they would be more likely to stay up to date with cervical cancer screening with the at-home SC device, but non-Hispanic women to a significantly lesser degree (p = 0.002). In terms of assessing utility of telemedicine in screening, both populations reported similar engagement in healthcare activities, willingness to try new technology and current use of smartphones. Hispanic and non-Hispanic women were both nearly equally divided as to their preference for in-clinic visits vs telehealth. Conclusions Facilitating screening uptake is especially critical for Hispanic women, who bear a disproportionate burden of cervical cancer diagnoses and mortality while facing more obstacles to screening than non-Hispanic women. A clinically validated and accessible at-home SC alternative holds potential for meaningful impact and improved health outcomes within this community.
abstract_zh: 背景 宫颈癌 是一种可预防的疾病,覆盖筛查不足和/或风险最高的人群对于消除疾病的目标至关重要。美国的西班牙裔女性的 发病率 率比非西班牙裔女性高得不成比例。客观对 SELF-CERV 研究进行事后分析,了解西班牙裔参与者与非西班牙裔参与者相比的独特经历和偏好,目的是促进和改善对更弱势群体的筛查和随访。方法 入组的 25 至 65 岁女性在模拟家庭环境中使用独特的设备自行采集 (SC) 阴道样本,进行高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 检测。为了进行方法比较,获得了临床医生收集的 (CC) 样本。参与者还完成了可用性和筛选偏好调查。结果 共有 609 名参与者获得同意,其中 603 人使用了 SC 设备。在 603 名 SC 用户中,115 名 (19.1%) 认为自己是西班牙裔/拉丁裔。与非西班牙裔女性相比,西班牙裔女性的年收入显着较低 (p < .001),私人保险比例较低,未投保的人数较多 (p < .001),教育水平较低 (p < .001)。西班牙裔和非西班牙裔女性对 宫颈癌 筛查目的的理解没有显着差异。尽管非主要讲英语的西班牙裔女性更有可能推迟筛查,但在推迟筛查方面没有发现差异(p = 0.22)。据观察,与非西班牙裔女性相比,经济障碍对西班牙裔女性的影响更大(p = 0.016)。诊所内窥镜检查的负面经历是相似的;然而,西班牙裔女性 (78%) 对 SC 的支持率明显高于非西班牙裔女性 (62%) (p = 0.001)。两个人群都报告称,她们更有可能通过家用 SC 设备了解最新的 宫颈癌 筛查,但非西班牙裔女性的程度明显较低 (p = 0.002)。在评估远程医疗在筛查中的效用方面,两个人群都报告了相似的医疗保健活动参与度、尝试新技术的意愿以及当前智能手​​机的使用情况。西班牙裔和非西班牙裔女性对于门诊就诊与远程医疗的偏好几乎持平。结论 促进筛查对于西班牙裔女性尤其重要,她们承担着不成比例的 宫颈癌 诊断和 死亡率 负担,同时比非西班牙裔女性面临更多筛查障碍。经过临床验证且易于使用的家庭 SC 替代方案有可能对该社区产生有意义的影响并改善健康结果。

title: HPV-associated Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An Imaging Framework for AJCC Version 9 TNM Staging
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, and staging directly impacts treatment. The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) and Union for International Cancer Control version 9 TNM staging system incorporates unequivocal imaging-detected and/or clinically detected extranodal extension (iENE) into clinical nodal staging and definitive pathologic extranodal extension into pathologic nodal staging. Additionally, it provides more explicit anatomic definitions for advanced local disease (clinical T4) while maintaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. Radiologists play a central role in the multidisciplinary team by evaluating endophytic tumor extent, regional nodal disease and iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET. This article reviews clinically relevant oropharyngeal anatomy and proposes a practical radiologic approach to assigning T, N, and M categories in HPV-associated OPSCC. It emphasizes cautious interpretation of iENE because of interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, with further high-grade evidence needed to establish its consistently reproducible, incremental prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier. It also highlights multidisciplinary factors that guide selection of surgical resection versus nonsurgical therapy. Posttreatment evaluation is discussed in the context of blood-based biomarkers such as tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA. The goal of this article is to provide a practical, staging-focused imaging framework for evaluation of HPV-associated OPSCC. Keywords: CT, MR Imaging, Head/Neck, Neck, Pharynx, Surgery, Human Papillomavirus, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Oropharynx, Transoral Robotic Surgery, Oropharyngeal Carcinoma, TTMV HPV DNA © RSNA, 2026.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), focusing on the role of imaging in TNM staging under the AJCC version 9 system, specifically addressing how staging impacts treatment decisions for HPV-positive disease.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The article is a narrative review that outlines the AJCC version 9 TNM staging system's modifications for HPV-associated OPSCC, including the incorporation of imaging-detected extranodal extension (iENE) and updated anatomic definitions for advanced local disease, while emphasizing the radiologist's role in multidisciplinary evaluation.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HPV-associated OPSCC is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, with staging directly influencing treatment choices; it also highlights the central role of radiologists in assessing tumor extent, nodal disease, iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance in interpreting iENE, emphasizing the need for high-grade evidence to establish its consistently reproducible prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes the need for further high-grade evidence to validate the prognostic utility of iENE and calls for cautious interpretation in clinical practice, while also discussing multidisciplinary factors guiding treatment selection and posttreatment evaluation using blood-based biomarkers such as tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides an imaging-focused framework for staging HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) under the AJCC version 9 TNM system. It highlights the distinct biological and prognostic profile of HPV-positive OPSCC compared to HPV-negative disease, with staging directly influencing treatment decisions. The review emphasizes the radiologist's central role in evaluating tumor extent, nodal disease, imaging-detected extranodal extension (iENE), and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET. Key controversies include the variability and diagnostic limitations of iENE interpretation, underscoring the need for high-grade evidence to confirm its prognostic value. Practical implications include the necessity for cautious iENE assessment in clinical practice, the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration in treatment selection, and the potential of blood-based biomarkers like tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA for posttreatment evaluation.

title_zh: HPV 相关口咽鳞状细胞癌:AJCC 第 9 版 TNM 分期的影像框架
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, and staging directly impacts treatment. The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) and Union for International Cancer Control version 9 TNM staging system incorporates unequivocal imaging-detected and/or clinically detected extranodal extension (iENE) into clinical nodal staging and definitive pathologic extranodal extension into pathologic nodal staging. Additionally, it provides more explicit anatomic definitions for advanced local disease (clinical T4) while maintaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. Radiologists play a central role in the multidisciplinary team by evaluating endophytic tumor extent, regional nodal disease and iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET. This article reviews clinically relevant oropharyngeal anatomy and proposes a practical radiologic approach to assigning T, N, and M categories in HPV-associated OPSCC. It emphasizes cautious interpretation of iENE because of interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, with further high-grade evidence needed to establish its consistently reproducible, incremental prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier. It also highlights multidisciplinary factors that guide selection of surgical resection versus nonsurgical therapy. Posttreatment evaluation is discussed in the context of blood-based biomarkers such as tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA. The goal of this article is to provide a practical, staging-focused imaging framework for evaluation of HPV-associated OPSCC. title: The State-of-the Art of Personalized Vaccines for Non-Communicable Diseases: A Narrative Review
abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including cancer, cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, autoimmune, and allergic diseases, account for a significant amount of global morbidity and mortality. Chronic viral infections have not been recognized as NCDs, despite the availability of several therapeutic vaccination strategies against oncogenic viruses, such as the hepatitis B virus (HBV) and the human papillomavirus (HPV). Indeed, chronic viral infection leads to the development and progression of malignancies directly linked to the viruses. These considerations support a connection between NCDs, infectious diseases, and therapeutic vaccination. Recent advances in technology have paved the way to the use of vaccines beyond the prevention of infectious diseases, heralding innovative therapeutic and preventative strategies for a variety of chronic NCDs. Here we will review the state of the art of personalized vaccine strategies for NCDs, with an emphasis on the diverse technological platforms used to develop them, including mRNA and DNA vaccines, viral vectors, dendritic cell-based vaccines, nanoparticle delivery systems, and next-generation adjuvants. The review intends to make the case for personalized and antigen-specific vaccination strategies as a compelling option for precision immunotherapy primarily in oncology, where neoantigen-based vaccines are being developed. In addition, we will also review tolerogenic vaccination strategies, vaccination strategies targeting pathological proteins and pathways in neurodegenerative and cardiovascular diseases, and vaccine-based treatment of chronic viral infections. Current evidence about vaccines suggests that several ways are available to induce an immune response or create tolerance to a disease, and possibly altering its course instead of simply controlling the symptoms. However, many challenges are still to be overcome, including disease variability, how to identify appropriate target antigens, the complexity of manufacturing process, long-term safety, and integration with already established treatments. By virtue of the convergence of multiple fields—immunology, genomics, bioinformatics, and new delivery systems—precision vaccinology is gaining momentum. Thus, it is envisaged that personalized vaccines will be an increasingly essential component of future preventive and therapeutic approaches for non-communicable diseases.

title: Modelling the Effects of Smoking Behavior on Male-to-Male HPV Transmission and Anal Cancer Progression
abstract: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection among men who have sex with men (MSM) has become a significant public health concern, particularly in countries where male vaccination is unavailable. Given the high susceptibility of MSM to HPV and anal cancer, and the unavailability of HPV vaccination for males in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), there is a need to identify alternative interventions for reducing disease transmission and burden in this population. The novel mathematical model presented in this article couples smoking behavior dynamics with HPV transmission and anal cancer progression among MSM. Smoking reduction is introduced as an intervention to assess its effects on disease transmission and burden. The basic reproduction number (R 0 ) is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and a global sensitivity analysis is performed using partial rank correlation coefficients (PRCC) to identify the influence of model parameters on RR 0 . Further, the theoretical analysis of the model reveals a backward bifurcation, implying that RR 0 < 1 is necessary but not sufficient to eradicate the disease. The study finds that smoking reduction among MSM reduces HPV infection and anal cancer burden relative to baseline projections without intervention. The joint effect of smoking reduction and vaccination shows that the critical vaccination coverage needed to achieve RR 0 <1 decreases as the level of smoking reduction increases. A similar outcome is observed for contact reduction. These findings highlight the importance of concurrent interventions, which can significantly curtail the spread of HPV and reduce disease burden in both the high-risk group and the general population.

title_zh: 模拟吸烟行为对男性到男性 HPV 传播 和肛门癌进展的影响
source_body_en: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection among men who have sex with men (MSM) has become a significant public health concern, particularly in countries where male vaccination is unavailable. The novel mathematical model presented in this article couples smoking behavior dynamics with HPV transmission and anal cancer progression among MSM. Smoking reduction is introduced as an intervention to assess its effects on disease transmission and burden. The basic reproduction number (R 0 ) is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and a global sensitivity analysis is performed using partial rank correlation coefficients (PRCC) to identify the influence of model parameters on RR 0 . Further, the theoretical analysis of the model reveals a backward bifurcation, implying that RR 0 < 1 is necessary but not sufficient to eradicate the disease. The study finds that smoking reduction among MSM reduces HPV infection and anal cancer burden relative to baseline projections without intervention. The joint effect of smoking reduction and vaccination shows that the critical vaccination coverage needed to achieve RR 0 <1 decreases as the level of smoking reduction increases. A similar outcome is observed for contact reduction. These findings highlight the importance of concurrent interventions, which can significantly curtail the spread of HPV and reduce disease burden in both the high-risk group and the general population.
abstract_zh: 男男性行为者 (MSM) 中的 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染已成为一个重大的公共卫生问题,特别是在无法获得男性 疫苗接种 的国家。鉴于 MSM 对 HPV 和肛门癌的高度易感性,以及低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC) 男性无法获得 HPV 传播,因此需要确定替代干预措施来减少该人群的疾病 传播 和负担。本文提出的新颖数学模型将吸烟行为动态与 HPV 传播 和 MSM 中肛门癌的进展联系起来。减少吸烟作为一项干预措施被引入,以评估其对疾病 传播 和负担的影响。采用下一代矩阵法推导基本再生数(R 0 ),并利用偏秩相关系数(PRCC)进行全局敏感性分析,以确定模型参数对RR 0 的影响。此外,模型的理论分析揭示了后向分歧,这意味着 RR 0 < 1 对于根除疾病是必要的,但不足以消除。研究发现,相对于没有干预的基线预测,MSM 中吸烟的减少可以减少 HPV 感染和肛门癌负担。减少吸烟和疫苗接种的联合效应表明,随着吸烟减少水平的增加,实现RR 0 <1所需的临界疫苗接种覆盖率降低。减少接触也观察到类似的结果。这些发现强调了同时干预措施的重要性,这可以显着减少 HPV 的传播并减轻高危人群和普通人群的疾病负担。

title: First-in-Human, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Phase 1 Study to Assess in Healthy Adults the Safety and Immunogenicity of Intramuscularly Administered AAVLP-HPV Vaccine
abstract: Abstract Seeking a simple vaccine to protect against all cancer-associated human papillomaviruses (HPV), L2 residues 17-36 of both HPV16 and HPV31 displayed on the surface of an Adeno-Associated Virus-Like Particle (AAVLP-HPV) was developed. Here, a phase 1 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical study has been conducted in 20 male and female subjects at a single dose level (20μg) without an adjuvant. AAVLP-HPV vaccine administration was safe and well tolerated. Repeat vaccination with AAVLP-HPV elicited L2-specific neutralizing antibodies of modest titer in serum. Antibodies cross-reactive with L2 of diverse HPV types were detected, but responses were weak in most vaccinees. We conclude that while AAVLP-HPV vaccination is well tolerated, an adjuvant is likely needed to consistently elicit durable and broadly neutralizing responses. One sentence summary Vaccination with AAVLP-HPV is safe and immunogenic in healthy adults. Funding The study was funded by 2A Pharma AB. MM and RBSR were funded by service contracts from 2A Pharma AB. RBSR and JA were funded by Public Health Service (grants.nih.gov) grant P50 CA098252.

title: Clinical Impact of HPV Self-Sampling and Molecular Biomarkers on Cervical Cancer Screening and Triage: “The Times They Are A-Changin’”—A Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a necessary but insufficient cause of cervical cancer (CC) and reflects a long-standing host–virus equilibrium shaped by immune control, viral persistence, and latency. The transition from cytology-based screening to primary high-risk HPV testing has substantially improved early detection of cervical precancerous lesions but has also introduced new clinical challenges related to fluctuating test results, overdiagnosis, overtreatment, and patient anxiety, whose magnitude may vary across countries depending on screening organization and access to prevention services. This narrative review provides a clinically oriented overview of HPV-based CC screening in the context of evolving knowledge on HPV natural history, persistence, and immune interaction, and discusses the implications for the interpretation of test results and risk stratification. New emerging screening and triage approaches, including molecular biomarkers, exosome-based biomarkers, and artificial-intelligence-supported risk assessment, are reshaping CC prevention strategies by enabling more precise identification of women at risk for clinically significant disease. These tools may be particularly relevant in self-sampling-based screening pathways, where molecular triage strategies can reduce the need for additional clinician-collected samples and improve management of HPV-positive women. At the same time, improved understanding of viral latency and host-related determinants of progression supports a shift from binary test interpretation toward longitudinal and individualized risk assessment. Integrating biological insight with technological innovation may facilitate personalized screening strategies that maintain high sensitivity while reducing unnecessary interventions. An evolutionary-informed and risk-adapted approach to HPV-related disease management is essential to optimize prevention outcomes and preserve the benefits of population-based screening programs.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,转向基于 HPV 的筛查改善了宫颈癌前病变的早期检测,但也带来了检测结果波动、过度诊断和过度治疗等挑战。由于 HPV 感染的复杂性及其与 宿主 免疫系统的相互作用,它强调需要进行纵向和个体化的风险评估。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于 HPV 检测结果的解释存在争议,特别是在结果波动和过度诊断风险的背景下。该综述强调需要更好地了解影响疾病进展的病毒潜伏期和 宿主 相关因素,以及整合分子生物标志物和人工智能以进行更精确的风险评估。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该评论表明,将生物学见解与分子生物标志物和人工智能等技术创新相结合,可以改善个性化筛查策略。它还强调了制定风险适应方法来管理 HPV 相关疾病的重要性,以优化预防结果并保持基于人群的筛查计划的有效性。

abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染是 宫颈癌 (CC) 的必要但不充分的原因,反映了由免疫控制、病毒持久性和潜伏期形成的长期 宿主 病毒平衡。从基于细胞学的筛查到初级 高危型HPV 检测的转变极大地改善了宫颈癌前病变的早期发现,但也带来了与检测结果波动、过度诊断、过度治疗和患者焦虑相关的新的临床挑战,其程度可能因国家而异,具体取决于筛查组织和预防服务的获取情况。这篇叙述性综述在 HPV 自然史、持久性和免疫相互作用的知识不断发展的背景下,对基于 HPV 的 CC 筛查进行了临床导向的概述,并讨论了对检测结果和风险分层解释的影响。新出现的筛查和分诊方法,包括分子生物标志物、基于外泌体的生物标志物和人工智能支持的风险评估,正在重塑 CC 预防策略,能够更准确地识别面临临床重大疾病风险的女性。这些工具可能与基于自我采样的筛查途径特别相关,其中分子分类策略可以减少对临床医生收集额外样本的需求,并改善对 HPV 阳性女性的管理。与此同时,对病毒潜伏期和 宿主 相关进展决定因素的更好理解支持从二元测试解释向纵向和个体化风险评估的转变。将生物学洞察力与技术创新相结合可能有助于个性化筛查策略,保持高灵敏度,同时减少不必要的干预。HPV 相关疾病管理的进化信息和风险适应方法对于优化预防结果和保持基于人群的筛查计划的益处至关重要。

title: Deciphering the Molecular Landscape of Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Anal Canal: From Biology to Precision Oncology
abstract: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal (SCAC) is a rare malignancy whose incidence has been steadily increasing worldwide. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV16 and HPV18 genotypes, is the main etiological factor and plays a central role in tumor development. While combined chemoradiotherapy remains the standard treatment for localized disease and achieves high rates of tumor control, a considerable proportion of patients experience recurrence or present with advanced disease. For the latter, therapeutic options remain limited. Over the last decade, advances in genomic profiling have significantly expanded our understanding of SCAC biology. Recurrent alterations affecting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, especially PIK3CA mutations, have emerged as the most common molecular events, particularly in HPV-positive tumors. Additional alterations involve receptor tyrosine kinase signaling, chromatin remodeling genes, DNA damage response pathways, and components of the MAPK cascade. Moreover, HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumors display distinct molecular features with important prognostic implications. Immunotherapy has recently become an important component of treatment for advanced SCAC, although reliable predictive biomarkers are still lacking. This review summarizes the current evidence on the molecular landscape of SCAC, discusses emerging prognostic and predictive biomarkers, and highlights potential opportunities for the development of more personalized therapeutic strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注肛管鳞状细胞癌 (SCAC) 的分子概况,重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 的作用,特别是 高危型HPV 类型,例如 HPV16 和 HPV18。核心问题是了解 SCAC 发生和进展的分子机制,并探索这些发现对精准肿瘤学的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 SCAC 分子特征现有文献的叙述性综合,重点关注 HPV 相关机制。它不报告特定的数据库、搜索日期或荟萃分析方法。证据来自该领域的一般观察和发现,没有明确提及研究选择标准或定量分析。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述认为,高危型HPV,尤其是HPV16和HPV18的持续感染是SCAC的主要病因。它强调,PI3K/AKT/mTOR 通路的反复改变,特别是 PIK3CA 突变,是 HPV 阳性肿瘤中最常见的分子事件。此外,HPV 阳性和 HPV 阴性肿瘤表现出不同的分子特征,具有重要的预后意义。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出,虽然联合放化疗是局部 SCAC 的标准 治疗,但相当一部分患者会出现复发或出现晚期疾病。它还提到晚期疾病的治疗选择仍然有限。此外,该综述还发现,晚期 SCAC 免疫治疗缺乏可靠的预测生物标志物。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要进一步研究 SCAC 的分子机制,特别是在 HPV 阳性肿瘤中,以开发更个性化的治疗策略。它还强调了识别免疫治疗的可靠预测生物标志物以及改进 监测 和 HPV 相关癌症的诊断方法的重要性。

abstract_zh: 肛管鳞状细胞癌(SCAC)是一种罕见的恶性肿瘤,其发病率在全球范围内一直在稳步增长。高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV),特别是HPV16和HPV18基因型的持续感染,是主要的病因,在肿瘤的发生发展中发挥着核心作用。虽然联合放化疗仍然是局部疾病的标准 治疗 并实现了较高的肿瘤控制率,但相当一部分患者出现复发或出现晚期疾病。对于后者,治疗选择仍然有限。在过去的十年中,基因组分析的进步极大地扩展了我们对 SCAC 生物学的理解。影响 PI3K/AKT/mTOR 通路的反复改变,尤其是 PIK3CA 突变,已成为最常见的分子事件,特别是在 HPV 阳性肿瘤中。其他改变涉及受体酪氨酸激酶信号传导、染色质重塑基因、DNA 损伤反应途径和 MAPK 级联的组成部分。此外,HPV 阳性和 HPV 阴性肿瘤表现出不同的分子特征,具有重要的预后意义。尽管仍然缺乏可靠的预测生物标志物,但免疫疗法最近已成为 治疗 治疗晚期 SCAC 的重要组成部分。这篇综述总结了 SCAC 分子格局的当前证据,讨论了新兴的预后和预测生物标志物,并强调了开发更个性化治疗策略的潜在机会。

title: Research progress on the association between vaginal Lactobacillus iners and cervical cancer
abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk Human Papillomavirus (hrHPV) is the central etiological factor in cervical cancer, while the host vaginal microenvironment plays a critical role in disease progression. Lactobacillus iners is one of the most widely distributed lactobacilli in the vagina. Because of its unique biological features, including exclusive production of L-lactic acid and a small genome, it occupies a transitional state within the vaginal ecosystem. Recent studies have shown that Lactobacillus iners (L. iners) plays dual and paradoxical roles in cervical carcinogenesis and progression. In the vaginal microenvironment, L. iners is associated with persistent hrHPV infection and an increased risk of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) progression; its protective effects are limited and often coexist with unfavorable inflammatory states. In contrast, within the tumor microenvironment, intratumoral colonization by L. iners can markedly increase L-lactate production, induce chemoradiotherapy resistance in tumor cells, and serve as an independent risk factor for poor prognosis. This review systematically summarizes the biological characteristics of L. iners, its roles and mechanisms in cervical cancer initiation, progression, and treatment resistance, and its translational value as a novel biomarker and potential therapeutic target. Current controversies, limitations, and future directions are also discussed.
journal: Journal of clinical technology and theory.

title: Community-Identified Barriers and Strategies for Improving HPV Vaccination in South Texas
abstract: Bexar County is a South Texas county with low human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates, which hinders efforts to prevent HPV-related cancers. We conducted a community assessment from the perspective of community members who administer social/health services and/or coalitions in Bexar County. We aimed to assess perceived barriers and possible community solutions to HPV vaccination in Bexar County. Data were collected using an online quantitative survey measuring knowledge and attitudes toward HPV vaccination based on the Increasing Vaccination Model, as well as perceived barriers to HPV vaccination and potential solutions to improve vaccination. Participants included persons administering social/health services/part of coalitions in Bexar County from January to March 2025 ( N = 45). Descriptive statistics were estimated. Most participants strongly agreed that HPV vaccination rates could be improved and that it was very important for 9- to 26-year-olds to get vaccinated for HPV. Primary barriers at the organizational level were competing health priorities, lack of provider knowledge/training, language barriers, and patient lack of awareness. Participants were asked to consider what community-level strategies could be deployed to increase HPV vaccination; the highest rated were mobile vaccination, public awareness campaigns, and financing for the vaccine. There is a strong community interest in improving HPV vaccination in Bexar County. Developing a multi-component intervention that addresses direct access issues, coupled with provider recommendations, could surmount the reported barriers to HPV vaccination in this community.

title_zh: 德克萨斯州南部社区确定的改善 HPV 疫苗接种 的障碍和策略
source_body_en: Bexar County is a South Texas county with low human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates, which hinders efforts to prevent HPV-related cancers. We conducted a community assessment from the perspective of community members who administer social/health services and/or coalitions in Bexar County. We aimed to assess perceived barriers and possible community solutions to HPV vaccination in Bexar County. Data were collected using an online quantitative survey measuring knowledge and attitudes toward HPV vaccination based on the Increasing Vaccination Model, as well as perceived barriers to HPV vaccination and potential solutions to improve vaccination. Participants included persons administering social/health services/part of coalitions in Bexar County from January to March 2025 ( N = 45). Descriptive statistics were estimated. Most participants strongly agreed that HPV vaccination rates could be improved and that it was very important for 9- to 26-year-olds to get vaccinated for HPV. Primary barriers at the organizational level were competing health priorities, lack of provider knowledge/training, language barriers, and patient lack of awareness. Participants were asked to consider what community-level strategies could be deployed to increase HPV vaccination; the highest rated were mobile vaccination, public awareness campaigns, and financing for the vaccine. There is a strong community interest in improving HPV vaccination in Bexar County. Developing a multi-component intervention that addresses direct access issues, coupled with provider recommendations, could surmount the reported barriers to HPV vaccination in this community.
