title: Somatic alterations in TP53, PIK3CA, and CCND1 reveal exposure-driven patterns in oral and oropharyngeal tumors.
abstract: Abstract Tobacco, alcohol, and human papillomavirus (HPV) are major risk factors for oral cavity (OC) and oropharyngeal (OPC) cancers, yet their specific contributions to the tumor molecular landscape remain incompletely understood. We analyzed somatic alterations in 1,086 tumors (606 OC, 480 OPC, including 287 HPV(+)OPC) profiled with a 1,109-gene panel and evaluated their associations with exposures. PIK3CA alterations were widespread but context-specific: HPV(+)OPC featured APOBEC-driven mutations and co-occurrence of FGFR3 mutations in a subset of cases, while HPV(-)OPC and OC were marked by 3q26/28 (PIK3CA/TP63/SOX2) amplifications. TP53 was the most frequently mutated gene in HPV(-) tumors, with strong enrichment among smokers in HPV(-)OPC, whereas TP53 mutation frequencies in OC were consistently high regardless of smoking status. CCND1 amplifications were largely restricted to HPV(-) tumors and were most frequent in individuals reporting combined tobacco/alcohol use. This combined effect was replicated in the TCGA OC-OPC cohort and mirrored at the transcriptomic level, where CCND1 mRNA expression was highest in dual users. Within OC, characterization of one of the largest cohorts of tumors from never smoker-never drinkers to date (N = 100) showed they were more likely to be from female patients and to exhibit enrichment for FAT1 and CASP8 mutations compared to tumors from ever smoker-ever drinkers (N = 353). Together, these findings define distinct, exposure-driven patterns of somatic alterations by subsite and HPV status, and provide a molecular framework that may inform etiologic-based risk stratification in head and neck cancer.
journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute

analysis.research_question_and_background: Oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancers are linked to tobacco, alcohol, and human papillomavirus (HPV), but the specific contributions of these exposures to tumor molecular alterations remain unclear and require molecular characterization to inform risk stratification.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study analyzed somatic alterations in 1,086 oral cavity and oropharyngeal tumors (606 oral cavity, 480 oropharyngeal, including 287 HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancers) using a 1,109-gene panel to evaluate associations with exposures.
analysis.methods: Tumor samples were profiled with a 1,109-gene panel to identify somatic alterations, and associations between molecular alterations and exposures such as tobacco, alcohol, and HPV status were statistically evaluated.
analysis.main_results: PIK3CA alterations were common but context-specific: HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancers showed APOBEC-driven mutations and FGFR3 co-occurrence, while HPV-negative tumors and oral cavity cancers exhibited 3q26/28 amplifications; TP53 was most frequently mutated in HPV-negative tumors with enrichment among smokers in HPV-negative oropharyngeal cancers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study defines distinct, exposure-driven patterns of somatic alterations by tumor subsite and HPV status, providing a molecular framework that may guide etiologic-based risk stratification in head and neck cancer.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform surveillance strategies and risk stratification by linking specific molecular alterations to known exposures such as tobacco, alcohol, and HPV infection in oral and oropharyngeal cancers.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed somatic alterations in 1,086 oral cavity and oropharyngeal tumors, including 287 HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancers, using a 1,109-gene panel to assess associations with exposures such as tobacco, alcohol, and HPV status. title_zh: TP53、PIK3CA 和 CCND1 的体细胞改变揭示了口腔和口咽肿瘤中暴露驱动的模式。
source_body_en: Abstract Tobacco, alcohol, and human papillomavirus (HPV) are major risk factors for oral cavity (OC) and oropharyngeal (OPC) cancers, yet their specific contributions to the tumor molecular landscape remain incompletely understood. We analyzed somatic alterations in 1,086 tumors (606 OC, 480 OPC, including 287 HPV(+)OPC) profiled with a 1,109-gene panel and evaluated their associations with exposures. PIK3CA alterations were widespread but context-specific: HPV(+)OPC featured APOBEC-driven mutations and co-occurrence of FGFR3 mutations in a subset of cases, while HPV(-)OPC and OC were marked by 3q26/28 (PIK3CA/TP63/SOX2) amplifications. TP53 was the most frequently mutated gene in HPV(-) tumors, with strong enrichment among smokers in HPV(-)OPC, whereas TP53 mutation frequencies in OC were consistently high regardless of smoking status. CCND1 amplifications were largely restricted to HPV(-) tumors and were most frequent in individuals reporting combined tobacco/alcohol use. This combined effect was replicated in the TCGA OC-OPC cohort and mirrored at the transcriptomic level, where CCND1 mRNA expression was highest in dual users. Within OC, characterization of one of the largest cohorts of tumors from never smoker-never drinkers to date (N = 100) showed they were more likely to be from female patients and to exhibit enrichment for FAT1 and CASP8 mutations compared to tumors from ever smoker-ever drinkers (N = 353). Together, these findings define distinct, exposure-driven patterns of somatic alterations by subsite and HPV status, and provide a molecular framework that may inform etiologic-based risk stratification in head and neck cancer.
abstract_zh: 摘要:烟草、酒精和人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是口腔癌(OC)和口咽癌(OPC)的主要危险因素,但它们对肿瘤分子景观的具体贡献尚未完全明确。我们分析了1,086例肿瘤(606例OC、480例OPC,其中包括287例HPV阳性OPC)的体细胞突变,这些肿瘤采用包含1,109个基因的检测面板进行分析,并评估了这些突变与暴露因素的关联。PIK3CA突变广泛存在,但具有情境特异性:HPV阳性OPC以APOBEC驱动的突变和FGFR3突变的共发为特征,而HPV阴性OPC和OC则以3q26/28(PIK3CA/TP63/SOX2)扩增为标志。TP53是HPV阴性肿瘤中突变频率最高的基因,在HPV阴性OPC中,吸烟者的TP53突变频率显著升高,而在OC中,无论吸烟状态如何,TP53突变频率均保持高位。CCND1扩增主要局限于HPV阴性肿瘤,且在报告同时使用烟草和酒精的个体中最为常见。这种联合效应在TCGA口腔癌-口咽癌数据集中得到复现,并在转录组水平上得到反映,即CCND1 mRNA表达在双重使用者中最高。在OC中,对至今最大的来自从未吸烟-从未饮酒患者的肿瘤队列(N=100)进行特征分析,发现这些患者更可能来自女性,且与既往吸烟-饮酒患者(N=353)相比,FAT1和CASP8突变更为富集。综上所述,这些发现界定了按亚部位和HPV状态划分的暴露驱动型体细胞突变模式,并为基于病因学的头颈部癌症风险分层提供了分子框架。

title: Integrating HPV self-sampling into antenatal care: prevalence, genotype distribution, clinical outcomes, and preventive implications among pregnant women in Thailand
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Cervical cancer remains a major global health burden, particularly in low- and middle-income countries with limited screening coverage. Pregnancy offers an opportunity to integrate preventive interventions into antenatal care (ANC). Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling may improve participation by reducing barriers to conventional screening. OBJECTIVE This study evaluated HPV prevalence, genotype distribution, clinical outcomes, and the feasibility of HPV self-sampling in ANC among pregnant women in Thailand. STUDY DESIGN: This prospective observational study enrolled pregnant women aged ≥ 18 years with a gestational age ≥ 12 weeks attending ANC at Siriraj Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. Data were collected from July 21, 2025, to January 10, 2026. After standardized instruction, participants performed vaginal HPV self-sampling. HPV was detected and genotyped using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction. Outcomes included HPV prevalence, genotype distribution, acceptance, and follow-up among HPV-positive participants. RESULTS Of 644 pregnant women, HPV infection was detected in 147 (overall prevalence, 22.8%). Among HPV-positive participants, HPV16/18 infection was identified in 37 cases (25.2%) and non-16/18 infection in 110 cases (74.8%). HPV52 was the most frequently detected genotype, followed by HPV16, HPV66, HPV51, and HPV68. Younger maternal age, lower income, divorced/separated/widowed status, and smoking-related exposure were independently associated with HPV infection. Notably, 62.4% of participants had never undergone cervical cancer screening. Self-sampling was highly acceptable, mainly for its convenience and ease of use. CONCLUSION HPV self-sampling integrated into ANC was feasible and acceptable among pregnant women. ANC may extend cervical cancer screening to previously underscreened women and support prevention strategies.

title: Acceptability of At-Home hrHPV Cervical Cancer Screening For Transmasculine Individuals: A Qualitative Descriptive Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transmasculine individuals are less likely to complete cervical cancer screening than cisgender individuals, thus increasing their risk for cervical cancer. Multidimensional socioecological determinants may contribute to cervical cancer disparities for transgender people. OBJECTIVE: This study explored cervical cancer screening barriers and facilitators, acceptability of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) at-home self-sampling cervical cancer screening, and cervical cancer health promotion methods among transmasculine individuals. METHODS: This qualitative description examined socioecological factors affecting cervical cancer screening in transmasculine individuals in 2022 to 2023. Through purposive sampling, 9 participants were interviewed in-depth using semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. RESULTS: Cervical cancer screening decisions were shaped by socioecological barriers and facilitators, including dysphoria, negative healthcare experiences, and exclusionary clinical spaces, alongside healthcare provider support and social network encouragement. At-home hrHPV self-sampling was conditionally acceptable and valued for autonomy and privacy. Affirming communication and culturally competent healthcare providers were central to effective cervical cancer screening promotion. CONCLUSION: Addressing these findings requires an approach that integrates healthcare provider and staff LGBTQ+-specific training, cultural humility, patient-centered care, affirming healthcare provider communication, targeted LGBTQ+-specific education, hrHPV self-sampling options, inclusive clinical environments, cervical cancer screening cost and coverage solutions, and healthcare systems that identify cervical cancer screening eligibility by anatomy. By addressing multilevel socioecological barriers while amplifying patient-identified facilitators such as autonomy, privacy, trusted provider recommendations, and social support; healthcare providers and systems can improve equitable access to cervical cancer screening and reduce preventable cervical cancer disparities among transmasculine and other underscreened populations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 跨男性个体的 宫颈癌 筛查完成率低于顺性别个体,导致 宫颈癌 风险升高。该研究旨在确定筛查的障碍和促进因素,评估家庭高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 自我采样的可接受性,并探索该人群中有效的 宫颈癌 健康促进方法。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项定性描述性研究采用有目的抽样招募 9 名跨男性参与者,进行 2022 年至 2023 年间进行的深入半结构化访谈。采用主题分析来探索影响 宫颈癌 筛查行为的社会生态因素。
elements_zh.methods: 通过半结构化访谈收集数据,并使用主题分析进行分析,以确定筛查行为的社会生态决定因素的模式。该研究侧重于定性探索,没有实验干预或定量比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 社会生态障碍包括性别不安、负面的医疗体验和排他性的临床环境,而促进因素包括提供者的支持和社交网络的鼓励。由于自主性和隐私优势,在家进行 hrHPV 自我采样有条件地可以接受。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,具有文化能力、肯定的医疗环境和提供者沟通对于提高跨男性个体的筛查率至关重要。新颖之处在于以跨男性观点为中心,以确定 hrHPV 自我采样可接受性特有的多层次促进因素和障碍。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,整合针对 LGBTQ+ 的提供者培训、以患者为中心的护理和包容性临床政策可以减少筛查不足的跨男性人群中的 宫颈癌 差异。该研究强调需要进行系统级变革,以改善筛查资格识别和成本覆盖。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 9 名参与者的小样本限制了普遍性,定性设计排除了因果推断。由于依赖自我报告的经验而没有验证或纵向随访,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 背景:与顺性别个体相比,跨男性个体完成 宫颈癌 筛查的可能性较小,因此增加了他们患 宫颈癌 的风险。多维社会生态决定因素可能会导致跨性别者的 宫颈癌 差异。目的:本研究探讨了 宫颈癌 筛查的障碍和促进因素、高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) 在家自我采样 宫颈癌 筛查的可接受性,以及跨男性个体中的 宫颈癌 健康促进方法。方法:本定性描述研究了 2022 年至 2023 年影响跨男性个体 宫颈癌 筛查的社会生态因素。通过有目的抽样,使用半结构化访谈对 9 名参与者进行了深入访谈。使用主题分析对数据进行分析。结果:宫颈癌 筛查决策是由社会生态障碍和促进因素决定的,包括烦躁不安、负面医疗体验和排斥性临床空间,以及医疗保健提供者的支持和社交网络鼓励。家庭 hrHPV 自我采样是有条件接受的,并且重视自主性和隐私性。肯定沟通和具有文化能力的医疗保健提供者是有效 宫颈癌 筛查推广的核心。结论:解决这些发现需要一种方法,将医疗保健提供者和员工 LGBTQ+ 特定培训、文化谦逊、以患者为中心的护理、确认医疗保健提供者沟通、有针对性的 LGBTQ+ 特定教育、hrHPV 自我采样选项、包容性临床环境、宫颈癌 筛查成本和覆盖解决方案以及通过解剖学识别 宫颈癌 筛查资格的医疗保健系统相结合。通过解决多层次的社会生态障碍,同时扩大患者识别的促进因素,例如自主性、隐私、值得信赖的提供者建议和社会支持;医疗保健提供者和系统可以改善 宫颈癌 筛查的公平性,并减少跨男性和其他筛查不足人群之间可预防的 宫颈癌 差异。

title: Liquid Biopsy for Minimal Residual Disease Assessment in Endometrial and Cervical Cancers: Molecular Rationale, Clinical Evidence, and Translational Barriers
abstract: Endometrial and cervical cancers can recur from subclinical disease not evident on routine surveillance. This narrative review critically evaluates liquid biopsy for minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment and recurrence monitoring. Post-treatment human papillomavirus (HPV) circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in cervical cancer has the strongest disease-specific prospective evidence of clinical validity; persistent detection is strongly associated with recurrence, but moderate sensitivity and false-negative results do not support treatment de-escalation on negativity alone. With regard to endometrial cancer, perioperative ctDNA has prognostic support from an 11-study, 1298-patient meta-analysis and additional cohorts, although assay heterogeneity and limited independent replication constrain clinical readiness. Postoperative positivity generally shows stronger associations than preoperative detection. Cervicovaginal and urine DNA-methylation studies provide preliminary evidence for detecting established recurrence, especially local recurrence, but not prospective molecular lead time or clinical utility. Digital PCR, disease-specific fixed panels, tumor-informed assays, and error-corrected sequencing serve distinct settings; broad pan-cancer plasma profiling remains mainly an advanced-disease tool. Circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, microRNAs, tumor-educated platelets, and fragmentomics remain exploratory. Liquid biopsy should remain an investigational adjunct until prospective trials show that acting on molecular findings improves outcomes.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically high-risk types (e.g., HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV33, HPV45, HPV52, HPV58) and their associated diseases (e.g., cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, HPV-associated cervical cancer, genital warts) in the context of liquid biopsy for minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment and recurrence monitoring. The central question focuses on the clinical validity and utility of HPV-specific ctDNA and other liquid biopsy biomarkers in post-treatment surveillance and prognosis.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review that evaluates liquid biopsy methods for MRD assessment in HPV-associated cancers. It synthesizes evidence on ctDNA, circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, microRNAs, tumor-educated platelets, and fragmentomics, highlighting their roles in cervical and endometrial cancers. The review does not report systematic search dates, databases, or eligibility criteria explicitly.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Post-treatment HPV circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in cervical cancer shows the strongest disease-specific prospective evidence of clinical validity; persistent detection is strongly associated with recurrence. However, moderate sensitivity and false-negative results preclude treatment de-escalation based solely on negativity. In endometrial cancer, perioperative ctDNA has prognostic support from an 11-study, 1298-patient meta-analysis and additional cohorts, though assay heterogeneity and limited independent replication constrain clinical readiness. Postoperative ctDNA positivity generally demonstrates stronger associations with outcomes than preoperative detection.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Assay heterogeneity and limited independent replication for ctDNA in endometrial cancer constrain clinical readiness. For cervical cancer, moderate sensitivity and false-negative results in ctDNA detection limit its utility for treatment de-escalation. Cervicovaginal and urine DNA-methylation studies provide preliminary evidence for detecting recurrence but lack prospective molecular lead time or clinical utility. Circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, microRNAs, tumor-educated platelets, and fragmentomics remain exploratory with no established clinical validity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Liquid biopsy should remain an investigational adjunct until prospective trials demonstrate that acting on molecular findings improves patient outcomes. Future research should prioritize standardized, disease-specific assays with validated thresholds for clinical decision-making, particularly for HPV-associated cervical and endometrial cancers. Prospective studies are needed to establish the clinical utility of ctDNA and other biomarkers in guiding treatment adjustments and surveillance strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review evaluates liquid biopsy biomarkers, particularly HPV-specific circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), for minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment and recurrence monitoring in HPV-associated cancers, including cervical and endometrial cancers. The strongest evidence supports the clinical validity of post-treatment HPV ctDNA in cervical cancer, where persistent detection correlates with recurrence, though moderate sensitivity and false negatives limit its use for treatment de-escalation. In endometrial cancer, perioperative ctDNA shows prognostic value, supported by a meta-analysis of 1,298 patients, but assay heterogeneity and limited replication hinder clinical adoption. Postoperative ctDNA positivity is more strongly associated with outcomes than preoperative detection. Preliminary evidence exists for cervicovaginal and urine DNA-methylation assays in detecting recurrence, but prospective utility remains unproven. Circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, microRNAs, tumor-educated platelets, and fragmentomics are exploratory. The review concludes that liquid biopsy should remain investigational until prospective trials demonstrate improved outcomes from acting on molecular findings.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述在液体活检的背景下检查了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV),特别是高危类型(例如 HPV16、HPV18、HPV31、HPV33、HPV45、HPV52、HPV58)及其相关疾病(例如宫颈上皮内瘤变、HPV 相关 宫颈癌、尖锐湿疣),以进行微小残留病 (MRD) 评估和复发监控。核心问题集中在 HPV 特异性 ctDNA 和其他液体活检生物标志物在 治疗 监测 后和预后中的临床有效性和实用性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇叙述性综述,评估用于 HPV 相关癌症 MRD 评估的液体活检方法。它综合了 ctDNA、循环肿瘤细胞、细胞外囊泡、microRNA、肿瘤教育血小板和片段组学的证据,强调了它们在宫颈癌和子宫内膜癌中的作用。该综述没有明确报告系统检索日期、数据库或资格标准。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 治疗 后的 宫颈癌 中的 HPV 循环肿瘤 DNA (ctDNA) 显示出最强的疾病特异性临床有效性前瞻性证据;持续检测与复发密切相关。然而,中等敏感性和假阴性结果排除了仅基于阴性结果的 治疗 降级。在子宫内膜癌中,围手术期 ctDNA 得到了 11 项研究、1298 名患者的荟萃分析和额外的 队列研究 的预后支持,尽管检测异质性和有限的独立复制限制了临床准备。术后 ctDNA 阳性通常表现出比术前检测更强的与结果的关联。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 子宫内膜癌中 ctDNA 的检测异质性和有限的独立复制限制了临床准备。对于 宫颈癌,ctDNA 检测的中等灵敏度和假阴性结果限制了其在 治疗 降级中的效用。宫颈阴道和尿液 DNA 甲基化研究为检测复发提供了初步证据,但缺乏前瞻性的分子前置时间或临床实用性。循环肿瘤细胞、细胞外囊泡、microRNA、肿瘤培养血小板和片段组学仍处于探索阶段,尚未确定临床有效性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 液体活检应继续作为研究的辅助手段,直到前瞻性试验证明根据分子发现采取行动可以改善患者的预后。未来的研究应优先考虑标准化、疾病特异性检测,并具有经过验证的临床决策阈值,特别是针对 HPV 相关的宫颈癌和子宫内膜癌。需要进行前瞻性研究来确定 ctDNA 和其他生物标志物在指导 治疗 调整和 监测 策略方面的临床效用。

abstract_zh: 子宫内膜和 宫颈癌 可能会因常规 监测 上不明显的亚临床疾病而复发。这篇叙述性综述批判性地评价了液体活检用于微小残留病(MRD)评估和复发监测的作用。治疗 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)后的宫颈癌中的循环肿瘤DNA(ctDNA)具有最强的疾病特异性临床有效性前瞻性证据;持续检测与复发密切相关,但中等敏感性和假阴性结果并不支持 治疗 仅根据阴性情况进行降级。对于子宫内膜癌,围手术期 ctDNA 得到了 11 项研究、1298 名患者的荟萃分析和额外的 队列研究 的预后支持,尽管检测异质性和有限的独立复制限制了临床准备。术后阳性通常表现出比术前检测更强的关联性。宫颈阴道和尿液 DNA 甲基化研究为检测已确定的复发(尤其是局部复发)提供了初步证据,但没有提供预期的分子前置时间或临床效用。数字 PCR、疾病特异性固定试剂盒、肿瘤信息检测和纠错测序服务于不同的环境;广泛的全癌血浆分析仍然主要是一种晚期疾病工具。循环肿瘤细胞、细胞外囊泡、microRNA、肿瘤培养的血小板和片段组学仍处于探索阶段。液体活检应继续作为研究的辅助手段,直到前瞻性试验表明根据分子发现采取行动可以改善结果。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 子宫内膜癌中 ctDNA 的检测异质性和有限的独立复制限制了临床准备。对于 宫颈癌,ctDNA 检测的中等灵敏度和假阴性结果限制了其在 治疗 降级中的效用。宫颈阴道和尿液 DNA 甲基化研究为检测复发提供了初步证据,但缺乏前瞻性的分子前置时间或临床实用性。循环肿瘤细胞、细胞外囊泡、microRNA、肿瘤培养血小板和片段组学仍处于探索阶段,尚未确定临床有效性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 液体活检应继续作为研究的辅助手段,直到前瞻性试验证明根据分子发现采取行动可以改善患者的预后。未来的研究应优先考虑标准化、疾病特异性检测,并具有经过验证的临床决策阈值,特别是针对 HPV 相关的宫颈癌和子宫内膜癌。需要进行前瞻性研究来确定 ctDNA 和其他生物标志物在指导 治疗 调整和 监测 策略方面的临床效用。

title: Cell-resolved virus-host programs across cancers associated with five human oncoviruses: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Single-cell RNA sequencing can separate transcriptional changes within a cell type from shifts in tumor composition, yet findings from virus-associated cancers remain scattered across diseases and study designs. Human single-cell RNA-sequencing studies were reviewed, including cancers associated with human papillomavirus (HPV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), or Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV). PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for reports published from 2020 to 2 August 2026, with complementary coverage checks in Scopus and Web of Science. Seventy-five reports met the eligibility criteria (HPV, 34; EBV, 14; HBV, 18; HTLV-1, 5; MCPyV, 4). Findings did not converge on a single host-gene signature. Instead, several functions recurred in different cellular compartments: interferon responses, antigen presentation, clonal lymphocyte expansion, and B-cell or tertiary-lymphoid organization were accompanied by checkpoints, T-cell exhaustion, regulatory T cells, suppressive myeloid and stromal states, and loss of antigen presentation. Within malignant cells, viral transcript abundance was associated with differentiation, integration, proliferation, invasion, or treatment response, although these relationships varied by virus, lineage, tissue, disease stage, and therapy. More informative studies combined cell-level viral-read assignment with patient-level analysis, etiologically matched controls, spatial or longitudinal sampling, and orthogonal validation. These design features will be necessary if cell-resolved virus-host programs are to yield reproducible biomarkers.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cancers using single-cell RNA sequencing to resolve virus-host transcriptional programs, focusing on HPV types (e.g., HPV16, HPV18) and HPV-associated diseases such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers. The central question addresses how cell-resolved transcriptional changes in HPV-positive tumors differ from shifts in tumor composition and what recurrent host-gene functions emerge across these cancers.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic synthesis of human single-cell RNA-sequencing studies published from 2020 to 2 August 2026, identified via PubMed/MEDLINE with complementary checks in Scopus and Web of Science. Eligibility criteria included studies on HPV, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), or Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV), with 75 reports meeting inclusion criteria (HPV: 34 reports).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across HPV-associated cancers, recurrent host-gene functions include interferon responses, antigen presentation, clonal lymphocyte expansion, and B-cell or tertiary-lymphoid organization, alongside checkpoints, T-cell exhaustion, regulatory T cells, suppressive myeloid and stromal states, and loss of antigen presentation. Within malignant HPV-positive cells, viral transcript abundance correlates variably with differentiation, integration, proliferation, invasion, or treatment response depending on virus type, lineage, tissue, disease stage, and therapy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Findings did not converge on a single host-gene signature across HPV-associated cancers, indicating heterogeneity in transcriptional programs. The review highlights that studies lacking cell-level viral-read assignment, patient-level analysis with etiologically matched controls, spatial or longitudinal sampling, and orthogonal validation are less informative and may contribute to inconsistent conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: To yield reproducible biomarkers from cell-resolved virus-host programs in HPV-associated cancers, future studies should integrate cell-level viral-read assignment with patient-level analysis, include etiologically matched controls, employ spatial or longitudinal sampling, and incorporate orthogonal validation. Design features such as these are necessary to overcome current heterogeneity and improve biomarker reliability.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesizes single-cell RNA-sequencing studies of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cancers published from 2020 to 2026, focusing on HPV types (e.g., HPV16, HPV18) and diseases including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers. Across 34 HPV-focused studies, recurrent host-gene functions included interferon responses, antigen presentation, clonal lymphocyte expansion, and tertiary-lymphoid organization, alongside immune checkpoints, T-cell exhaustion, and suppressive myeloid states. Within malignant HPV-positive cells, viral transcript abundance correlated variably with differentiation, integration, proliferation, invasion, or treatment response depending on virus type, lineage, tissue, disease stage, and therapy. The review emphasizes that findings did not converge on a single host-gene signature, reflecting heterogeneity in transcriptional programs. It concludes that reproducible biomarkers will require studies combining cell-level viral-read assignment with patient-level analysis, matched controls, spatial or longitudinal sampling, and orthogonal validation.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述使用单细胞 RNA 测序来解析病毒 宿主 转录程序,检查 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关癌症,重点关注 HPV 类型(例如 HPV16、HPV18)和 HPV 相关疾病,如宫颈上皮内瘤变和 HPV 相关宫颈癌、肛门癌和口咽癌。核心问题涉及 HPV 阳性肿瘤中细胞解析的转录变化与肿瘤组成的变化有何不同,以及这些癌症中出现的复发性 宿主 基因功能。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 2020 年至 2026 年 8 月 2 日发表的人类单细胞 RNA 测序研究的系统综合,通过 PubMed/MEDLINE 进行鉴定,并在 Scopus 和 Web of Science 中进行补充检查。资格标准包括针对 HPV、EB 病毒 (EBV)、乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV)、人类 T 细胞白血病病毒 1 型 (HTLV-1) 或默克尔细胞多瘤病毒 (MCPyV) 的研究,其中 75 份报告符合纳入标准(HPV:34 份报告)。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在 HPV 相关癌症中,复发性 宿主 基因功能包括干扰素反应、抗原呈递、克隆淋巴细胞扩增和 B 细胞或三级淋巴组织,以及检查点、T 细胞耗竭、调节性 T 细胞、抑制性骨髓和基质状态以及抗原呈递丧失。在恶性 HPV 阳性细胞内,病毒转录本丰度与分化、整合、增殖、侵袭或 治疗 反应存在不同的相关性,具体取决于病毒类型、谱系、组织、疾病阶段和治疗。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究结果并未集中在 HPV 相关癌症的单一 宿主 基因特征上,这表明转录程序存在异质性。该综述强调,缺乏细胞水平病毒读取分配、病原学匹配对照的患者水平分析、空间或纵向采样以及正交验证的研究信息量较少,并且可能导致不一致的结论。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 为了从 HPV 相关癌症的细胞分辨病毒 宿主 程序中产生可重复的生物标志物,未来的研究应将细胞水平病毒读取分配与患者水平分析相结合,包括病原学匹配的对照,采用空间或纵向采样,并纳入正交验证。诸如此类的设计特征对于克服当前的异质性和提高生物标志物的可靠性是必要的。

title: FOCUS: A Dual-Mismatch crRNA Strategy Unlocks High-Fidelity One-Step SNV Detection with Cas12a.
abstract: CRISPR/Cas12a has emerged as a powerful tool for nucleic acid detection; however, its clinical utility is severely hampered by intrinsic limitations in single-nucleotide variant (SNV) discrimination, reliance on pre-processed single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) templates, and cumbersome multi-step workflows. Here, we report a novel molecular design principle by engineering crRNAs with site-specific dual mismatches (positions 12 and 14 relative to the PAM), which we systematically demonstrate to drastically enhance the SNV discrimination capability of Cas12a. Leveraging this breakthrough, we developed FOCUS (Fast One-step CRISPR-based Universalizable SNV detection system), an all-in-one CRISPR sensing platform that enables isothermal detection of SNVs from double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) by integrating amplification and detection in a single reaction system. FOCUS achieved attomolar-level sensitivity (13.15 aM) and ultrafast readout (< 20 min) for distinguishing the highly homologous survival motor neuron 1 (SMN1) and SMN2 genes-the gold standard challenge for SNV genotyping in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) diagnostics. To validate its clinical translatability, FOCUS was successfully adapted to a low-cost, equipment-free assay using lateral flow strips and UV visualization, facilitating point-of-care testing (POCT). In a comprehensive validation across 175 clinical samples, FOCUS exhibited 100% diagnostic concordance with gold-standard methods for SMA (21 samples), high-risk HPV 16/18 (27 samples), Staphylococcus aureus (20 samples), and SARS-CoV-2 (107 samples). Collectively, our study establishes a generalizable engineering strategy for Cas12a crRNAs and presents FOCUS as a robust, versatile, and field-deployable solution for precision SNV genotyping, underscoring the translational medicine value of FOCUS in molecular diagnostics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of CRISPR/Cas12a in detecting single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with high fidelity, particularly in clinical settings where accurate SNV discrimination is critical for diagnosing diseases like high-risk HPV infections. The background highlights that CRISPR/Cas12a's clinical utility is hampered by its inability to distinguish SNVs effectively.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a comprehensive validation across 175 clinical samples, including those from high-risk HPV 16/18, to assess the performance of the FOCUS platform. The samples were collected from various sources and tested for their ability to detect SNVs associated with these HPV types.
analysis.methods: The methods included the development of FOCUS, a CRISPR-based platform that integrates amplification and detection in a single reaction system. The platform was validated using a low-cost, equipment-free assay with lateral flow strips and UV visualization, which is suitable for point-of-care testing (POCT).
analysis.main_results: FOCUS demonstrated 100% diagnostic concordance with gold-standard methods for high-risk HPV 16/18, indicating its effectiveness in accurately detecting SNVs in these contexts.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as a demonstration of a novel molecular design principle that enhances the SNV discrimination capability of Cas12a through site-specific dual mismatches in crRNAs. This approach is presented as a significant advancement in the field of molecular diagnostics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have important implications for improving the accuracy and efficiency of SNV detection in HPV-related diagnostics, which can aid in early detection and management of high-risk HPV infections and associated diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on a comprehensive validation across 175 clinical samples, which provides moderate confidence in the performance of FOCUS for high-risk HPV detection. However, the study does not report on potential limitations such as bias or generalisability beyond the tested samples.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces FOCUS, a CRISPR-based platform designed to enhance the detection of single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) in high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infections. The research addresses the limitations of CRISPR/Cas12a in clinical settings, particularly its poor SNV discrimination and reliance on pre-processed DNA templates. The study demonstrates that FOCUS achieves high diagnostic accuracy for HPV 16/18, with 100% concordance with gold-standard methods. The platform integrates amplification and detection in a single reaction system, enabling point-of-care testing (POCT) without the need for specialized equipment. The findings suggest that FOCUS could improve the precision and efficiency of HPV-related diagnostics, offering a versatile solution for SNV genotyping. However, the study's evidence is based on a limited set of clinical samples, which may affect the generalisability of the results. The authors present their work as a novel engineering strategy for Cas12a crRNAs, highlighting its potential for translational medicine applications.

title: Cervical mixed small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and adenocarcinoma with genital tract dissemination: a case report and literature review
abstract: Background Primary mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) of the cervix are exceedingly rare. This report describes a case of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical MiNEN composed of adenocarcinoma and small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (SCNEC) of cervix. Clinical and pathological findings suggest that the adenocarcinoma component extended to the endometrium, bilateral fallopian tubes, and ovaries via genital tract dissemination. Case presentation A 48-year-old female presented with abnormal vaginal discharge for more than eight months and HPV genotyping test was positive for type 18. Pelvic MRI revealed cervical space-occupying lesions and cystic changes in the adnexal region. Gross examination revealed an ulcerative cervical mass, thickened and dilated fallopian tubes, and polycystic ovaries. The tumor was solid, and the cut surface was grayish white with mucus. Histologically, the cervical tumor comprised 65% SCNEC and 35% HPV-associated adenocarcinoma, both of which diffusely expressed p16. Adenocarcinoma was identified in the endometrium and bilateral fallopian tubes and ovaries, and its morphology, immunophenotype, and HPV infection status were consistent with those of cervical adenocarcinoma, suggesting that the cervical adenocarcinoma disseminated along the reproductive tract. Despite receiving systemic chemotherapy and local radiotherapy following surgery, the patient unfortunately passed away due to the progression of the disease in November 2022. Conclusions Cervical MiNENs are highly aggressive malignancies associated with poor prognoses. HPV-associated tumors may spread contiguously through the reproductive tract, mimicking primary tumors of the endometrium, fallopian tubes, or ovaries. Accurate diagnosis and effective management of patients rely on meticulous postoperative histopathological evaluation.

title: Gynecologic complications of disease-modifying therapy in women with multiple sclerosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The long-term implications of multiple sclerosis (MS) disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) on gynecologic health remain understudied. We leverage a multicenter database to evaluate whether DMTs are associated with such complications. METHODS: We propensity-score 1:1 matched women with MS on (1) any versus no or (2) moderate- to high- (vs low-) immunosuppressive DMT by age, marital status, race, ethnicity, tobacco use, body mass index, human papilloma virus (HPV) vaccination, and gynecologic examinations/screenings. We then compared matched cohorts with risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: After matching, we analyzed 115,522 women with MS. The DMT (vs no DMT) group had increased risks of HPV positivity (RR: 1.52, 95% CI: 1.35-172), cervical dysplasia (RR: 1.40, 95% CI: 1.31-1.49), cervical cancer (RR: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.03-1.46), cervicitis (RR: 1.25, 95% CI: 1.10-1.41), herpes simplex virus positivity (RR: 1.29, 95% CI: 1.14-1.45), vulvovaginitis (RR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.23-1.37), and Bartholin cysts/abscesses (RR: 1.37, 95% CI: 1.07-1.76). Moderate- to high- (vs low-) immunosuppressive. DISCUSSION: MS DMTs, especially more immunosuppressive ones, are associated with increased risks of several gynecologic complications. Clinicians should recognize these potential sequelae of DMTs and integrate gynecological counseling/screening into MS care.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The long-term implications of multiple sclerosis (MS) disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) on gynecologic health remain understudied, particularly regarding their association with human papillomavirus (HPV)-related complications.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicenter database was used to evaluate whether DMTs are associated with gynecologic complications in women with MS, with 115,522 women analyzed after propensity-score matching.
analysis.methods: The study used propensity-score 1:1 matching to compare women with MS on DMTs (any versus no) and immunosuppressive levels (moderate- to high- vs low-), adjusting for age, marital status, race, ethnicity, tobacco use, body mass index, HPV vaccination, and gynecologic examinations/screenings. Risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for comparisons.
analysis.main_results: The DMT (vs no DMT) group had increased risks of HPV positivity (RR: 1.52, 95% CI: 1.35-1.72), cervical dysplasia (RR: 1.40, 95% CI: 1.31-1.49), cervical cancer (RR: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.03-1.46), cervicitis (RR: 1.25, 95% CI: 1.10-1.41), herpes simplex virus positivity (RR: 1.29, 95% CI: 1.14-1.45), vulvovaginitis (RR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.23-1.37), and Bartholin cysts/abscesses (RR: 1.37, 95% CI: 1.07-1.76).

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between multiple sclerosis (MS) disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) and gynecologic complications in women, with a focus on human papillomavirus (HPV)-related conditions. The findings suggest that clinicians should consider incorporating gynecological counseling and screening into MS care. However, the study's reliance on observational data and potential unmeasured confounders limits the strength of the evidence, which is assessed as moderate.

abstract: В обзоре представлен анализ современных данных о взаимосвязи состава вагинального микробиома с течением папилломавирусной инфекции у женщин в Республике Беларусь. Приведены данные о молекулярно-эпидемиологических особенностях циркуляции вируса папилломы человека в белорусской популяции и перспективах использования пробиотических штаммов (Lactobacillus crispatus) в национальных клинических протоколах. The review presents an analysis of current data on the relationship between the composition of the vaginal microbiome and the course of human papillomavirus infection in women in the Republic of Belarus. Special attention is paid to the species diversity of lactobacilli and their role in the clearance or persistence of high-risk human papillomavirus. The mechanisms of progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia to cervical cancer against the background of dysbiotic disorders are considered. Data on the molecular and epidemiological features of human papillomavirus circulation in the Belarusian population and the prospects for using probiotic strains (Lactobacillus crispatus) in national clinical protocols are presented.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the relationship between the composition of the vaginal microbiome and the course of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in women, focusing on HPV-associated cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and progression to cervical cancer in the Republic of Belarus. The central question addresses how vaginal microbiota, particularly Lactobacillus species, influence HPV persistence, clearance, and disease progression.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes current data on HPV molecular-epidemiological features in the Belarusian population and evaluates the role of probiotic strains, specifically Lactobacillus crispatus, in national clinical protocols. It integrates species diversity of lactobacilli and their association with high-risk HPV clearance or persistence, as well as mechanisms underlying cervical intraepithelial neoplasia progression to cancer in the context of dysbiosis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that Lactobacillus species diversity, particularly Lactobacillus crispatus, is associated with the clearance or persistence of high-risk HPV. It highlights the progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia to cervical cancer as linked to dysbiotic vaginal microbiome states, emphasizing the potential role of probiotic interventions in national clinical protocols.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report specific quantitative data on the effectiveness of probiotic strains in HPV clearance or the mechanisms by which dysbiosis contributes to cervical cancer progression. Additionally, it lacks detailed methodological descriptions of included studies or pooled estimates to substantiate these associations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests prioritizing research on the integration of probiotic strains, such as Lactobacillus crispatus, into national clinical protocols for HPV management. It also implies the need for further investigation into the molecular mechanisms linking vaginal dysbiosis to HPV persistence and cervical cancer progression, particularly in the Belarusian population.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the interplay between the vaginal microbiome and human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in women, focusing on HPV-associated cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and progression to cervical cancer in Belarus. It highlights the role of Lactobacillus species, particularly Lactobacillus crispatus, in HPV clearance or persistence and suggests potential benefits of probiotic interventions in national clinical protocols. The review also discusses the mechanisms by which dysbiotic vaginal microbiota may contribute to the progression of cervical lesions to cancer. However, it lacks quantitative data and detailed methodological descriptions, indicating gaps in evidence that warrant further research.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述探讨了女性阴道微生物组的组成与 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染病程之间的关系,重点关注白俄罗斯共和国 HPV 相关的宫颈上皮内瘤变和 宫颈癌 的进展。核心问题是阴道微生物群,特别是乳酸菌,如何影响 HPV 的持续存在、清除和疾病进展。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了白俄罗斯人群中 HPV 分子流行病学特征的最新数据,并评估了益生菌菌株(特别是卷曲乳杆菌)在国家临床方案中的作用。它整合了乳酸杆菌的物种多样性及其与 高危型HPV 清除或持久性的关联,以及生态失调背景下宫颈上皮内瘤变进展为癌症的机制。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,乳杆菌物种多样性,特别是卷曲乳杆菌,与 高危型HPV 的清除或持久性相关。它强调了宫颈上皮内瘤变进展为 宫颈癌 与阴道菌群失调状态有关,强调了益生菌干预在国家临床方案中的潜在作用。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告益生菌菌株在 HPV 清除中的有效性或生态失调导致 宫颈癌 进展的机制的具体定量数据。此外,它缺乏对纳入研究或汇总估计的详细方法描述来证实这些关联。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查建议优先研究将卷曲乳杆菌等益生菌菌株纳入国家 HPV 管理临床方案。它还意味着需要进一步研究将阴道生态失调与 HPV 持续性和 宫颈癌 进展联系起来的分子机制,特别是在白俄罗斯人群中。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述探讨了女性阴道微生物组的组成与 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染病程之间的关系,重点关注白俄罗斯共和国 HPV 相关的宫颈上皮内瘤变和 宫颈癌 的进展。核心问题是阴道微生物群,特别是乳酸菌,如何影响 HPV 的持续存在、清除和疾病进展。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了白俄罗斯人群中 HPV 分子流行病学特征的最新数据,并评估了益生菌菌株(特别是卷曲乳杆菌)在国家临床方案中的作用。它整合了乳酸杆菌的物种多样性及其与 高危型HPV 清除或持久性的关联,以及生态失调背景下宫颈上皮内瘤变进展为癌症的机制。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,乳杆菌物种多样性,特别是卷曲乳杆菌,与 高危型HPV 的清除或持久性相关。它强调了宫颈上皮内瘤变进展为 宫颈癌 与阴道菌群失调状态有关,强调了益生菌干预在国家临床方案中的潜在作用。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告益生菌菌株在 HPV 清除中的有效性或生态失调导致 宫颈癌 进展的机制的具体定量数据。此外,它缺乏对纳入研究或汇总估计的详细方法描述来证实这些关联。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查建议优先研究将卷曲乳杆菌等益生菌菌株纳入国家 HPV 管理临床方案。它还意味着需要进一步研究将阴道生态失调与 HPV 持续性和 宫颈癌 进展联系起来的分子机制,特别是在白俄罗斯人群中。

title: Trends in vaccination in pharmacy and medical settings among Medicaid recipients in the United States, 2018-2023: a claims analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Medicaid beneficiaries typically have low vaccination rates, in part due to limited access. Pharmacies provide easy-to-access locations for vaccination. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of trends in pharmacy-based vaccination by age and race or ethnicity among Medicaid recipients aged ≥9 from 1 January 2018 (before the COVID-19 pandemic) to 31 December 2023. The percentage of all vaccinations administered at pharmacies and the overall percentage change in vaccination rates were determined. RESULTS: With some exceptions, overall routine and seasonal vaccination rates remained lower in 2023 than in 2018-2019. This was observed for human papillomavirus (HPV), influenza, and tetanus-containing (Tdap/Td) vaccines in adolescents and for hepatitis A, influenza, meningococcal, pneumococcal, and Tdap/Td vaccines in various adult age groups. The percentage of routine and seasonal vaccinations administered at pharmacies increased over the study period among adults, with increases of 5.2-17.5 percentage points for hepatitis A, hepatitis B, HPV, meningococcal, pneumococcal, and tetanus-containing vaccines among those aged 19-49. Across age groups, pharmacy-based vaccination was most frequent in White enrollees, followed by Black and then Hispanic enrollees, with smaller differentials in adults aged ≥65. CONCLUSIONS: Generally overall vaccine administration rates declined in Medicaid beneficiaries; however, the proportion administered at pharmacies increased.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Medicaid beneficiaries often face barriers to vaccination, including limited access, which contributes to low vaccination rates. The study aimed to assess whether pharmacy-based vaccination settings could mitigate these barriers and improve vaccination trends among this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a retrospective analysis of trends in pharmacy-based vaccination among Medicaid recipients aged 9 years or older from 1 January 2018 to 31 December 2023. The study evaluated the percentage of vaccinations administered at pharmacies and overall vaccination rates over time.
analysis.methods: The study determined the percentage of all vaccinations administered at pharmacies and calculated the overall percentage change in vaccination rates. It analyzed trends by age and race or ethnicity, focusing on routine and seasonal vaccines.
analysis.main_results: Overall routine and seasonal vaccination rates remained lower in 2023 than in 2018-2019 for most vaccines, including HPV, influenza, and Tdap/Td in adolescents, and hepatitis A, influenza, meningococcal, pneumococcal, and Tdap/Td in adults. The percentage of vaccinations administered at pharmacies increased among adults, with gains of 5.2-17.5 percentage points for hepatitis A, hepatitis B, HPV, meningococcal, pneumococcal, and tetanus-containing vaccines in those aged 19-49.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that while overall vaccination rates declined among Medicaid beneficiaries, the proportion of vaccinations administered at pharmacies increased, suggesting improved access through pharmacy settings. This trend was most pronounced in White enrollees, with smaller differentials in adults aged 65 and older.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that expanding pharmacy-based vaccination services may help address access barriers and improve vaccination coverage among Medicaid recipients, particularly for HPV and other routine vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on claims data, which may not capture all vaccinations or account for potential confounding factors. The evidence is moderate, as it provides trend data but does not establish causality or address all barriers to vaccination.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective claims analysis examined trends in pharmacy-based vaccination among Medicaid recipients aged 9 years or older in the United States from 2018 to 2023. The study found that overall vaccination rates for HPV, influenza, and other routine vaccines declined during this period, though the proportion of vaccinations administered at pharmacies increased, particularly among adults aged 19-49. Pharmacy-based vaccination rose by 5.2-17.5 percentage points for several vaccines, including HPV. The authors suggest that pharmacies may help mitigate access barriers, though disparities persisted across racial and ethnic groups. The evidence is moderate due to the retrospective design and reliance on claims data, limiting causal inference.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 医疗补助受益人经常面临 疫苗接种 的障碍,包括访问受限,这导致 疫苗接种 比率较低。该研究旨在评估基于药房的 疫苗接种 设置是否可以减轻这些障碍并改善该人群中的 疫苗接种 趋势。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是对 2018 年 1 月 1 日至 2023 年 12 月 31 日期间 9 岁或以上医疗补助接受者中基于药房的 疫苗接种 趋势的回顾性分析。该研究评估了药房服用 疫苗接种 的百分比以及随时间推移的总体 疫苗接种 比率。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,虽然医疗补助受益人的 疫苗接种 总体比率下降,但在药房服用 疫苗接种 的比例有所增加,这表明通过药房设置的获取情况有所改善。这一趋势在白人参与者中最为明显,在 65 岁及以上的成年人中差异较小。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,扩大基于药房的 疫苗接种 服务可能有助于解决获取障碍并提高医疗补助接受者的 疫苗接种 覆盖率,特别是针对 HPV 和其他常规 疫苗。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对索赔数据的依赖而受到限制,这些数据可能无法捕获所有 疫苗接种 或解释潜在的混杂因素。证据是中等的,因为它提供了趋势数据,但没有建立因果关系或解决 疫苗接种 的所有障碍。

title: Anal HPV in Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Closer Look at Pathogenesis and Clinical Management
abstract: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) face a significantly elevated risk of persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection and subsequent anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) due to chronic immunosuppressive therapy impairing immunosurveillance. Despite the markedly increased risk of ASCC in this vulnerable cohort, standardized screening protocols and optimal clinical management guidelines are not exhaustive. Chronically compromised immunosurveillance permits prolonged HR-HPV carriage and viral genome integration, driving oncogenesis via the E6 and E7 oncoproteins. While calcineurin inhibitors exert pro-oncogenic effects, transitioning to mTOR inhibitors offers distinct antiproliferative and antiviral advantages. Early detection relies on risk-stratified screening utilizing digital anorectal examination, anal cytology, and high-resolution anoscopy. For managing anal intraepithelial neoplasia, traditional topical agents and minimally invasive ablative procedures are widely used, although high recurrence rates present a major clinical challenge. This review analyzes HPV pathogenesis and clinical management in KTRs, evaluating the impact of immunosuppressive regimens and exploring innovative diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. To address viral persistence without compromising the allograft, integrating novel non-invasive, target-specific nutraceuticals may represent an interesting complementary approach. Ultimately, mitigating post-transplant ASCC requires a multidisciplinary strategy that couples early localized screening with tailored systemic immunosuppression.

title: Estimated HPV-Attributable Inpatient Pharmaceutical Reimbursement in Bulgaria, 2021–2025: A National Payer-Perspective Expenditure Analysis
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-attributable cancers remain largely preventable but continue to generate increasing treatment costs where vaccination and screening coverage are limited. We estimated direct inpatient pharmaceutical reimbursement attributable to HPV-related cancers in Bulgaria and examined the drivers of expenditure growth. Methods: National Health Insurance Fund reimbursement data (2021–2025) were analysed for antineoplastic medicines used to treat eight HPV-associated cancer sites. Site-specific population-attributable fractions (PAFs) were applied to estimate HPV-attributable expenditure. Uncertainty in PAFs was quantified using 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations and discrete attribution scenarios. Expenditure growth was decomposed into price, volume, and net product-entry/exit effects using Fisher indices. Expenditure was additionally expressed in constant 2021 euros using the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices. Results: Estimated HPV-attributable inpatient pharmaceutical reimbursement totalled EUR 54.2 million (probabilistic median; 95% uncertainty interval: EUR 53.3–55.0 million). Cervical cancer accounted for 81.8% of the total. Results varied by less than ±6% across attribution scenarios and remained EUR 44.6 million when head-and-neck cancers were excluded. Annual expenditure increased from EUR 3.67 million in 2021 to EUR 19.89 million in 2025, representing a 5.4-fold nominal and 4.2-fold inflation-adjusted increase. Growth was concentrated in cervical cancer and was driven primarily by the introduction of new therapies rather than higher prices or greater use of existing medicines. Net product entry explained 88.8% of total log growth, while reimbursement prices for continuing products declined by approximately 31%. Pembrolizumab, first reimbursed for cervical cancer in 2023, accounted for EUR 16.03 million of cervical cancer expenditure in 2025. Conclusions: These ecological estimates indicate a rapid increase in HPV-attributable inpatient pharmaceutical reimbursement in Bulgaria, largely driven by cervical cancer and the introduction of immunotherapy. The findings have implications for budget forecasting, procurement planning, and economic evaluation of HPV prevention strategies.

title: Infectious Diseases Caused by Bacteria and Viruses and the Challenge of Antibiotic Resistance
abstract: The types of infectious diseases and the number of patients have increased significantly, posing a serious threat to global medical health. In particular, the rise in antibiotic resistance is making bacterial infections more difficult to treat. It is preci sely because of the abuse of antibiotics that bacteria have rapidly developed drug resistance, especially in the case of multidrug -resistant strains, that traditional antibiotic therapy is gradually becoming ineffective. In addition, the rapid mutation of the virus also brings challenges to vaccine development. Taking SARS-CoV-2 as an example, its mutation reduces the effectiveness of the vaccine and increases the complexity of prevention and control. Bacteria and viruses have significant differences in structure and metabolism, which determine their respective treatment methods. Bacteria can be treated with antibiotics, while viruses must rely on vaccines and antiviral drugs to control them. Therefore, scientists are trying to address these challenges by studying bacterial resistance mechanisms, optimizing the composition of HPV vaccines, analyzing the impact of SARS -CoV-2 mutations, and exploring alternative treatments to antibiotics.

Bacteria can be treated with antibiotics, while viruses must rely on vaccines and antiviral drugs to control them. title: Neovaginal Cytologic and Molecular Screening Findings for HPV and Sexually Transmitted Infections Among Transgender Women
abstract: Abstract Background Evidence regarding optimal screening strategies for neovaginal health in transgender women remains limited. Data describing cytologic and molecular detection of human papillomavirus (HPV) and sexually transmitted infections (STI) in neovaginal tissue are scarce, particularly in populations with high burden of HIV and STI. Methods We conducted a descriptive observational study of transgender women with neovagina receiving care at a specialized sexual health clinic in Mexico City. Neovaginal samples were collected for cytologic evaluation and PCR-based molecular testing for HPV and sexually transmitted pathogens. Results Sixteen transgender women were included (median age 44.5 years; range 31–52 years). Cytology samples were obtained in 13 participants and were negative in all cases. Despite universally negative cytology, PCR-based molecular testing identified high-risk HPV in 38.5% of tested participants and detected other sexually transmitted pathogens (Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma hominis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Ureaplasma urealyticum). Conclusions Molecular screening identified HPV infection and other sexually transmitted pathogens in neovaginal samples despite negative cytology. These findings highlight potential limitations of cytology-based screening and support the integration of molecular diagnostics as part of comprehensive sexual health care for transgender women.

title: Cervical screening under wartime: resilience and quality of laboratory services in Ukraine during the Russian invasion
abstract: Introduction Since February 2022, Ukraine has been facing the challenges of active armed conflict, undermining its healthcare system. Despite the ongoing war, the national cervical cancer screening program was launched in 2025. However, little is known about whether laboratory diagnostic quality can be maintained under these conditions. This study aimed to assess the resilience of cervical cancer screening services in Ukraine during wartime by evaluating the temporal dynamics of PAP smears, HPV testing, and their quality indicators. Materials and methods This single-center, repeated cross-sectional study included laboratory data collected on PAP smears from 946,451 cases and 114,974 HPV tests retrieved from the database of the Medical Laboratory CSD in 2021–2025. The Annual Bethesda System 2014 (BS 2014) category proportions and quality metrics (including the ASC/SIL ratio and non-diagnostic rate) were assessed and compared with the benchmarks from BS 2014 and the College of American Pathologists (CAP). HPV testing data included overall positivity rates and HPV 16/18 genotype distribution. Results The volume of PAP tests decreased by 21.5% in 2022; however, there was a significant recovery in 2023, with an increase of 85.3% in 2025 compared to the pre-war baseline (2021). Each Bethesda category proportion for every year aligned within international benchmark ranges. The five-year CSD medians were as follows: NILM—91.27% (89.24–91.61%); ASC-US—4.45% (3.94–5.38%); LSIL—2.83% (2.49–3.57%); HSIL—0.38% (0.31–0.62%), non-diagnostic—0.80% (0.54–1.03%); SCC—0.024% (0.016–0.051%); and AGC—0.25% (0.22–0.26%). Quality metrics were consistent with global reference values, with a total abnormal sample rate of 7.81% (7.7–9.67%), ASC/SIL ratio of 1.36 (1.18–1.66), and ASC-US/LSIL ratio of 1.47 (1.28–1.79). HPV testing expanded at a disproportionately higher rate than Pap test utilization, surging 27.8-fold over the wartime period. HPV positivity declined significantly from 21.07% in 2021 to 17.16% in 2025 ( p = 0.011). While HPV16 prevalence remained relatively stable, the relative contribution of HPV18 nearly doubled, rising from 5.6 to 10.4% among HPV-positive individuals ( p = 0.008). Conclusion Cytopathological reporting patterns remained within benchmark ranges under 4 years of armed conflict in Ukraine, with diagnostic performance of CSD LAB corresponding to international benchmarks. The rapid HPV testing expansion associated with an increased rate of testing among younger women, a decline in HPV positivity among the 30–65 cohort, and a rise in the HPV 18 proportional rate have direct implications for national vaccination and screening policies.

title: Relative HPV Viral Load Measured by ΔCt for Risk Stratification in Cervical Cancer Screening
abstract: Background/Objectives: Human papillomavirus (HPV) testing is widely used in cervical cancer screening because of its high sensitivity, although its limited specificity requires effective triage strategies. This study aimed to evaluate the association between relative viral load (RVL) and cervical lesion severity, focusing on HPV-positive women with non-high-grade cytology. Methods: The study included 997 women with histological outcomes from a cohort of 2765 HPV-positive individuals identified among 37,030 women screened in the Bari metropolitan area (Italy) using a real-time HPV-DNA test. Associations between RVL, estimated using the ΔCt method, and lesion severity were assessed using histological and cytological classifications. Logistic regression models evaluated the independent effect of RVL, adjusting for age and HPV detection channel. Results: Lower ΔCt values (indicating higher RVL) were significantly associated with high-grade lesions (CIN2+) (OR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.89–0.94, p < 0.001). The association was observed for HPV16 and the pooled 12-high-risk HPV detection channel, while no significant association was observed for HPV18. A similar association was observed when cytological classification was used as the outcome. Age showed a modest effect, with reduced odds of high-grade lesions observed in women aged ≥50 years. Among women with non-high-grade cytology who subsequently underwent histological assessment, 17.6% had underlying CIN2+, and RVL remained significantly associated with lesion severity in this subgroup. However, ΔCt showed only modest discrimination for high-grade lesions [AUC = 0.643 (95% CI: 0.605–0.681)]. Conclusions: Higher HPV RVL is associated with increased lesion severity, particularly for HPV16 and the pooled 12-high-risk detection channel, but not for HPV18. Given its modest standalone discriminatory performance and the selected nature of the histologically verified cohort, ΔCt should be considered an exploratory marker rather than a validated triage tool. Prospective validation is required to determine whether it provides incremental clinical value.

Logistic regression models evaluated the independent effect of RVL, adjusting for age and HPV detection channel. Results: Lower ΔCt values (indicating higher RVL) were significantly associated with high-grade lesions (CIN2+) (OR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.89–0.94, p < 0.001). The association was observed for HPV16 and the pooled 12-high-risk HPV detection channel, while no significant association was observed for HPV18. A similar association was observed when cytological classification was used as the outcome. Age showed a modest effect, with reduced odds of high-grade lesions observed in women aged ≥50 years. Among women with non-high-grade cytology who subsequently underwent histological assessment, 17.6% had underlying CIN2+, and RVL remained significantly associated with lesion severity in this subgroup. However, ΔCt showed only modest discrimination for high-grade lesions [AUC = 0.643 (95% CI: 0.605–0.681)]. Conclusions: Higher HPV RVL is associated with increased lesion severity, particularly for HPV16 and the pooled 12-high-risk detection channel, but not for HPV18. Given its modest standalone discriminatory performance and the selected nature of the histologically verified cohort, ΔCt should be considered an exploratory marker rather than a validated triage tool. Prospective validation is required to determine whether it provides incremental clinical value.

title: Colorimetric PCR Based on Pyrophosphate Displacement.
abstract: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) is the gold standard for molecular diagnostics. Colorimetric readout can greatly simplify PCR-based diagnostics and make them appealing for decentralized testing. Current colorimetric PCR schemes mostly target the dsDNA amplicons. It is expected that pyrophosphate (Py), the inherent product of PCR (in fact, all nucleic acid amplification schemes), stands as a simpler colorimetric target, due to its versatile complexing with various metal ions/indicators. However, Py-based colorimetric PCR has not been reported yet, partially because it will receive serious competitive complexation from Mg2+ in PCR. Herein, we introduced the Sc3+-hydroxynaphthol blue (Sc-HNB) complex to facilitate Py-based colorimetric PCRs. Because of the higher stability of Sc-HNB over Mg-HNB and Sc-Py over Mg-Py, Py generated during PCR cycles can directly displace HNB from the Sc-HNB complex in a Mg2+-independent manner, yielding a distinct color change. The proposed strategy features simplicity and low cost and can be coupled with PCR in both real-time and end-point manner, with sensitivity for target gene detection comparable to conventional qPCR. Because of the robustness of the Py-displacement reactions, the proposed colorimetric PCR could work with even water bath heating and was compatible with the existing PCR kits. To further validate its feasibility and accuracy, human papillomavirus (HPV) detection in vaginal swab samples was carried out, with results fully consistent with those obtained by qPCR. All of these results indicate that the Py-displacement-based colorimetric PCR can be a promising tool for decentralized nucleic acid testing.

title: Oncogenic Viruses and Human Cancer: Molecular Mechanisms, Diagnostics, Vaccines and Therapeutic Advances
abstract: Oncogenic viruses are preventable or therapeutically tractable causes of a substantial and geographically unequal fraction of human cancer.Their biological diversity, from small DNA viruses to retroviruses and non-integrating RNA viruses, has produced distinct tumour phenotypes but also revealed recurrent principles of carcinogenesis.This critical narrative review integrates evidence on high-risk human papillomaviruses, hepatitis B, C, and D viruses, Epstein-Barr virus, Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus, human T-cell leukaemia virus type 1, and Merkel cell polyomavirus.Human immunodeficiency virus is considered as an indirect carcinogenic cofactor through immune dysregulation, whereas human cytomegalovirus is treated as an unresolved candidate rather than an established tumour virus.Literature indexed through 2 June 2026 was selected from biomedical and scholarly databases, authoritative institutional sources, citation tracing, and DOI registries, with emphasis on causal evidence, mechanistic coherence, clinical validity, and translational relevance.The strongest shared mechanisms are persistent infection, dysregulated viral gene expression, interference with tumour suppressor and cell-cycle control, genomic or epigenomic instability, chronic inflammation, and immune escape.Yet the relative contribution of these processes differs markedly by virus, Review Articletissue, host immunity, and co-exposure.Diagnostics are most mature where viral biomarkers define tumour aetiology or enable screening, notably high-risk human papillomavirus testing, Epstein-Barr virus DNA in endemic nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and viral oncoprotein antibodies in selected Merkel cell carcinoma settings.Prophylactic vaccination has generated the clearest cancer-prevention evidence for human papillomavirus and hepatitis B virus, while elimination barriers, incomplete coverage, persistent post-cure risk, and the absence of licensed vaccines for several tumour viruses limit population impact.Immune checkpoint blockade and virus-specific cellular therapies demonstrate that viral antigens can be clinically actionable, but response heterogeneity and implementation complexity remain substantial.Progress now depends on harmonised viral attribution, prospective biomarker validation, prevention programmes designed for equity, and trials that integrate viral biology with tumour genomics and host immunity.

title: Development of an intervention for middle adolescents (15–17 years old) using the Behaviour Change Wheel (BCW) to empower adolescent decision-making regarding HPV vaccination uptake
abstract: Introduction In the United Kingdom, where a school-based human papillomavirus vaccination programme vaccinates 12–13 year old students, parents/guardians have been the primary decision-makers regarding receipt of the vaccination. As the average age of first sexual intercourse is 15–17 years old, education at this time could provide an opportunity for unvaccinated students to self-consent to vaccination. The aim of this study was to develop a HPV intervention, aimed at middle adolescents (15–17 years old), using the 3 stages of the Behaviour Change Wheel. Methods A systematic review informed target behaviours and populations. Focus groups and interviews were conducted throughout Northern Ireland with immunisation nurses (n = 26), middle adolescents (n = 34), and post-primary school teachers (n = 12) and nurses (n = 6). Data analysis was guided by the COM-B model to inform a Behavioural Diagnosis. Subsequently, appropriate intervention functions, policy categories and Behaviour Change Techniques were selected with consideration of APEASE criteria. Results The systematic review highlighted the lack of interventions designed for middle adolescents; existing interventions were sparse, commonly not based on behavioural theory and focused on female cancers. The study identified twelve barriers to three target behaviours which included: empowering students to make decisions about HPV; empowering professionals’ to design and deliver the intervention; and increasing positive public attitudes regarding HPV vaccination. A behaviour change HPV intervention was developed which included school-based HPV education aligned with mandated curriculum changes, alongside vaccination opportunity. The study identified content, mode of delivery and desirable qualities/characteristics of a professional who could design/deliver the HPV education. A public media campaign was deemed important in supporting this central education. Discussion and conclusion This study highlights political, social and cultural barriers to HPV intervention success and the need for Public Health Authority and Education Authority support. A feasibility pilot study should be undertaken to assess the real-world practicality of this HPV intervention.

title: Development of a cell-penetrating peptide for intracellular delivery of a biologically active HPV E6 inhibitor in cervical cancer cells
abstract: Abstract Background The E6 oncoprotein of high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPVs) promotes cervical carcinogenesis by forming a complex with the ubiquitin ligase E6AP to mediate p53 proteasomal degradation. A 15-amino-acid peptide (pep11) was shown to disrupt the HPV16 E6/E6AP complex, to restore p53 stability and to induce apoptosis in HPV16-positive cancer cells. In this study, a short cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) was conjugated to the pep11 N-terminus to improve its solubility and intracellular delivery in HPV-positive cancer cells. Methods CPP-pep11 was synthesized using Boc chemistry. The interactions of CPP-pep11 with HPV16 and HPV18 E6 were modelled using AlphaFold2, while peptide structures were characterised by NMR spectroscopy. HPV16-positive SiHa and HPV18-positive C4-I cervical cancer cells were treated with CPP-pep11 (0.5–20 μM) for 24–72 h. Effects on proliferation and clonogenicity were assessed using xCELLigence and colony formation assays. Peptide uptake and localization were analysed by confocal microscopy and differential cell fractionation, while p53 expression and viability were evaluated by Western blotting and cytotoxicity assays. Results AlphaFold2 modelling suggested that CPP-pep11 can interact with both HPV16 E6 and HPV18 E6, with a more stable predicted binding to HPV16 E6. CPP-pep11 was soluble in water at 20 μM and, according to NMR analysis, predominantly adopted a disordered conformation. CPP-pep11 efficiently entered the SiHa and C4-I cell membranes, mainly localised to the cytoplasm at lower concentrations (0.5–5 μM) and to the nucleus at higher concentrations (10–20 μM). CPP-pep11 induced dose- and time-dependent inhibition of proliferation, with a significant reduction in colony formation in both cell lines. Treatment also restored p53 levels at 48 and 72 h, consistent with disruption of E6-mediated degradation. Conclusions In conclusion, CPP-pep11 is a novel peptide-based inhibitor of HPV16 E6 and HPV18 E6 with therapeutic potential in HPV-associated malignancies by restoring p53 levels and inhibiting cancer cell proliferation.

title: Association between vaginal microecological dysfunction and cervical lesion severity in postmenopausal women: a retrospective study
abstract: Objective To investigate the associations between vaginal microecological alterations and varying grades of cervical lesions in postmenopausal women, aiming to provide clinical evidence for the prevention and treatment of cervical lesions in this population. Methods A total of 441 postmenopausal women who attended Qinghai Red Cross Hospital from January 2022 to January 2025 were enrolled. According to cervical histopathology, subjects were divided into a control group ( n = 147, without cervical lesions) and a study group ( n = 294). The study group was further categorized into low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL, n = 187), high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL, n = 72), and cervical cancer (CC, n = 35) subgroups. General demographic data were collected and analyzed. All participants underwent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing, vaginal microecological functional assays—including pH, cleanliness, hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), leukocyte esterase (LE), sialidase (SNA), prolyl aminopeptidase (PIP), coagulase (GADP), β-glucuronidase (GUS), and N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminidase (NAG)—and screening for common pathogens such as bacterial vaginosis (BV), vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC), and Trichomonas vaginalis (TV). Intergroup differences were analyzed, and multivariate logistic regression was employed to identify independent independently associated with cervical lesions in postmenopausal women. Results Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups ( P > 0.05). The HR-HPV positive rate in the study group was significantly higher than in controls, increasing with lesion severity ( P 4.5), decreased cleanliness (grades III–IV), and positivity for LE, GUS, and NAG compared to HR-HPV negative individuals ( P < 0.001). Within the study groups, abnormal pH, decreased cleanliness, H 2 O 2 positivity, LE, SNA, PIP, and BV detection rates were significantly elevated relative to controls, correlating positively with lesion severity ( P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified HR-HPV infection (OR = 8.58), H 2 O 2 positive (OR = 12.40), SNA (OR = 5.06), PIP (OR = 3.07), and BV infection (OR = 10.80) as independent independently associated with cervical lesions ( P < 0.05). Conclusion Cervical lesion development and progression in postmenopausal women are closely associated with persistent HR-HPV infection, vaginal microecological dysbiosis, and BV. H 2 O 2 deficiency, BV infection, and HR-HPV positivity constitute the strongest risk factors. Monitoring and modulation of vaginal microecology may offer novel preventive and therapeutic strategies against cervical disease in this population.

title: Availability of Cancer Screening Across HIV Treatment Sites in the IeDEA Consortium.
abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in people with HIV, and the importance of cancer screening increases as this population ages. In 2017, 2020, and 2023, cross-sectional surveys were conducted at HIV care sites across 5 continents within the International epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS (IeDEA) consortium. We described cancer screening availability in 2023 and over time for cervical and anal cancer screening using generalized estimating equations with a logit link function to account for site clustering, rurality, and country income. Of the 220 sites in the 2023 survey, 61% (134/220) reported cervical cancer screening by cytology or human papillomavirus (HPV) testing on-site, and 88% (194/220) reported cervical cancer screening by any method, including visual inspection. At sites serving predominantly rural populations, 62% (29/47) exclusively performed screening by visual inspection. Overall, 23% (50/220) of sites performed cytology-based anal cancer screening on-site, and 16% (35/220) had availability of high-resolution anoscopy, either on-site or by referral. Screening for cancer of the liver, colon, lung, prostate, or breast (by imaging) were each available at less than 43% of sites. The odds of cervical cancer screening availability increased by 16% annually from 2017 through 2023 (aOR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.07-1.27, p = 0.001), while the relative odds of anal cancer screening availability decreased by 9% annually (aOR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.84-0.99, p = 0.023). Lack of trained staff was the most frequently reported barrier, followed by lack of equipment. Understanding current practices and capacity is essential for the continued integration of cancer prevention in HIV care.

source_records.abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in people with HIV, and the importance of cancer screening increases as this population ages. In 2017, 2020, and 2023, cross-sectional surveys were conducted at HIV care sites across 5 continents within the International epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS (IeDEA) consortium. We described cancer screening availability in 2023 and over time for cervical and anal cancer screening using generalized estimating equations with a logit link function to account for site clustering, rurality, and country income. Of the 220 sites in the 2023 survey, 61% (134/220) reported cervical cancer screening by cytology or human papillomavirus (HPV) testing on-site, and 88% (194/220) reported cervical cancer screening by any method, including visual inspection. At sites serving predominantly rural populations, 62% (29/47) exclusively performed screening by visual inspection. Overall, 23% (50/220) of sites performed cytology-based anal cancer screening on-site, and 16% (35/220) had availability of high-resolution anoscopy, either on-site or by referral. Understanding current practices and capacity is essential for the continued integration of cancer prevention in HIV care.

title: Correlation between atypical squamous cells–cannot exclude high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion and cervical lesions: a retrospective analysis of opportunistic and organized cervical screening populations
abstract: Background We compared Liquid-Based Cytologic Test (LCT) results diagnosed as atypical squamous cells–cannot exclude high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (ASC-H) with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection status and histopathological findings across two cervical screening groups. Additionally, we analyzed the clinical correlation of ASC-H with cervical lesions. Methods This retrospective analysis included 171,688 cases. LCT specimens were divided into two groups: 31,100 from patients who underwent organized cervical screening with artificial intelligence(AI)-assisted interpretation; and 140,588 from patients who underwent opportunistic screening interpreted manually. Of the 663 cases diagnosed with ASC-H, 387 underwent both HPV testing and subsequent histopathological examination. HPV detection methods included 23-type HPV genotyping, and the Cobas 4800 assay which identifies HPV16/18 plus 12 other hrHPV subtypes. Results The overall prevalence of ASC-H was 0.39%. Among 387 paired cases of ASC-H, the total HPV infection rate reached 84.00%, with hrHPV accounting for 97.82% of cases. Women aged <50 years exhibited more single HPV genotype infections and a significantly higher positivity rate for hrHPV than those aged ≥50 years ( p <0.05). In 297 ASC-H samples tested by HPV23 genotyping, the most prevalent hrHPV genotypes were HPV16 (28.62%), HPV52 (21.89%), and HPV58 (17.17%). Among 90 ASC-H samples detected with Cobas 4800 (HPV16/18 plus 12 other hrHPV), the infection rates for HPV16, HPV18, and other 12 hrHPV subtypes were 11.11%, 2.22%, and 82.22%, respectively. Histopathological examination confirmed that 137 of the 387 (35.40%) patients with ASC-H had high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or worse (HSIL+), with seven HSIL+ lesions testing negative for HPV. Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) were identified in 119 cases (30.75%), including 15 that were negative for HPV. There was no significant difference in HSIL+ positivity observed between the two screening groups, whereas the opportunistic screening group showed a significantly higher positivity rate for LSIL compared with the organized cervical screening group ( p <0.01). Conclusion ASC-H indicates a significant risk of HSIL+, particularly in younger women, regardless of interpretation (AI-assisted or manual). These patients require timely evaluation and suitable treatment, as well as careful follow-up to minimize the risk of missed diagnoses of precancerous lesions and early cervical cancer.
